21-00-00-800-801Supply Conditioned Air to the AirplanePDF p. 57
2. Supply Conditioned Air to the Airplane
(Figure 201)
A. General
SUBTASK 21-00-00-860-111
(1) It is recommended that the conditioned air to cool the airplane on the ground be supplied from
a ground air source, when practical, as an alternative to operating the cooling packs. To supply
conditioned air, do this task: Supply Conditioned Air with a Ground Air Source,
TASK 21-00-00-800-805.
B. Procedure
SUBTASK 21-00-00-860-001
(1) Do one of these tasks to supply conditioned air to the airplane:
(a) Do this task: Supply Conditioned Air with a Cooling Pack, TASK 21-00-00-800-803.
(b) Do this task: Supply Conditioned Air with a Ground Air Source, TASK 21-00-00-800-805.
21-00-00-800-802Remove Conditioned Air from the AirplanePDF p. 59
3. Remove Conditioned Air from the Airplane
(Figure 201)
A. Procedure
SUBTASK 21-00-00-860-002
(1) Do one of these tasks to remove conditioned air from the airplane:
(a) Do this task: Remove Conditioned Air Supplied by a Cooling Pack,
TASK 21-00-00-800-804.
(b) Do this task: Remove Conditioned Air Supplied by a Ground Air Source,
TASK 21-00-00-800-806.
21-00-00-800-803Supply Conditioned Air with a Cooling PackPDF p. 59
4. Supply Conditioned Air with a Cooling Pack
(Figure 201)
A. General
(1) It is recommended that the conditioned air to cool the airplane on the ground be supplied from
a ground air source, when practical, as an alternative to operating the cooling packs. To supply
conditioned air, do this task: Supply Conditioned Air with a Ground Air Source,
TASK 21-00-00-800-805.
(2) When conditions permit, open the doors for the air conditioning packs when they operate.
B. References
Reference Title
24-22-00-860-811 Supply Electrical Power (P/B 201)
36-00-00-860-801 Supply Pressure to the Pneumatic System (Selection) (P/B 201)
C. Location Zones
Zone Area
211 Flight Compartment - Left
212 Flight Compartment - Right
D. Prepare to Supply Conditioned Air with a Cooling Pack
SUBTASK 21-00-00-860-003
(1) Do this task: Supply Electrical Power, TASK 24-22-00-860-811.
SUBTASK 21-00-00-860-004
(2) Do this task: Supply Pressure to the Pneumatic System (Selection), TASK 36-00-00-860-801.
SUBTASK 21-00-00-860-005
WARNING
MAKE SURE THERE IS AN EXIT IN THE AIRPLANE FUSELAGE FOR THE
CONDITIONED AIR. IF THERE IS NO EXIT FOR THE CONDITIONED AIR,
PRESSURIZATION OF THE CABIN WILL OCCUR WHICH CAN CAUSE
INJURY TO PERSONS.
(3) Do one of these steps to make sure there is an exit for the conditioned air:
(a) Make sure the cabin pressure outflow valve is open.
(b) Make sure at least one passenger entry door is open.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
SUBTASK 21-00-00-860-124
CAUTION
DO NOT OPERATE A COOLING PACK AND A GROUND AIR SOURCE AT THE
SAME TIME. THE COOLING PACK CAN NOT CONTROL THE AIR
TEMPERATURE IF YOU ALSO OPERATE A GROUND AIR SOURCE. IF YOU
OPERATE THEM AT THE SAME TIME, DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT CAN
OCCUR.
(4) Make sure that the ground air source is disconnected.
E. Supply Conditioned Air with a Cooling Pack
SUBTASK 21-00-00-860-104
(1) Turn these selectors on the P5-17 cabin temperature control panel to the AUTO position:
(a) CONT CAB
(b) FWD CAB
(c) AFT CAB
SUBTASK 21-00-00-860-007
(2) Set the applicable L PACK switch or the R PACK switch, on the P5-10 air conditioning panel, to
the AUTO position.

A. General

a ground conditioned air source refer to the 737-NG Maintenance Facility and Equipment
Planning Document, D626A002.
B. Location Zones
Zone Area
100 Lower Half of Fuselage
C. Access Panels
Number Name/Location
191E Access Door - Forward Fairing
D. Supply Conditioned Air with a Ground Air Source
SUBTASK 21-00-00-010-001
(1) To get access to the ground conditioned air connector, do this step:
Open this access panel:
Number Name/Location
191E Access Door - Forward Fairing
SUBTASK 21-00-00-210-001
(2) Make sure that the swing check valve in the ground conditioned air connector can move freely.
SUBTASK 21-00-00-860-011
(3) Do these steps to connect the duct from the ground air source to the ground conditioned air
connector.
(a) Engage the fasteners on the duct with the slots in the ground conditioned air connector.
(b) Turn the duct until it is locked to the ground conditioned air connector.
SUBTASK 21-00-00-860-012
WARNING
MAKE SURE THAT THERE IS AN EXIT IN THE AIRPLANE FUSELAGE FOR
THE CONDITIONED AIR. IF THERE IS NO EXIT FOR THE AIR, THE
PRESSURE IN THE CABIN WILL INCREASE. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO
PERSONNEL.
(4) Do one of these steps to make sure there is an exit for the conditioned air:
(a) Make sure the cabin pressure outflow valve is open.
(b) Make sure at least one passenger entry door is open.
SUBTASK 21-00-00-860-123
CAUTION
DO NOT OPERATE A COOLING PACK AND A GROUND AIR SOURCE AT THE
SAME TIME. THE COOLING PACK CAN NOT CONTROL THE AIR
TEMPERATURE IF YOU ALSO OPERATE A GROUND AIR SOURCE. IF YOU
OPERATE THEM AT THE SAME TIME, DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT CAN
OCCUR.
(5) Make sure that the L PACK and R PACK switches on the P5-10 air conditioning panel are set
to OFF.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
SUBTASK 21-00-00-860-158
(6) Optional: Make sure the L RECIRC FAN and R RECIRC FAN switches are set to OFF.
SUBTASK 21-00-00-860-013
(7) Operate the ground air source to supply conditioned air to the airplane.
(a) Make sure that the conditioned air pressure does not exceed 15 inches of water (.54 psi)
gauge pressure.
(b) Make sure that the conditioned air temperature does not exceed 71 degrees C (160
degrees F).

2. MMEL 21-1 (DDPG) Preparation - Air Conditioning Pack(s) Inoperative
A. General
(1) This task gives the maintenance steps that prepare the airplane for flight with both air
conditioning packs inoperative.
B. Location Zones
Zone Area
118 Electrical and Electronics Compartment - Right
192 Lower Wing-To-Body Fairing - Under Wing Box
212 Flight Compartment - Right
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
C. Both Air Conditioning Packs Inoperative - Deactivation Procedure
SUBTASK 21-00-00-840-001
(1) Do this step to put the recirculation fan in the INOP ON condition:
(a) Open this circuit breaker and install safety lock:
F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-4
Row Col Number Name
D 2 C01445 A/C OVERBOARD EXH VALVE RECONFIG CONT
SUBTASK 21-00-00-710-027
(2) Close the flow control and shutoff valves for the air conditioning packs
(TASK 21-00-00-040-805).
(a) Manually set the outflow valve to the full OPEN position.
(b) Put one of the pack switches in the HIGH position.
(c) Advise dispatch of unpressurized flight.
NOTE: Maximum altitude for flight planning will be affected.

21-00-00-040-806MMEL 21-5 (DDPG) Preparation - Ram Air Modulating System InoperativePDF p. 83
12. MMEL 21-5 (DDPG) Preparation - Ram Air Modulating System Inoperative
(Figure 903)
A. General
(1) This task gives the maintenance steps which prepare the airplane for flight with the ram air
modulation system inoperative.
 349-999
(2) The inlet ram air modulation system consists of a deflector door, two modulation panels and a
smart ram air door actuator (SRADA). The exit ram air modulation system consists of a smart
ram air door actuator (SRADA), three louvers, and a linkage mechanism to move the louvers.
(3) If the ram air inlet panels are put into an inoperative flight open condition, the ram air
modulated exhaust duct louvers must be put into a corresponding open condition also.
Conversely, the ram air inlet panels must be put into an inoperative flight open condition if the
fault condition is with the ram air modulated exhaust system.
 ALL

G. Ram Air Exit Modulating System Reactivation
SUBTASK 21-00-00-440-009
(1) Do one of the steps that follow to reactivate the system:
(a) If secured open by installing the Smart Ram Air Door Actuator (SRADA) stowage link, do
this task to reactivate: Smart Ram Air Door Actuator Stowage Link - Removal,
TASK 21-51-27-000-802.
(b) If secured open by removing the ram air exhaust actuator, do the following to reactivate
(Figure 904):
1) Remove the nut, washers and bolt that are attaching the most forward louver drive
arm to the most forward hole in the link assembly.
2) Move the link assembly until the hole in the most forward louver drive arm aligns
with the second most forward hole in the link assembly.
3) In the same order that they were just removed, install the bolt, washers and nut
through the hole in the most forward louver drive arm and the second most forward
hole in the link assembly.
4) Install the ram air exhaust actuator, do this task: Ram Air Exhaust Actuator -
Installation, TASK 21-51-27-400-801.
SUBTASK 21-00-00-410-021

20. DDG 21-14 Preparation - Cabin Pressure Control System Inoperative
A. General
(1) This task gives the maintenance steps which prepare the airplane for flight with two modes or
one automatic mode of the cabin pressure control system inoperative.
(2) The cabin pressure control system has two automatic modes and one manual mode.
(3) When two of the three modes do not operate, then the airplane must be prepared for
unpressurized flight.
(4) When the manual mode operates and one of the two automatic modes does not operate, then
deactivate the controller that is Inoperative.
B. Location Zones
Zone Area
145 Aft Cargo Compartment Equipment Bay - Left
212 Flight Compartment - Right
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL

22. MMEL 21-15 (DDPG) Preparation - Aft Outflow Valve - Two Actuators Inoperative
A. General
(1) This task gives the maintenance steps that prepare the airplane for flight with two actuators of
the aft outflow valve inoperative.
(2) The aft outflow valve has two automatic mode actuators and one manual mode actuator. When
two of the three actuators do not operate, the airplane must be prepared for unpressurized
flight.

212 Flight Compartment - Right
D. Airplane Preparation for Unpressurized Flight, Manual Mode Operates
SUBTASK 21-00-00-040-003
(1) At the P5-6 Pressurization Control Panel, do these steps to command the outflow valve to the
25% open position in the manual mode:
(a) Put the selector in the MAN position.
(b) Hold the VALVE switch in the OPEN or CLOSE position until the valve position indicator
shows 25% open.
SUBTASK 21-00-00-860-050
(2) Make sure that the outflow valve moved to the 25% open position.
SUBTASK 21-00-00-040-024
(3) Open these circuit breakers and install safety tags:
F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-4
Row Col Number Name
D 2 C01445 A/C OVERBOARD EXH VALVE RECONFIG CONT
F 3 C01270 PRESSURIZATION CONTROL AUTO 1
F 5 C01271 PRESSURIZATION CONTROL AUTO 2
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
E. Airplane Preparation for Unpressurized Flight, Manual Mode Does Not Operate
SUBTASK 21-00-00-040-025
(1) Start both engines, do this task: Start the Engine Procedure (Normal Start),
TASK 71-00-00-800-808-F00.
SUBTASK 21-00-00-040-026
(2) Run the engines for two minutes to allow them to stabilize.
SUBTASK 21-00-00-040-027
(3) Advance the thrust levers as necessary to make sure that N1 is greater than 60% and N2 is
greater than 89%.
SUBTASK 21-00-00-040-028
(4) Look at the outflow valve position indicator as is goes to the closed position.
SUBTASK 21-00-00-040-029
(5) When the outflow valve is in the 25% open position,
Open these circuit breakers and install safety tags:
F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-4

E. Outflow Valve Operational Test - Manual Mode
SUBTASK 21-00-00-710-010
(1) On the P5-6 Pressurization Control Panel, put the mode selector to MAN.
SUBTASK 21-00-00-710-011
(2) Make sure the MANUAL light goes on.
SUBTASK 21-00-00-710-012
(3) Hold the VALVE switch in the OPEN position for 30 seconds.
SUBTASK 21-00-00-710-013
(4) Look at the aft outflow valve to make sure it moved to the fully open position.
SUBTASK 21-00-00-710-014
(5) Hold the VALVE switch in the CLOSE position for 30 seconds.
SUBTASK 21-00-00-710-015
(6) Look at the aft outflow valve to make sure it moved to the fully closed position.
F. Outflow Valve Operational Test - Automatic Modes
SUBTASK 21-00-00-710-016
(1) On the P5-6 Pressurization Control Panel, put the mode selector to AUTO.
SUBTASK 21-00-00-710-017

21-00-05-780-801Airplane Pack Operation - Confidence CheckPDF p. 183
2. Airplane Pack Operation - Confidence Check
(Figure 201, Figure 202, and Figure 203)
A. General
(1) This confidence check consists primarily of these tests:
NOTE: The Phase II Test is applicable to 737-600 and 737-700 models.
(a) Phase I Test - pressurize cabin from 0.0 to 4.0 psid (27.6 kPa) using the Auxiliary Power
Unit (APU), and the packs.
(b) Phase III Test - perform a cabin leak down test from 4.0 psid (27.6 kPa) cabin pressure
and note the cabin differential pressure for 120 seconds at 10 second intervals.
(2) Figure 201 gives a graphical representation of the confidence check tests.
(3) Figure 202 gives a data sheet to record the Phase I, II, III test results.
(4) Figure 203 gives supplemental troubleshooting information.

3. Airplane Pack Operation - Confidence Check, Dispatch with One Pack Inoperative
A. General
(1) This confidence check consists primarily of these tests:
(a) Phase I Test - pressurize cabin from 0.0 to 4.0 psid (27.6 kPa) using one engine and one
pack.
(b) Phase II Test - perform a cabin leak down test from 4.0 psid (27.6 kPa) cabin pressure
and note the cabin differential pressure for 120 seconds at 10 second intervals.
(2) Table 204 and Table 205 gives a data sheet to record the Phase I and II test results.
(3) Table 206 gives supplemental troubleshooting information.
(4) The intent of this confidence check can be satisfied by reviewing Airplane Condition And
Monitoring System (ACMS) or Quick Access Recorder (QAR) data from the most recent flight.
If the following conditions are true, accomplishment of this task is not necessary.
NOTE: Only applicable for aircraft that have programmed their Digital Flight Data Acquisition
Unit (DFDAU) to record pneumatic and cabin pressure control system parameters per
the guidance given in Service Letters 737-SL-21-095 and 737-SL-36-024.
(a) Left and right duct pressure is 32 psig (220.6 kPa) or more during climb and cruise.
(b) Outflow valve position is 15 degrees or more during climb and cruise.

a) Make sure that the duct pressure on the side with the operable pack is at least
35 psig (241.3 kPa).
<1> If duct pressure is less than 35 psig (241.3 kPa), do this task: Bleed Air
Regulator/PRSOV/450° F Thermostat Health Check,
TASK 36-11-00-710-802.
NOTE: Control pressure must be 21 psig (144.8 kPa) - 28 psig
(193.1 kPa).
<2> If no fault is found, do this task: Precooler Control Valve System Health
Check, TASK 36-12-00-700-801.
<3> If no fault is found, there could be a problem with the kiss seal,
obstruction in the precooler fan air flow, 390°F (199°C) sensor, or 450°F
(232°C) thermostat.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
b) Manually operate the outflow valve MANUAL VALVE CLOSE/OPEN switch as
necessary to achieve a steady 4.0 psid (27.6 kPa) cabin pressure on the DIFF
PRESS indicator.
c) If a differential pressure of 4.0 psid (27.6 kPa) cannot be maintained, either a
pack supply or airplane leakage problem exists, do the applicable fault
isolation tasks.
9) Switch the bleed source to the opposite engine.
a) If the left pack is the operable pack, put ISOLATION VALVE to OPEN and 1
BLEED to OFF.
b) If the right pack is the operable pack, put ISOLATION VALVE to OPEN and 2
BLEED to OFF.
10) Make sure that the duct pressure is at least 35 psig (241.3 kPa).
a) If duct pressure is less than 35 psig (241.3 kPa), do this task: Bleed Air
Regulator/PRSOV/450° F Thermostat Health Check, TASK 36-11-00-710-802.
NOTE: Control pressure must be 21 psig (144.8 kPa) - 28 psig (193.1 kPa).
b) If no fault is found, do this task: Precooler Control Valve System Health Check,
TASK 36-12-00-700-801.
c) If no fault is found, there could be a problem with the kiss seal, obstruction in
the precooler fan air flow, 390°F (199°C) sensor, or 450°F (232°C) thermostat.
d) Manually operate the outflow valve MANUAL VALVE CLOSE/OPEN switch as
necessary to achieve a steady 4.0 psid (27.6 kPa) cabin pressure on the DIFF
PRESS indicator.
e) If a differential pressure of 4.0 psid (27.6 kPa) cannot be maintained, either a
pack supply or airplane leakage problem exists, do the applicable fault
isolation tasks.
11) Decrease the engine power to 30% N1 for both engines.
a) Make sure that the duct pressure is at least 32 psig (220.6 kPa).
<1> If duct pressure is less than 32 psig (220.6 kPa), do this task: High
Stage Regulator/High Stage Valve Health Check,
TASK 36-11-00-710-803.
NOTE: Control pressure must be 16 psig (110.3 kPa) - 18 psig
(124.1 kPa).
b) Manually operate the outflow valve MANUAL VALVE CLOSE/OPEN switch as
necessary to achieve a steady 4.2 psid (29.0 kPa) cabin pressure on the DIFF
PRESS indicator.
c) If a differential pressure of 4.2 psid (29.0 kPa) cannot be maintained, either a
pack supply or airplane leakage problem exists, do the applicable fault
isolation tasks.

(Figure 801)
A. General
(1) This procedure is for the repair of a taped joint that connects two sections of Fiberglass or
Kevlar air conditioning ducts.
(2) This procedure may also be used to make a temporary repair to a damaged Fiberglass or
Kevlar air conditioning duct when time is not available to make a permanent repair or if the
materials are not available to make a permanent repair. If a temporary repair is made, make

SUBTASK 21-20-02-840-003
(3) If insulation is installed on the duct joint, then remove the insulation.
SUBTASK 21-20-02-840-004

WARNING
DO NOT GET METHYL ETHYL KETONE (MEK) IN YOUR MOUTH OR
EYES, OR ON YOUR SKIN. DO NOT BREATHE THE FUMES FROM MEK.

SUBTASK 21-20-02-340-001

G50789 to install the insulation.
SUBTASK 21-20-02-840-007
(2) Replace the panels or other airplane structure removed to gain access to the duct joint.

E. Repair the Air Conditioning Duct
SUBTASK 21-20-02-340-006
(1) Apply a thin, smooth layer of the applicable Hetron 92 resin, G02137 or resin, A00040 to the
duct where the Fiberglass fabric will be applied. Make sure the area of the resin is a minimum
of the size and shape of the Fiberglass fabric pieces.
SUBTASK 21-20-02-340-007
(2) Place a piece of the Fiberglass fabric on the resin so that it extends beyond the cut or crack a
minimum of 1/2 inch on all sides.
SUBTASK 21-20-02-340-008
(3) Soak the Fiberglass fabric with the applicable resin.
SUBTASK 21-20-02-340-009
(4) Put a piece of plastic sheet on the Fiberglass fabric and press lightly to remove any bubbles or
any wrinkles and to remove unwanted resin.
SUBTASK 21-20-02-340-010
(5) Remove the plastic sheet from the Fiberglass fabric piece and remove any unwanted resin with
a wiping cloth.
SUBTASK 21-20-02-340-011
(6) Place another piece of the Fiberglass fabric on the first piece, soak it with resin, and smooth it.
Continue using the same procedure until the thickness of the patch equals the thickness of the
duct.
SUBTASK 21-20-02-340-012
(7) Allow the resin to cure for 24 hours at room temperature.

(a) You must install insulation that meets one of these specifications:
1) BMS 8-385 Type 4, foam insulation, G50449
2) BMS 8-385 Type 6, foam insulation, G51169
3) BMS 8-300 Type VIII, foam insulation, G51170I.
(b) Use BMS 5-157 MPVF or BMS 5-157 MPEEK tape to install the insulation.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
SUBTASK 21-20-02-840-015
(2) Replace the panels or other airplane structure removed to gain access to the duct joint.

4. Structural Repair - Fiberglass/Kevlar Duct
(Figure 801)
A. General
(1) This procedure gives instructions for making a structural repair to a Fiberglass or Kevlar air
conditioning duct.
(2) A structural repair is applicable when the damage to the air conditioning duct is a cut or a hole
that is more than 0.25 in. (6.35 mm) wide and more than 3 in. (76.2 mm) long but less than 5
percent of the total surface area of the duct. If the damage is more than 5 percent of the total
surface area of the duct, then replace the duct section.

SUBTASK 21-20-02-840-016
(1) Do this task: Remove Pressure from the Pneumatic System, TASK 36-00-00-860-806.

SUBTASK 21-20-02-840-017

SUBTASK 21-20-02-840-019
(4) Do these steps to prepare the damaged area of the duct.
(a) Cut away the damaged area to make a rounded opening with a smooth shape.
1) Cut the sides of the opening at an angle to make a taper of 0.5 in. (12.7 mm)
between each ply of material.
(b) Sand the edge of the opening to make a smooth surface.
(c) Sand the surface of the duct around the opening a distance of 0.5 in. (12.7 mm) for each
ply in the duct. For example, if there are 6 plies, sand 3 in. (76.2 mm) from the opening
on all sides (1/2 x 6 = 3 inches)(12.7 x 6 = 76.2 millimeters).

 ALL

(a) Make sure that the fabric is on all of the opening.
(b) If necessary, cut the fabric.

1) Make the resin smooth.
(d) Continue with the same procedure with fabric until the beaded end agrees with the duct
end dimensions.
SUBTASK 21-20-02-340-117
(8) Cut the last piece of fabric to the necessary dimensions:
NOTE: The dimensions can include the repaired bead and the internal and external surfaces
of the full diameter of the duct.
(a) Make sure that the external layer of the Outer Mold Line (OML) is on all of the repaired
bead and is around the part end.
(b) Make sure that the external layer extends more than 0.5 in. (12.7 mm) from the repair
layer of the Inner Mold Line (IML).
(c) From the center of the fabric to the edges, remove all bubbles and wrinkles.
SUBTASK 21-20-02-340-118

DO NOT GET METHYL ETHYL KETONE (MEK) IN YOUR MOUTH OR EYES,
OR ON YOUR SKIN. DO NOT BREATHE THE FUMES FROM MEK. PUT ON A

DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT.

unwanted resin.

(10) To cure resin, G50399, or resin, G50400, do these steps (SRM 51-30-10):
(a) Attach a vacuum bag, STD-94, to hold the repair layers and to keep the duct shape.
1) Allow the resin to cure for 24 hours at 75 ±5°F (24 ±3°C).
2) Cure for a minimum of 2 - 2.5 hours under a minimum of 20 in/Hg (68 kPa) at
170 ±10°F (77 ±6°C).
NOTE: Moisture protection is not necessary during 170 ±10°F (77 ±6°C) cure.
SUBTASK 21-20-02-340-120
(11) If necessary, sand the patch on the outer duct surface to get a correct fit.
(a) Keep a wall thickness of 0.045 in. (1.143 mm) - 0.065 in. (1.651 mm) in this area.
NOTE: Wrinkles, creases, and unwanted resin are not permitted in this area. Sand these
items flush where necessary.
SUBTASK 21-20-02-340-121
(12) Use a brush, STD-122, to seal exposed fabric with a layer of resin, G50399, or resin, G50400.

 ALL

(13) Let the resin, G50399, or resin, G50400, cure.

3) BMS 8-300 Type VIII foam insulation, G51170.

(3) Replace the panels or other airplane structure removed to gain access to the duct joint.

WARNING
DO NOT GET METHYL ETHYL KETONE (MEK) IN YOUR MOUTH OR
EYES, OR ON YOUR SKIN. DO NOT BREATHE THE FUMES FROM MEK.

(a) Use the solvent, B00148 and a cotton wiper, G00034 to clean the duct ends.

SUBTASK 21-20-02-840-064
(5) Prepare a piece of the polyurethane foam duct that matches the damaged duct and is the

E. Repair the Taped Joint
SUBTASK 21-20-02-340-063
(1) Apply the applicable resin to the duct ends. Allow the resin to partially dry until it is sticky. Press
the duct ends together by aligning the installation checkmarks.
SUBTASK 21-20-02-340-064
(2) Apply the applicable resin to each joint area a minimum of 2 inches on both sides of the joint.
SUBTASK 21-20-02-340-065
(3) Apply the applicable resin to one side of the two pieces of the Fiberglass fabric.
SUBTASK 21-20-02-340-066
(4) Wrap one piece of the Fiberglass fabric around each duct joint a minimum of four times. Make
sure the resin on the Fiberglass fabric is in contact with the duct.
SUBTASK 21-20-02-340-067
(5) Put a piece of plastic sheet on the joint and press on it to smooth the Fiberglass fabric to
remove any bubbles or any wrinkles.
SUBTASK 21-20-02-340-068
(6) Allow the resin to cure for 24 hours at room temperature.

21-20-02-330-810Tape Replacement - Foam Wrapped Insulated DuctPDF p. 234
11. Tape Replacement - Foam Wrapped Insulated Duct
(Figure 803)
A. General
(1) This procedure has instructions to repair those air conditioning ducts insulated with Melamine
or Polyimide Foam. The Foam Insulation is wrapped around the duct and held in place with an
adhesive tape.
(2) CFR 14 Part 121.312 mandates that insulation material installed in the fuselage as a
replacement after September 2, 2005 must meet the flame propagation requirements of CFR
Part 25.856, effective September 2, 2003.
(a) Existing insulation material can be removed and re-installed if it is not damaged.
Replacement insulation material must meet the flame propagation requirement.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(b) Melamine foam insulation, G50449, BMS8-385, is the preferred foam insulation material
that meets the flame propagation requirement. Melamine BMS8-385 Type 4 is the
preferred foam insulation material that meets the flame propagation requirement.
Melamine BMS 8-385 Type 6 and polyimide BMS 8-300 Type VIII insulation are optional
to BMS8-385 Type 4.
(c) Do not use BMS8-39 polyurethane foam insulation for repairs due to the degradation in
flammability properties over time.
(d) When insulation material is removed and re-installed, any existing tape that does not
meet the flame propagation requirement must be removed or completely covered with
tape that does meet the requirement.
(e) Air conditioning ducts with polyimide foam insulation, G02470 must be wrapped with
tape, G50327, tape, G51202 or tape, G50789 to meet the flammability/flame propagation
requirement. Wrap the tape, G50327, tape, G51202 or tape, G50789 across 100% of the
brown hypalon insulation surface of the polyimide foam insulation, G02470.

E. Replace the Tape
SUBTASK 21-20-02-420-001
(1) Install the tape, G50327, tape, G51202 or tape, G50789 to the repair area (Figure 803).
(a) Make sure the tape, G50327, tape, G51202 or tape, G50789 has an overlap of all the
edges and seams of the insulation by a minimum of 1.00 inch (25.4 mm).
F. Rework Ducts Insulated with Polyimide Foam Insulation
SUBTASK 21-20-02-420-002
(1) Install tape, G50327, tape, G51202 or tape, G50789 to completely cover all exposed surfaces
of foam insulation as shown in (Figure 803).
(a) The tape, G50327, tape, G51202 or tape, G50789 must cover 100% of the brown colored
hypalon insulation surface.
(b) Cut the tape, G50327, tape, G51202 or tape, G50789 as required to fit around air outlets,
branches and insulation vent holes.
(c) The tape, G50327, tape, G51202 or tape, G50789 may be installed spiral wrapped or
lengthwise down the duct depending on installers preference.
(d) The tape, G50327, tape, G51202 or tape, G50789 may be installed in any configuration
as long as 100% complete coverage of the foam insulation, G02470 insulation is
obtained.
(e) Maintain a minimum of 1/8 inch overlap of tape, G50327, tape, G51202 or tape, G50789.
(f) Avoid compression of the foam insulation, G02470 insulation.
(g) Wrinkles in the tape, G50327, tape, G51202 or tape, G50789 are acceptable if pinched
together and contain no voids.
(h) The tape, G50327, tape, G51202 or tape, G50789 may be installed to the foam
insulation, G02470 insulation prior to installation on the duct if desired by the installer.
(i) For foam insulation, G02470 insulation installed on duct joints, tape, G50327, tape,
G51202 or tape, G50789 may be applied to the foam insulation, G02470 insulation
before or after the foam insulation, G02470 insulation is installed over the duct joint.
(j) The tape, G50327, tape, G51202 or tape, G50789 orientation is optional.
SUBTASK 21-20-02-420-008
(2) If necessary, install the air conditioning duct.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL

SUBTASK 21-20-02-840-075
(1) Replace the panels or other airplane structure removed to gain access to the duct.

17. External Patch - Reinforced Thermoplastic Laminate Duct
(Figure 805)
A. General
(1) This procedure gives instructions for the repair of a puncture, crack or cut in a Reinforced
Thermoplastic Laminate air conditioning duct with an external patch.
(2) An external patch is applicable when the cut or the crack is less than 0.25 inches (6.35 mm)
wide and is less than 3.0 inches (76.2 mm) long.
(3) An external patch is applicable when the puncture is less than 0.25 inches (6.35 mm) diameter.
B. References
Reference Title
36-00-00-860-806 Remove Pressure from the Pneumatic System (P/B 201)

(Supersedes O-A-51)

Wiper (Cheesecloth, Gauze)

Grade A or B Form 1

CL A)

Laminating Plastics
BMS9-3
G50400 Resin - Fiberglass Layup, Short Worklife,

BMS8-201 Type IV

Type II)
D. Prepare for the Repair
SUBTASK 21-20-02-860-001
(1) Do this task: Remove Pressure from the Pneumatic System, TASK 36-00-00-860-806.
NOTE: This will make sure that there is no airflow in the ducts when you do the repair.
SUBTASK 21-20-02-010-001
(2) Gain access to the damaged air conditioning duct joint.
SUBTASK 21-20-02-010-002
(3) If insulation is installed on the duct, then remove the insulation.
SUBTASK 21-20-02-120-001
(4) Do these steps to prepare the damaged area of the duct.
(a) Use sandpaper on the damaged area to remove the gloss from the finish of the duct.
(b) Use the solvent, B00062 and a cotton wiper, G00034 to clean the duct joint area.
(c) Make sure fibers from the damaged area of the duct do not extend more than 0.125
inches (3.175 mm) into the inside of the duct.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
SUBTASK 21-20-02-340-069
(5) Do these steps to prepare the materials for the duct repair:
(a) Cut sufficient pieces of the Fiberglass fabric, G00316 to equal the number of plies of the
damaged duct. Cut the Fiberglass fabric, G00316 pieces 0.50 inches (12.7 mm) larger on
all sides than the damage. Round the corners of the pieces of the Fiberglass fabric.
(b) Prepare the Fiberglass duct repair resin, G50400.
E. Repair the Air Conditioning Duct
SUBTASK 21-20-02-340-070
(1) Apply a thin, smooth layer of the resin, G50400 to the duct where the Fiberglass fabric will be
applied. Make sure the area of the resin is a minimum of the size and shape of the Fiberglass
fabric pieces.
SUBTASK 21-20-02-340-071
(2) Place a piece of the Fiberglass fabric on the resin so that it extends beyond the area of
damage a minimum of 1/2 inch on all sides.
SUBTASK 21-20-02-340-072
(3) Soak the Fiberglass fabric with the applicable resin.
SUBTASK 21-20-02-340-073
(4) Put a piece of plastic sheet on the Fiberglass fabric and press lightly to remove any bubbles or
any wrinkles and to remove unwanted resin.
SUBTASK 21-20-02-340-074
(5) Remove the plastic sheet from the Fiberglass fabric piece and remove any unwanted resin with
a wiping cloth.
SUBTASK 21-20-02-340-075
(6) Place another piece of the Fiberglass fabric on the first piece, soak it with resin, and smooth it.
Continue using the same procedure for each new ply of the fabric.
SUBTASK 21-20-02-340-076
(7) Allow the resin to cure for 24 hours at room temperature.
F. Put the Airplane Back to Its Usual Condition
SUBTASK 21-20-02-410-001
(1) If insulation was removed from the duct joint, install new insulation.
SUBTASK 21-20-02-410-002
(2) Replace the panels or other airplane structure removed to gain access to the duct joint.
21-20-02-330-817Structural Repair - Reinforced Thermoplastic Laminate DuctPDF p. 254
18. Structural Repair - Reinforced Thermoplastic Laminate Duct
(Figure 805)
A. General
(1) This procedure gives instructions for making a structural repair to a Reinforced Thermoplastic
Laminate air conditioning duct.
(2) A structural repair is applicable when the damage to the air conditioning duct is a cut or a hole
that is more than 0.25 inches (6.35 mm) wide and more than 3.0 inches (76.2 mm) long but
less than 5 percent of the total surface area of the duct. If the damage is more than 5 percent
of the total surface area of the duct, then replace the duct section.
(3) A structural repair is applicable when the damage to the air conditioning duct is a puncture that
is more than 0.25 inches (6.35 mm) in diameter.
(4) It is not permitted to overlap structural repairs to the air conditioning duct.
B. References

36-00-00-860-806 Remove Pressure from the Pneumatic System (P/B 201)

D. Prepare for the Repair
SUBTASK 21-20-02-010-003
(1) Do this task: Remove Pressure from the Pneumatic System, TASK 36-00-00-860-806.
NOTE: This will make sure that there is no airflow in the ducts when you do the repair.
SUBTASK 21-20-02-010-004
(2) Gain access to the damaged air conditioning duct.
SUBTASK 21-20-02-010-005
(3) If insulation is installed on the duct, then remove the insulation.
SUBTASK 21-20-02-120-002
(4) Do these steps to prepare the damaged area of the duct.
(a) Cut away the damaged area to make a rounded opening with a smooth shape.
(b) Use sandpaper to prepare the surface of the duct around the opening a distance of 0.50
inches (12.7 mm) for each ply in the duct. For example, if there are 6 plies, sand 3 inches
from the opening on all sides (0.50 x 6.0 = 3.0 inches)(12.7 x 152.4 = 76.2 mm).
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(c) Use sandpaper to prepare the surface of the duct an additional 0.50 inches (12.7 mm)
from the repair area.
(d) Make sure fibers from the damaged area of the duct do not extend more than 0.125
inches (3.175 mm) into the inside of the duct.
(e) Use the solvent, B00062 and a cotton wiper, G00034 to clean the duct joint area.
SUBTASK 21-20-02-350-001
(5) Cut a piece of plastic sheet 2.0 to 3.0 inches (50.8 to 76.2 mm) larger on all sides than the
opening. Cut a piece of cardboard or aluminum 2.0 to 3.0 inches (50.8 to 76.2 mm) larger than
the opening on all sides.
SUBTASK 21-20-02-350-002
(6) Attach the plastic sheet to the inside of the opening with adhesive tape so that it covers the
opening. Attach the cardboard or aluminum to the inside of the opening with adhesive tape so
that it covers the opening and provides support for the plastic sheet.
SUBTASK 21-20-02-340-077
(7) Do these steps to prepare the materials for the duct repair:
(a) Cut sufficient pieces of the Fiberglass fabric, G00316 to equal the number of plies of
damaged the duct. Cut an additional piece of fabric, G00316
(b) Cut the first piece of the Fiberglass fabric, G00316 pieces 0.50 inches (12.7 mm) larger
on all sides than the damage. Round the corners of the pieces of the Fiberglass fabric.
(c) Cut each piece of the Fiberglass fabric, G00316 0.50 inches (12.7 mm) larger on all sides
than the piece before.
(d) Prepare the Fiberglass duct repair resin, G50400.
E. Repair the Air Conditioning Duct
SUBTASK 21-20-02-340-078
(1) Apply a thin, smooth layer of resin, G50400 to the plastic sheet in the opening in the duct.
SUBTASK 21-20-02-340-079
(2) Place a piece of the Fiberglass fabric in the opening over the plastic sheet so that it covers the
opening completely.
SUBTASK 21-20-02-340-080
(3) Soak the Fiberglass fabric with the applicable resin.
SUBTASK 21-20-02-340-081
(4) Put a piece of plastic sheet on the Fiberglass fabric and press lightly with a squeegee or with
your hand. Smooth from the center to the edges of the Fiberglass fabric to remove bubbles or
wrinkles and to remove unwanted resin.
SUBTASK 21-20-02-340-082
(5) Remove the plastic sheet from the patch and remove unwanted resin with a cotton wiper,
G00034.
SUBTASK 21-20-02-340-083
(6) Place the next piece of the Fiberglass fabric on the first piece so that it covers the opening.
Trim the Fiberglass fabric if necessary. Soak the Fiberglass fabric with resin and smooth it.
Continue using the same procedure until the thickness of the patch equals the thickness of the
duct.
SUBTASK 21-20-02-340-084
(7) Round the corners of the last piece of the Fiberglass fabric. Smooth the Fiberglass fabric to
remove bubbles or winkles.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
SUBTASK 21-20-02-340-085
(8) Wipe the duct around the patch with a cotton wiper, G00034 and solvent, B00148 to remove
unwanted resin.
SUBTASK 21-20-02-340-086
(9) Allow the resin to cure for 24 hours at room temperature.
F. Put the Airplane Back to Its Usual Condition
SUBTASK 21-20-02-410-003
(1) If insulation was removed from the duct joint, install new insulation.
SUBTASK 21-20-02-410-004
(2) Replace the panels or other airplane structure removed to gain access to the duct joint.

212 Flight Compartment - Right
F. Prepare for the Repair
SUBTASK 21-20-02-840-112
(1) Do this task: Remove Pressure from the Pneumatic System, TASK 36-00-00-860-806.
NOTE: This will make sure that there is no airflow in the ducts when you do the repair.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
SUBTASK 21-20-02-840-113
(2) Gain access to the damaged air conditioning duct (TASK 21-21-01-000-804-002).
SUBTASK 21-20-02-840-114
(3) If insulation is installed on the duct, then remove the insulation.
SUBTASK 21-20-02-840-115
(4) Do these steps to prepare the damaged area of the duct:
(a) Cut away the damaged area to make a rounded opening with a smooth shape.
(b) Cut the sides of the opening at an angle to make a taper of 0.5 in. (12.7 mm) between
each layer of material.
(c) Sand the edge of the opening to make a smooth surface.
(d) Sand the surface of the duct around the opening a distance of 0.5 in. (12.7 mm) for each
layer in the duct.
NOTE: For example, if there are 6 layers, sand 3 in. (76 mm) from the opening on all
sides (1/2 x 6 = 3 inches).
WARNING
DO NOT GET METHYL ETHYL KETONE (MEK) IN YOUR MOUTH OR
EYES, OR ON YOUR SKIN. DO NOT BREATHE THE FUMES FROM MEK.
PUT ON A PROTECTIVE SPLASH GOGGLE AND GLOVES WHEN YOU
USE MEK. KEEP MEK AWAY FROM SPARKS, FLAME AND HEAT. MEK IS
A POISONOUS AND FLAMMABLE SOLVENT WHICH CAN CAUSE
INJURIES TO PERSONS OR DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT.
(e) Clean the edge of the opening and sanded surface of the duct with solvent, B00148, and
a cotton wiper, G00034.
(f) Remove the water and contamination from the structure (SRM 51-70-04).
1) Make sure that bonding surfaces are clean and dry.
SUBTASK 21-20-02-840-116
(5) Cut one piece of the fabric, G50775, or fabric, G50173, to the necessary size.
(a) This must include the repaired bead and the inner surfaces and external surfaces of the
full diameter of the duct.
NOTE: The external layer on the Outer Mold Line (OML) must be on all of the repaired
bead. It must also be put around the part end, and extend more than 0.5 in.
(12.7 mm) from the repair layer of the Inner Mold Line (IML).
SUBTASK 21-20-02-840-122
(6) Cut sufficient pieces of the fabric, G50797, or fabric, G50798, to give the same thickness as
the repaired bead.
SUBTASK 21-20-02-840-117
(7) Cut a piece of plastic sheet 2 in. (51 mm) – 3 in. (76 mm) larger on all sides than the opening.
SUBTASK 21-20-02-840-123
(8) Cut a piece of cardboard or aluminum 2 in. (51 mm) – 3 in. (76 mm) larger than the opening on
all sides.
SUBTASK 21-20-02-840-118
(9) Attach the plastic sheet to the inner surface of the opening with adhesive tape.
(a) Make sure that all of the opening has plastic sheet on it.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
SUBTASK 21-20-02-840-124
(10) Attach the cardboard or aluminum to the inner surface of the opening with adhesive tape.
(a) Make sure that the cardboard or aluminum is on the opening and gives support for the
plastic sheet.
SUBTASK 21-20-02-840-119
(11) Prepare the resin, A00040 or resin, A50145.
G. Repair the Beaded End
SUBTASK 21-20-02-340-099
(1) Apply a thin, smooth layer of resin, A00040, or resin, A50145, to the plastic sheet in the
opening in the duct.
SUBTASK 21-20-02-340-100
(2) Place a piece of the fabric, G50775, or fabric, G50173, in the opening over the plastic sheet.
(a) Make sure that all of the opening has fabric on it.
SUBTASK 21-20-02-340-101
(3) Soak the fabric, G50775, or fabric, G50173, with resin, A00040 or resin, A50145.
SUBTASK 21-20-02-340-102
(4) Put a piece of the plastic sheet on the fabric, G50775, or fabric, G50173.
(a) Apply light pressure to the plastic sheet with a squeegee or with your hand.
(b) From the center of the fabric, G50775, or fabric, G50173, to the edges, remove all
bubbles or wrinkles and unwanted resin.
SUBTASK 21-20-02-340-103
(5) Remove the plastic sheet from the patch and remove unwanted resin with a cotton wiper,
G00034.
SUBTASK 21-20-02-340-104
(6) Put the next piece of the fabric, G50775, or fabric, G50173, on the first piece of fabric.
(a) Make sure that the fabric is on all of the opening.
(b) Cut the fabric, G50775, or fabric, G50173, if necessary.
(c) Soak the fabric, G50775, or fabric, G50173, with resin, A00040 or resin, A50145 and
smooth it.
(d) Use the same procedure until the thickness of the patch agrees with the thickness of the
duct.
(e) Continue the same procedure with fabric, G50797, or fabric, G50798, until the bead
agrees with the necessary dimensions.
SUBTASK 21-20-02-340-105
(7) Cut the last piece of the fabric, G50775, or fabric, G50173, to the necessary dimensions:
(a) The dimensions can include the repaired bead and the internal and external surfaces of
the full diameter of the duct.
NOTE: The external layer on the OML must be on all of the repaired bead. It must also
be put around the part end, and extend more than 0.5 in. (12.7 mm) from the
repair layer of the IML.
(b) From the center of the fabric, G50775, or fabric, G50173, to the edges, remove all
bubbles or wrinkles.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
SUBTASK 21-20-02-340-106
WARNING
DO NOT GET METHYL ETHYL KETONE (MEK) IN YOUR MOUTH OR EYES,
OR ON YOUR SKIN. DO NOT BREATHE THE FUMES FROM MEK. PUT ON A
PROTECTIVE SPLASH GOGGLE AND GLOVES WHEN YOU USE MEK. KEEP
MEK AWAY FROM SPARKS, FLAME AND HEAT. MEK IS A POISONOUS AND
FLAMMABLE SOLVENT WHICH CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONS OR
DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT.
(8) Clean the duct around the patch with a cotton wiper, G00034, and solvent, B00148, to remove
unwanted resin, A00040 or resin, A50145.
SUBTASK 21-20-02-340-107
(9) Attach a vacuum bag, STD-94, to the duct to hold the repair layers and to keep the duct shape
(SRM 51-70-04).
(a) Cure for a minimum of 24 hours under a minimum of 20 in/Hg (68 kPa) vacuum at 65°F
(18°C) - 75°F (24°C).
1) Continue to hold vacuum and complete the cure at 160°F (71.1°C) - 180°F (82.2°C)
for 2 to 2.5 hours.
(b) Remove the vacuum bag, STD-94, without damage to the cured layers.
SUBTASK 21-20-02-340-108
(10) If necessary, sand the patch on the outer duct surface to get a correct fit.
(a) Keep a wall thickness of 0.045 in. (1.143 mm) - 0.065 in. (1.651 mm) in this area.
NOTE: Wrinkles, creases, and unwanted resin are not permitted in this area. Sand these
items flush where necessary.
SUBTASK 21-20-02-340-110
(11) Seal any exposed fabric with a brushed-on coating of resin, A00040 or resin, A50145.
SUBTASK 21-20-02-340-109
(12) Let the resin, A00040, or resin, A50145 cure.

3) BMS 8-300 Type VIII foam insulation, G51170.
(b) Use BMS 5-157 MPVF tape, G50327, tape, G51202, or BMS 5-157 MPEEK tape,
G50789, to install the insulation.
SUBTASK 21-20-02-840-121
(2) Install the panels or other airplane structure removed to get access to the duct joint.

G. Mix Manifold Removal
SUBTASK 21-21-01-010-018-002
(1) To remove the check valves [39] from the recirculation fans, do these steps:
(a) Hold the check valves [39] when you remove the couplings [37] and sleeves [38].
(b) Remove the check valves [39].
SUBTASK 21-21-01-010-019-002
(2) To remove the forward muffler [41] from the mix bay, do these steps:
(a) Remove the clamp [46] that is installed at the rear bulkhead of the mix bay.
(b) Remove the nuts [47], washers [48], and spacers [49] that are below the bracket.
(c) Remove the screws [51], washers [50], and washers [48] from the clamp [52].
(d) Remove the coupling [35] and the sleeve [36] from the upper duct of the forward muffler.
(e) Carefully remove the forward muffler [41].
SUBTASK 21-21-01-010-020-002
(3) To remove the upper mix manifold [31], do these steps:
(a) Disconnect the electrical connectors [32] from the mix manifold temperature sensors.
(b) Remove the tie strap that attaches the hoseduct to the top of the upper mix manifold [31].
(c) Remove the clamps [33] and sleeves [34].
(d) Remove the screws [56] and washers [55].
(e) Carefully remove the upper mix manifold [31].
SUBTASK 21-21-01-010-021-002
(4) Remove the collector ring [54] and gaskets [53].
SUBTASK 21-21-01-010-022-002
(5) Remove the couplings [40] from the lower ducts of the mix manifold.
SUBTASK 21-21-01-020-004-002
(6) Disconnect the drain tubes from the lower mix manifold [43].
(a) Remove the straps [42].
NOTE: Clamps may be installed instead of the straps depending on configuration.
(b) Pull the four drain tubes off the lower mix manifold [43].
(c) Make a record of the locations of the drain lines and the straps [42] to make sure that
they are installed in the same positions.
SUBTASK 21-21-01-020-005-002
(7) To remove the lower mix manifold [43] from the mix bay, do these steps:
(a) Remove the screws [44] and washers [45] that attach support brackets of the lower mix
manifold [43] to the airplane structure.

 ALL
(b) Remove the bolts [61] and washers [62] that attach the clamps [60] to the lower mix
manifold [43].
1) Make a record of the locations of the bolts [61], washers [62] and clamps [60] to
make sure they are installed in the same positions.
(c) Remove the bolts [65] and washers [62] that attach the lower mix manifold [43] to the
spacer on the airplane skin.
(d) Carefully remove the lower mix manifold [43] from the mix bay.

21-21-01-400-804-002Ground Conditioned Air Check Valve InstallationPDF p. 283
7. Ground Conditioned Air Check Valve Installation
(Figure 403)
A. General
(1) The hinge on the check valve has a spring which holds the check valve almost open when the
air conditioning system is off. When the air conditioning system is on, the pressure in the mix
manifold causes the swing check valve to close. Before you install the lower mix manifold, you
must do a check of the check valve and adjust the hinge if it is necessary. The check valve
must open and close correctly.

G. Ground Conditioned Air Check Valve Installation
SUBTASK 21-21-01-420-007-002
(1) Do these steps to install the check valve [59] in the lower mix manifold [43]:
(a) Put the check valve [59] in its position in the lower mix manifold [43].
(b) Loosely install the bolts [63] and washers [64].
(c) Adjust the check valve [59] so that the bolts [63] are in the center of the adjustment slots.
(d) Fully tighten the bolts [63].
Config 2
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
H. Ground Conditioned Air Check Valve Adjustment
SUBTASK 21-21-01-710-004-002
(1) Check the check valve [59] as follows:
(a) Put a straight edge on the flange of the rear duct of the lower mix manifold [43].
(b) Move the straight edge to the end of the check valve [59] opposite the hinge.
(c) Make sure that the end of the check valve [59] touches the straight edge.
(d) Move the straight edge to the end of the check valve [59] below the hinge.
(e) Make sure that there is a small clearance between the edge of the check valve [59] and
straight edge.
(f) If there is no clearance, adjust the hinge as follows:
1) Loosen the hinge adjustment bolts [63].
2) Move the hinge up as necessary.
3) Tighten the hinge adjustment bolts [63].
(g) Push down on the check valve [59] at the hinge.
(h) Make sure that the clearance in the above step closes without too much downward force.
(i) Release the pressure on the check valve [59].
(j) Make sure that there is clearance again between the edge of the check valve [59] and
straight edge.
(k) If too much force is necessary to remove the clearance when you push down on the
check valve [59], adjust the hinge as follows:
1) Loosen the hinge adjustment bolts [63].
2) Move the hinge down as necessary.
3) Tighten the hinge adjustment bolts [63].
(l) Do this check again to make sure that the check valve [59] operates correctly.

 ALL

SUBTASK 21-22-02-020-006

follows:

assembly [2] aligns with the hole in the tab on the outlet valve [8].
SUBTASK 21-22-02-420-004

SUBTASK 21-23-01-790-001
(1) Do the overhead distribution duct test as follows:
(a) If the packs are operational, do the overhead distribution test as follows:
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
1) Do this task: Supply Pressure to the Pneumatic System (Selection),
TASK 36-00-00-860-801.
2) Put the L and R PACK switches, on the P5-10 air conditioning panel, to the AUTO
position.
3) Make sure that there is not excessive leakage of air at the connections on the
distribution duct that was replaced.
4) Repair any connection in the overhead distribution ducts where airflow can be felt
on a hand a minimum of 2 inches away from the surface of a joint.
(b) If the packs are not operational and a test of the overhead distribution ducts is necessary,
do these steps:
1) Supply ground conditioned air to the distribution system, do this task: Supply
Conditioned Air with a Ground Air Source, TASK 21-00-00-800-805.
2) Make sure that there is not excessive leakage of air at the connections on the
distribution duct that was replaced.
a) Excessive leakage is airflow that can be felt on a hand a minimum of 2 inches
away from the surface of a joint.
3) Repair any connection in the overhead distribution ducts where airflow can be felt
on a hand a minimum of 2 inches away from the surface of a joint.

21-23-01-300-801Overhead Distribution Duct Insulation RepairPDF p. 367
4. Overhead Distribution Duct Insulation Repair
(Figure 201)
A. General
(1) The repair of the duct insulation consists of replacement of the tape that holds the insulation to
the duct.
(2) CFR 14 Part 121.312 mandates that insulation material installed in the fuselage as a
replacement after September 2, 2005 must meet the flame propagation requirements of CFR
Part 25.856, effective September 2, 2003.
(3) Existing insulation material can be removed and re-installed if it is not damaged. Replacement
insulation material must meet the flame propagation requirement.
(4) Melamine foam insulation, G50449, BMS8-385, Type 4, Grade 1 is the preferred foam
insulation material that meets the flame propagation requirement. Melamine foam insulation,
G51169, BMS 8-385, Type 6 and foam insulation, G51170, BMS 8-300, Type VIII insulation is
optional to BMS8-385 Type 4.
(5) Air conditioning ducts with polyimide foam insulation, G02470 must be wrapped with tape,
G50327, tape, G51202 or tape, G50789 to meet the flammability/flame propagation
requirements. Wrap tape, G50327, tape, G51202 or tape, G50789 across 100% of the brown
hypalon insulation surface on the polyimide foam insulation, G02470.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(6) Do not use BMS8-39 polyurethane foam insulation for repairs due to the degradation in
flammability properties over time.
(7) When insulation material is removed and re-installed, any existing tape that does not meet the
flame propagation requirement must be removed or completely covered with tape that does
meet the requirement.

D. Insulation Repair for Overhead Distribution Duct
SUBTASK 21-23-01-010-002
(1) Remove ceiling panels as required to get access to the distribution duct.
SUBTASK 21-23-01-010-004
(2) As required, remove the interior furnishings for access.
SUBTASK 21-23-01-020-009
(3) Remove all loose tape from the ends or seams of the insulation blanket on the distribution
duct.
SUBTASK 21-23-01-420-006
(4) Apply tape to the seams or ends of the insulation blanket as follows:
(a) Put the edges of the insulation together and apply two-inch wide tape, G50327, tape,
G51202 or tape, G50789 to the seam of the insulation blanket so that no insulation foam
edge can be seen.
(b) Apply a circumferential wrap of two-inch wide tape, G50327, tape, G51202 or tape,
G50789 on the insulation at the ends of the duct so that the tape extends one inch
beyond the end of the insulation blanket.
(c) Apply circumferential wraps of one-inch wide tape, G50327, tape, G51202 or tape,
G50789 along the length of the duct to secure the insulation blanket to the duct.
SUBTASK 21-23-01-410-002
(5) Install all ceiling panels that were removed for access.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
SUBTASK 21-23-01-410-004

D. General
SUBTASK 21-23-01-350-004
(1) This procedure provides instructions for either the replacement or repair of the insulation on
the duct segments of the overhead distribution system that connect to the sidewall risers.
Some airplanes did not have insulation installed on the production line in the area of the spuds
that connect to the sidewall risers. For those airplanes, refer to SB 737-21A1139 for
instructions to install this insulation.
E. Preparation for the Replacement/Repair of the Insulation
SUBTASK 21-23-01-864-001
(1) Make sure that the L and R PACK switches on the P5-10 air conditioning panel are set to OFF.
SUBTASK 21-23-01-864-002
(2) Remove the pressure from the pneumatic system. To remove the pressure, do this task:
Remove Pressure from the Pneumatic System, TASK 36-00-00-860-806.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
SUBTASK 21-23-01-010-005
(3) Remove the ceiling panels as required to get access to the duct segment of the overhead
distribution system that connects to the sidewall risers.
SUBTASK 21-23-01-020-012
(4) If necessary, remove the overhead distribution system duct segment that connects to the
sidewall risers ducts. To remove the duct segment, do this task: Overhead Distribution Duct
Removal, TASK 21-23-01-000-801.
SUBTASK 21-23-01-020-011
(5) If applicable, remove all tape and insulation from the area around the riser spuds on the duct
segment to be repaired.
SUBTASK 21-23-01-110-001
(6) Clean the area around the riser spuds without the insulation as follows:
WARNING
DO NOT GET METHYL ETHYL KETONE (MEK) IN YOUR MOUTH OR
EYES, OR ON YOUR SKIN. DO NOT BREATHE THE FUMES FROM MEK.
PUT ON A PROTECTIVE SPLASH GOGGLE AND GLOVES WHEN YOU
USE MEK. KEEP MEK AWAY FROM SPARKS, FLAME AND HEAT. MEK IS
A POISONOUS AND FLAMMABLE SOLVENT WHICH CAN CAUSE
INJURIES TO PERSONS OR DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT.
(a) Wet a lint-free cloth, G00834 with Series 91 solvent, B01011.
(b) Wipe the area around the riser spuds on the duct segment until all traces of dirt, debris,
or tape is removed.
(c) Use a lint-free cloth, G00834 and remove all traces of the solvent.
SUBTASK 21-23-01-350-001
(7) Cut the foam insulation, G02470 insulation into four sections to the approximate size
necessary to cover the bare surfaces around the riser spuds.
(a) Refer to Figure 202that illustrates the four sections of foam insulation.
SUBTASK 21-23-01-350-002
(8) Position each section in its place and mark the location on the section where the riser spuds
will intersect the section.
SUBTASK 21-23-01-350-003
(9) Make small cuts in the areas of the insulation where the riser spuds will fit so that the insulation
will fit around the spuds.
(a) Cut from the center of the semicircle that you marked to the circumference of the marked
semicircle.
(b) Make the cuts on each of the four sections of insulation.
SUBTASK 21-23-01-420-007
(10) Position the four sections of foam insulation around the riser spuds on the duct segment.
SUBTASK 21-23-01-420-008
(11) Install tape, G50327, tape, G51202 or tape, G50789 on the foam insulation as shown on
Figure 202 and in accordance with these guidelines:
(a) One-inch wide or 2-inch wide advanced insulation blanket tape, G50327, tape, G51202
or tape, G50789 must cover 100% of the brown colored “Hypalon” insulation surface.
(b) Cut the tape, G50327, tape, G51202 or tape, G50789 as required to fit around the spuds.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(c) Tape may be installed spiral wrapped or lengthwise depending on the installers'
preference.
(d) Tape may be installed in any configuration as long as 100% coverage of the foam
insulation is obtained.
(e) The tape must overlap all edges and seams of the insulation by a minimum of 1.00 inch
(25.4mm).
(f) Wider tape may be cut into narrower strips or any unique shape if desired to assist in
complete foam insulation coverage.
(g) Maintain a minimum of 1/8-inch overlap of the tape.
(h) Avoid compression of the foam insulation.
(i) Wrinkles in the tape are acceptable if the wrinkles are pinched together to remove all
voids.
(j) Covering of existing insulation tape is not required.
(k) Tape may be installed to the foam insulation prior to installation of the duct if desired by
the installer.
(l) Tape orientation is optional.
SUBTASK 21-23-01-420-009
(12) Install the repaired overhead distribution system duct segment. To install the duct segment, do
this task: Overhead Distribution Duct Installation, TASK 21-23-01-400-801.
SUBTASK 21-23-01-780-001
(13) Do this test of the overhead distribution system:
(a) Supply conditioned air to the overhead distribution system. To supply conditioned air, do
this task: Supply Conditioned Air to the Airplane, TASK 21-00-00-800-801.
(b) Make sure that there are no leaks at the joints of the repaired duct segment of the
overhead distribution assembly.
(c) Repair any leak that you can feel with your hand when it is 2 in. (51 mm) from the duct.
F. Put the Airplane Back to Its Usual Condition
SUBTASK 21-23-01-864-003
(1) Remove the conditioned air from the airplane if it is not necessary. To remove conditioned air,
do this task: Remove Conditioned Air from the Airplane, TASK 21-00-00-800-802.
SUBTASK 21-23-01-410-005
(2) Install all ceiling panels that were removed for access to the overhead distribution system duct
segment.

SUBTASK 21-23-01-211-001
(26) Inspect the orifice [12] upstream of the outboard plenum/nozzle assembly [13] at the Y section.
(a) If the orifice [12] is clogged, then do these steps:
1) Make sure that there is no air flow in the distribution duct [1] that contains the
orifice [12].
2) Get access to the distribution duct [1].
3) If the flex hose [10] is attached to the distribution duct [1] with plastic strap [15]
remove and discard the plastic strap [15].
4) If the flex hose [10] is attached to the distribution duct [1] with clamps [11], do these
steps:
a) Loosen the clamps [11].
b) Move the clamps [11] away from the flex hose [10].
5) Move the flex hose [10] away from the orifice [12] identifier tags.
6) Remove the orifice [12] from the end of the duct.
(b) Once the orifice [12] is clear, then do these steps:
1) Make sure that the new orifice [12] is the same as the orifice [12] that was removed.
2) Clean the mating surfaces of the orifice [12].
3) Clean the mating surfaces of the duct.
NOTE: The new adhesive will not bond to the duct unless the old adhesive is
removed.
4) Do these steps to install the orifice [12] in the duct:
a) Apply the adhesive, A00028 to the mating surfaces of the duct and the
orifice [12].
b) When the adhesive, A00028 is tacky, put the orifice [12] on the end of the duct.
NOTE: Make sure that none of the holes in the orifice are blocked by the
adhesive.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
 006, 007, 013, 014, 018-020, 043, 044, 056-063, 067-078, 081, 083-103, 111-114, 121-129, 131, 132, 135,
138-169, 174-179, 182-187, 189-203, 205-209, 212-220, 223, 224, 231-236, 239-298, 301-304, 306, 308, 315-317,
322-341, 343, 346-377 (Continued)
c) Remove the unwanted adhesive, A00028 from the outer side of the duct and
the orifice [12].
NOTE: The flexible sleeve can be bonded to the duct if the unwanted
adhesive is not removed.
d) Bend the identification tags to the same shape as the end of the duct.
NOTE: If possible, bend the identification tags in the direction of the airflow
through the duct.
e) Make sure that all of the identification tags are on the outer side of the duct.
f) Make sure that none of the identification tags are bonded to the duct.
g) Make sure that the orifice [12] is tightly attached to the duct.
5) Do these steps to install the flex hose [10] on the duct:
a) Move the flex hose [10] onto the duct connection.
b) Make sure that the flex hose [10] has the same overlap on each side of the
duct connection.
c) Make sure that you can see the part number on the orifice [12] identification
tags.
6) Do these steps to install the plastic straps [15] or clamps [11] on the flex hose [10]:
a) If the flex hose [10] was attached to the duct with plastic straps [15], install
new plastic straps [15] on the flex hose [10].
b) If the flex hose [10] was attached to the duct with clamps [11], move the
clamps [11] onto the flex hose [10].
c) Align the clamps [11] or the plastic straps [15] with the duct wall.
NOTE: Do not align the straps or the clamps with the duct bead. The flexible
sleeve will not make a good seal if it is tightened against the duct
bead.
d) Tighten the clamps [11] or the plastic straps [15].
7) Make sure that there is air flow in the duct that contains the orifice. To do this,
operate one or more of these systems:
a) The lavatory/galley ventilation system.
b) The equipment cooling system.
c) The supplemental heating systems.
d) The cooling packs.
e) The pneumatic air supply system.
8) Make sure that there is no air leakage from the duct connections.
9) Make sure that the conditioned air outlet does not have excessive noise or
excessive air flow.
 ALL

I. Heavy Check Cleaning
SUBTASK 21-23-01-010-011
(1) Remove the overhead stowage bin, do this task: Overhead Stowage Bin - Removal,
TASK 25-24-31-020-801 or Overhead Stowage Bin - Removal, TASK 25-24-31-000-801-001 or

TASK 25-23-61-000-804).
SUBTASK 21-23-01-020-020
(3) Remove the overhead distribution duct, do this task: Overhead Distribution Duct Removal,
TASK 21-23-01-000-801.
SUBTASK 21-23-01-160-001
(4) Clean the orifice [12] on the sidewall diffuser [17].
(a) Remove the sidewall diffuser [17].
1) Remove the adjustable plastic strap, G51500, from the hose duct [18].
2) Remove the hose duct [18] from the sidewall diffuser [17].
3) Remove the screws [16] from the sidewall diffuser [17].
(b) Clean the orifice [12] with a stiff bristle brush, STD-133.
(c) Install the sidewall diffuser [17].
1) Install the hose duct [18] on the sidewall diffuser [17].
2) Install the adjustable plastic strap, G51500, on the hose duct [18].
3) Install the screws [16].
(d) Inspect the airflow after the cleaning.

SUBTASK 21-23-02-210-001
(1) Make sure that the bottom of the transition duct [7] is approximately 8 inches above the
passenger compartment floor.
SUBTASK 21-23-02-211-001
(2) If necessary, reposition the transition duct [7] so that the bottom of the transition duct is
properly positioned 8 inches above the passenger compartment floor.
SUBTASK 21-23-02-430-001
(3) If the sidewall riser ducts [3] need to be moved down to be installed on the transition duct
spuds [6], do these steps:
(a) Cut the plastic tie straps [8] from the three supports [1] that hold the riser ducts [3].
(b) Position the riser ducts [3] so that they can be installed on the spuds [6].
SUBTASK 21-23-02-360-002
(4) If the riser ducts are installed without a flex sleeve, then do these steps for the repair:
(a) Make sure there is no contamination in the riser ducts or the transition duct spuds.
(b) Remove all tape from the spuds [6] on the transition duct [7].
(c) Remove all remaining parts of tape from the riser ducts and the spuds with a wiper,
G50262 that is wet with alcohol, B00130 or solvent, B00083.
(d) Use a dry wiper, G50262 to remove the remaining alcohol, B00130 or solvent, B00083
from the riser ducts and the spuds.
1) Do not allow the alcohol, B00130 or solvent, B00083 to dry on the riser ducts and
the spuds.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(e) Wrap the ends of the spuds [6] on the transition duct [7] with G565 tape, G00093 to
build-up the diameter of the spud to match the diameter of the riser duct so that there is a
tight fit between the two.
(f) Slide the riser duct [3] over the transition duct spud [6] so that there is a 1-inch overlap
between the spud and the riser duct.
1) Shape the round riser duct as necessary to fit over the oblong spud.
(g) Install the clamps [4] that hold the riser ducts and transition duct spuds together as
follows:
1) Position the clamps equally between the end of the riser duct and the transition duct
bead (0.25 to 0.45 inch from the end of the riser duct).
2) Position the clamps so that the screw head is 45 degrees forward or aft from the
station line.
NOTE: The screw head can interfere with the side panel if it is positioned on the
station line.
3) Tighten the clamp at 13 to 17 inch-pounds.
SUBTASK 21-23-02-360-003
(5) If the riser ducts are installed with a flex sleeve, then do these steps for the repair:
(a) Make sure there is no contamination in the riser ducts, the flex sleeves, or the transition
duct spuds.
(b) If necessary, clean the riser ducts, the flex sleeves, and the spuds with a wiper, G50262
that is wet with alcohol, B00130 or solvent, B00083.
(c) If necessary, use a dry wiper, G50262 to remove the remaining alcohol, B00130 or
solvent, B00083 from the riser ducts, the flex sleeves, and the spuds.
1) Do not allow the alcohol, B00130 or solvent, B00083 to dry on the riser ducts, the
flex sleeves, and the spuds.
(d) Slide the flex sleeve [5] over the riser duct [3] or transition duct spud [6] so that there is a
1-inch overlap between the duct or spud and the flex sleeve.
1) Shape the round flex sleeve as necessary to fit over the oblong spud.
(e) Install the clamps [4] that hold the riser ducts, the flex sleeves, and the transition duct
spuds together as follows:
1) Position the clamps equally between the end of the flex sleeve and the duct bead
(0.25 to 0.45 inch from the end of the flex sleeve).
2) Position the clamps so that the screw head is 45 degrees forward or aft from the
station line.
NOTE: The screw head can interfere with the side panel if it is positioned on the
station line.
3) Tighten the clamp at 13 to 17 inch-pounds.
SUBTASK 21-23-02-430-003
(6) If the riser ducts were moved down and the plastic tie straps removed, install a new adjustable
plastic strap, G50218 to hold each riser duct to the supports [1], as required.
E. Post-Repair Check of the Sidewall Riser Ducts/Transition Duct

(1) Supply conditioned air to the passenger cabin. Do this task: Supply Conditioned Air to the

 ALL
SUBTASK 21-23-02-790-001
(2) Do a check for any leaks in the sidewall riser ducts/transition duct installation.

(1) Do the steps that follow to remove the return air grille [1] with latches:

a) Carefully move the right adjacent return air grille to the left.

(1) Do the steps that follow to install the return air grille [1] with latches:

(c) Move the return air grille [1] outboard until the lower edge rests against the inner chord of

air grille [1].

grille [1] and the left edge of the right adjacent return air grille.

 ALL

21-23-03-200-801Return Air Grille Baffle InspectionPDF p. 405
7. Return Air Grille Baffle Inspection
A. General
(1) This task has instructions to inspect, remove, and install the baffles on the backside of the
return air grilles.
(2) In the event of a rapid decompression of the airplane fuselage, the baffles are designed to
detach from the backside of the return air grilles to permit airflow movement from the main
cabin to the lower lobe compartments. After a decompression event, it is necessary to inspect
the baffles and reinstall them to the backside of the return air grilles.
B. References
Reference Title
25-22-00 P/B 401 PASSENGER SEATS - REMOVAL/INSTALLATION
C. Location Zones
Zone Area
200 Upper Half of Fuselage
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL

SUBTASK 21-23-03-020-003
(1) Remove the passenger seats as needed to get access to the return air grille [1]. Do the
applicable task: PASSENGER SEATS - REMOVAL/INSTALLATION,
PAGEBLOCK 25-22-00/401.
(2) Remove the return air grille [1] (Return Air Grille Removal, TASK 21-23-03-000-801).
E. Baffle Inspection
SUBTASK 21-23-03-212-001
(1) If the baffle [3] is missing or has damage (tears, punctures, rips, cuts), install a new baffle [3].
SUBTASK 21-23-03-212-002
(2) If the baffle [3] has become partially or fully detached from the backside of the return air
grille [1], reinstall the baffle [3] with the attachment hardware.
SUBTASK 21-23-03-212-003
(3) If the baffle [3] has missing or damaged attachment hardware, install new attachment
hardware.
SUBTASK 21-23-03-212-004
(4) Inspect the lower sidewall areas for unwanted materials or missing baffle [3] hardware, and
clean the areas as applicable before you reinstall the return air grille [1].

(1) To remove the baffle on the return air grille [1], do this task: (Return Air Grille Baffle Removal,

2. Sidewall Riser Ducts - Removal
(Figure 401 or Figure 402 or Figure 403)
A. General
(1) This procedure contains the tasks to remove and install the sidewall riser ducts between the
distribution bay and the overhead distribution ducts.
(a) The sidewall riser duct installation consists of these components:
1) Six ducts
2) Three support assemblies
3) Six flexible hoses
4) Six flexible sleeves
5) A transition duct assembly.
 006, 007, 013, 014, 018-020, 043, 044, 056-063, 067-078, 081, 083-103, 111-114, 121-129, 131, 132, 135,
138-169
6) Tape, clamps and plastic ties
 174-179, 182-187, 189-203, 205-209, 212-220, 223, 224
7) Clamps and plastic ties
 231-236, 239-298, 301-304, 306, 308, 315-317, 322-341, 343, 346-999
8) Plastic ties
 ALL
(2) There are three sets of riser ducts, two on the left side of the passenger cabin and one set on
the right side.
(3) Access to the sidewall riser ducts is through the sidewall panels directly above the distribution
bay in the main passenger cabin.
 006, 007, 013, 014, 018-020, 043, 044, 056-063, 067-078, 081, 083-103, 111-114, 121-129, 131, 132, 135,
138-169, 174-179, 182-187, 189-203, 205-209, 212-220, 223, 224
(4) There are two configurations of the installation where the sidewall riser ducts connect to the
spuds on the transition duct. One configuration consists of the sidewall riser ducts directly
connected to the spuds on the transition duct with a clamp to secure each riser duct and spud
together. The other configuration uses a flex sleeve between each riser duct and transition duct
spud with two clamps to secure the connections.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
 231-236, 239-298, 301-304, 306, 308, 315-317, 322-341, 343, 346-999
(5) There are two configurations of the installation where the sidewall riser ducts connect to the
spuds on the transition duct. One configuration consists of the sidewall riser ducts directly
connected to the spuds on the transition duct with a tie-strap to secure each riser duct and
spud together. The other configuration uses a flex sleeve between each riser duct and
transition duct spud with an upper tie strap and lower clamp to secure the connections.
 ALL

E. Sidewall Riser Ducts Installation
SUBTASK 21-23-04-160-001
(1) If you removed the transition duct [12] with the sidewall riser ducts [4], then remove all the
sealant between the faying surfaces of the transition duct [12] and elbow duct [10] as follows:
(a) Lightly abrade the surfaces with old adhesive with 320 grit or finer abrasive cloth,
B00102, until the old adhesive is removed.
(b) Wet a cotton wiper, G00034, with solvent, B00083, or alcohol, B00130, and wipe all
faying surfaces until all traces of the old adhesive are gone.
1) Wet the wiper by pouring the solvent onto the wiper, not by dipping the wiper into
the solvent source.

1) Do not thin the primer or use primer that is cloudy or milky.

and 4 hours maximum.

elbow duct are the bonding surfaces.

application of the adhesive.

WARNING

F. Recirculation Air Filter Removal
SUBTASK 21-25-01-020-011
(1) Remove the left recirculation air filter [3].
(a) Remove the screws [6] from the retainer [7] on the filter housing [8].
(b) Remove the retainer [7] from the filter housing [8].
WARNING
DO NOT LET THE FILTER TOUCH YOUR SKIN. DO NOT SHAKE OR HIT
THE FILTER. DO NOT LET THE FILTER FALL. DO NOT USE
COMPRESSED AIR TO CLEAN THE FILTER OR FILTER HOUSING. THIS
CAN CAUSE THE INFECTIOUS MATERIAL TO BECOME AIRBORNE.
DISCARD THE FILTER IN A PLASTIC DISPOSAL BAG. OBEY THESE
INSTRUCTIONS TO PREVENT INJURIES TO PERSONNEL.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(WARNING PRECEDES)
CAUTION
DO NOT LET THE RECIRCULATION FILTER TOUCH THE WIRE BUNDLE
THAT IS IMMEDIATELY FORWARD OF THE FILTER. THE FORWARD AND
AFT LOWER OUTBOARD CORNERS OF THE FILTER HAVE SHARP
EDGES. THE SHARP EDGES CAN CUT THE INSULATION ON THE WIRE
BUNDLE.
(c) If possible, slide the plastic bag, G00624, over the filter when removing the recirculation
air filter [3] from the filter housing [8] to minimize contamination.
(d) Seal the bag closed with tape.
WARNING
OBEY THE AIRLINE POLICY, LOCAL HEALTH DEPARTMENT, AND LAW
ENFORCEMENT REGULATIONS WHEN YOU DISCARD THIS MATERIAL.
OBEY THESE INSTRUCTIONS TO PREVENT INJURIES TO
PERSONNEL.
(e) Discard the bag with the filter. Refer to the airline, local health, safety and regulatory
procedures for disposal of material.
SUBTASK 21-25-01-020-012
(2) Remove the right recirculation air filter [3].
(a) Release the quarter-turn fasteners [1] which attach the access panel [2] to the filter
housing [4].
(b) Remove the access panel [2].
WARNING
DO NOT LET THE FILTER TOUCH YOUR SKIN. DO NOT SHAKE OR HIT
THE FILTER. DO NOT LET THE FILTER FALL. DO NOT USE
COMPRESSED AIR TO CLEAN THE FILTER OR FILTER HOUSING. THIS
CAN CAUSE THE INFECTIOUS MATERIAL TO BECOME AIRBORNE.
DISCARD THE FILTER IN A PLASTIC DISPOSAL BAG. OBEY THESE
INSTRUCTIONS TO PREVENT INJURIES TO PERSONNEL.
(c) If possible, slide the plastic bag, G00624, over the filter when removing the recirculation
air filter [3] from the filter housing [4] to minimize contamination.
(d) Seal the bag closed with tape.
WARNING
OBEY THE AIRLINE POLICY, LOCAL HEALTH DEPARTMENT, AND LAW
ENFORCEMENT REGULATIONS WHEN YOU DISCARD THIS MATERIAL.
OBEY THESE INSTRUCTIONS TO PREVENT INJURIES TO
PERSONNEL.
(e) Discard the bag with the filter. Refer to the airline, local health, safety and regulatory
procedures for disposal of material.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL

SUBTASK 21-25-01-670-003
WARNING
ISOPROPYL ALCOHOL IS POISONOUS AND FLAMMABLE. USE
PROTECTION EQUIPMENT. MAKE SURE THAT YOU USE ISOPROPYL
ALCOHOL IN AN AREA WITH AIRFLOW. IF YOU DO NOT OBEY, INJURY TO
PERSONNEL CAN OCCUR.
(1) Disinfect hard non-porous surfaces near the filter with a solution of alcohol, B00130, Calla
1452 cleaner, B50280, or Matrix #3 cleaner, B50364.
NOTE: Follow the disinfectant manufacturer's instruction and refer to the EPA List N for
applicable contact/dwell time.
NOTE: Refer to the EPA List N or local health authority guidance for required contact/dwell
time for Isopropyl Alcohol to be used as a disinfectant.
SUBTASK 21-25-01-670-001

disinfecting of tools.
SUBTASK 21-25-01-020-020
WARNING

ONE TIME. DO NOT TRY TO CLEAN IT. DISCARD THE EQUIPMENT IN A
PLASTIC DISPOSAL BAG. OBEY THESE INSTRUCTIONS TO PREVENT
INJURIES TO PERSONNEL.

PERSONNEL.

safety and regulatory procedures for disposal of material.

WARNING
CLEAN YOUR HANDS WITH SOAP AND FLUSH WITH HOT WATER. DIRTY
HANDS WITH CONTAMINATION CAN CAUSE DISEASE AND ILLNESSES TO
PERSONS.

E. Recirculation Air Filter Installation
SUBTASK 21-25-01-420-007
(1) Install the left recirculation air filter [3].
(a) Make sure that there is no unwanted material or contamination in the filter housing [8]
which could cause damage to the recirculation fan.
CAUTION
DO NOT LET THE RECIRCULATION FILTER TOUCH THE WIRE BUNDLE
THAT IS IMMEDIATELY FORWARD OF THE FILTER. THE FORWARD AND
AFT LOWER OUTBOARD CORNERS OF THE FILTER HAVE SHARP
EDGES. THE SHARP EDGES CAN CUT THE INSULATION ON THE WIRE
BUNDLE.
(b) Put the new recirculation air filter [3] in the filter housing [8].
(c) Check the spring clips.
1) Make sure that the spring clips apply pressure to keep the filter in position.
2) Make sure that all spring clips are installed and not damaged.
(d) Hold the retainer [7] in its position on the filter housing [8].
(e) Install the screws [6] for the retainer [7] on the filter housing [8].
SUBTASK 21-25-01-420-008
(2) Install the right recirculation air filter [3].
(a) Make sure that there is no unwanted material or contamination in the filter housing [4]
which could cause damage to the recirculation fan.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
CAUTION
MAKE SURE THAT THE AFT SPRING CLIPS OF THE RECIRCULATION
AIR FILTER ARE IN TIGHT CONTACT WITH THE FILTER RAIL. IF THE
AFT SPRING CLIPS ARE NOT IN THE CORRECT POSITION, THEN THE
FLOATING SPRING CLIPS CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE
RECIRCULATION FAN AND FILTER HOUSING DURING INSTALLATION.
(b) Put the new recirculation air filter [3] in the filter housing [4].
(c) Check the spring clips.
1) Make sure that the spring clips apply pressure to keep the filter in position.
2) Make sure that all spring clips are installed and not damaged.
(d) Put the access panel [2] in its position and turn the quarter-turn fastener [1] to attach the
access panel [2] to the filter housing [4].

2. Recirculation Fan Check Valve Inspection
(Figure 601)
NOTE: This procedure is a scheduled maintenance task.
A. References
Reference Title

21-25-03-400-801 Recirculation Fan Check Valve Installation (P/B 401)
B. Tools/Equipment
Reference Description

C. Location Zones
Zone Area

126 Air Conditioning Distribution Bay - Right
D. Prepare for the Inspection
SUBTASK 21-25-03-020-004
(1) Remove the recirculation fan check valve, do this task: Recirculation Fan Check Valve
Removal, TASK 21-25-03-000-801.
E. Recirculation Fan Check Valve Inspection
SUBTASK 21-25-03-210-002
(1) Examine the recirculation fan check valve as follows:
(a) Use your finger or a pencil to push on each flapper to open them.
(b) Make sure that each flapper opens freely and moves smoothly to the stop tube.
(c) Make sure that each flapper closes smoothly and touches fully on the face of the check
valve body.
(d) Make sure that there is no damage to the flappers:
1) Measure the thickness of the area on the flappers where the flappers contact the
stop tube.
2) Make sure that the stop-tube contact area on the flappers is a minimum of 0.020 in.
(0.508 mm) thick.
a) Measure with a micrometer, STD-595, a vernier caliper (0 - 6 inch, readable to
1/1000 inch), STD-1097, or an equivalent tool.
3) Repair or replace check valves that do not meet the minimum thickness.
(e) Make sure that there is no corrosion or lint on the flappers or the hinge pin.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
F. Put the Airplane Back to Its Usual Condition
SUBTASK 21-25-03-420-003
(1) Install the recirculation fan check valve, do this task: Recirculation Fan Check Valve
Installation, TASK 21-25-03-400-801.

B. Preparation for Galley Ceiling Ventilation Grill Cleaning
SUBTASK 21-26-03-000-001

or the aft passenger entry way. To remove the ventilation grill, do this task: Galley Ceiling
Ventilation Grill Removal, TASK 21-26-03-000-801.
C. Galley Ceiling Ventilation Grill Cleaning
SUBTASK 21-26-03-100-001
(1) Do these steps to clean the ventilation grill:
(a) Prepare a cleaning solution of a general purpose household detergent cleaner, B00541
diluted with water in accordance with the instructions on the detergent container.
(b) Clean the grill with a cotton wiper cotton wiper, G00034 that is moist with the cleaning
solution.
(c) If the cotton wiper, G00034 with the cleaning solution did not remove all dirt deposits or
contamination from the grill, clean the grill with a cotton wiper, G00034 that is moist with
alcohol, B00130.
(d) Flush the grill with clean water until all traces of the detergent solution or alcohol are
removed.
(e) Dry the grill with a dry, clean cotton wiper, G00034.

F. Equipment Cooling System Tryout
NOTE: This tryout is to make sure these components in the equipment cooling system are in a zero
energy state.
• Equipment Cooling Supply Fan
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
• Equipment Cooling Exhaust Fan
• Equipment Cooling Overboard Exhaust Valve
NOTE: Wait a minimum of 60 seconds after deactivation before you do the tryout steps.
SUBTASK 21-27-00-860-371
(1) For the equipment cooling supply and exhaust fans, do these steps:
(a) Do this task: Supply Electrical Power, TASK 24-22-00-860-811.
(b) Make sure that the EQUIP COOLING SUPPLY switch on the equipment cooling panel is
in the NORM position.
(c) Make sure that the EQUIP COOLING EXHAUST switch on the equipment cooling panel
is in the NORM position.
(d) Make sure that the EQUIP COOLING SUPPLY OFF light is on.
(e) Make sure that the EQUIP COOLING EXHAUST OFF light is on.
(f) Put the EQUIP COOLING SUPPLY switch in the ALTN position.
(g) Put the EQUIP COOLING EXHAUST switch in the ALTN position.
(h) Wait a minimum of 60 seconds.
(i) Make sure that the EQUIP COOLING SUPPLY OFF light is on.
(j) Make sure that the EQUIP COOLING EXHAUST OFF light is on.
(k) Do this task: Remove Electrical Power, TASK 24-22-00-860-812.
SUBTASK 21-27-00-860-372

 ALL
