21-27-00-720-802Equipment Cooling - Functional TestPDF p. 519
5. Equipment Cooling - Functional Test
(Figure 502)
A. General
(1) This task does a functional test of the equipment cooling. The exhaust cooling system
pressures (measured in inches of water) are recorded at different locations. This test will find
the minimum static pressure for the test ports.
B. Tools/Equipment
NOTE: When more than one tool part number is listed under the same "Reference" number, the
tools shown are alternates to each other within the same airplane series. Tool part numbers
that are replaced or non-procurable are preceded by "Opt:", which stands for Optional.
Reference Description
COM-4917 Fitting - Hose, Barbed Brass
Part #: 707002-0202 Supplier: 25795
COM-10778 Meter - Pressure/Vacuum
Part #: 220-2PSI Supplier: 0UJL0
COM-11876 Static pressure probe - 1/8 inch diameter
Part #: A-302 Supplier: 85274
SPL-11929 Probe - Needle, E/E Cooling
Part #: B21006-1 Supplier: 81205
STD-11875 1/8 inch ID plastic tubing
C. Location Zones
Zone Area
117 Electrical and Electronics Compartment - Left
118 Electrical and Electronics Compartment - Right
211 Flight Compartment - Left
212 Flight Compartment - Right
D. Access Panels
Number Name/Location
117A Electronic Equipment Access Door

F. Equipment Cooling - Functional Test
SUBTASK 21-27-00-700-005
(1) Before you do the test:
(a) Make sure that there are no missing electrical boxes from the equipment bay racks.
(b) Make sure that all empty locations on the equipment bay racks have blanking plugs
installed.
SUBTASK 21-27-00-780-001
(2) Measure the exhaust cooling system pressures at the locations shown in the table below:
(a) Make sure that the EQUIP COOLING SUPPLY switch, on the equipment cooling panel, is
in the alternate position.
(b) To measure the pressure at the P92 Power Distribution Panel (PDP) test point location,
do these steps:
1) Connect the pressure/vacuum meter, COM-10778 to the needle probe, SPL-11929.
2) Put the needle probe, SPL-11929, through the flex hose located below the PDP to a
depth of approx. 1.25 in. (3.18 cm).
a) Turn the probe to get the maximum indication of the pressure
3) Use the pressure/vacuum meter, COM-10778, to record the pressure value.
(c) For other test point locations, do these steps:
1) Use the barbed brass hose fitting, COM-4917 to connect the tube, STD-11875, to
the pressure/vacuum meter, COM-10778.
2) Connect the probe, COM-11876, to the other end of the tube, STD-11875.
3) Put the probe, COM-11876, through the test port locations.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
4) Use the pressure/vacuum meter, COM-10778, to record the pressure value.
(d) For the E5-2 shelf pressure, put the probe, COM-11876, through one of the 3/8 inch
diameter plenum holes at the bottom of the shelf.

21-27-00-700-805Equipment Cooling Overboard Exhaust Valve Smoke Clearance Mode - Operational TestPDF p. 533
9. Equipment Cooling Overboard Exhaust Valve Smoke Clearance Mode - Operational Test
(Figure 501)
A. General
(1) This task does a test of the equipment cooling overboard exhaust valve in the smoke removal
mode.
(2) When persons are in the airplane during this test, they must be in good physical condition.
When a person feels pain during a pressure change, you must make the pressure stable
immediately or it must be lowered. Do this until the person can make the pressure equal in
their ears, or be removed from the airplane.
B. References
Reference Title
21-00-00-800-804 Remove Conditioned Air Supplied by a Cooling Pack (P/B 201)
24-22-00-860-811 Supply Electrical Power (P/B 201)
24-22-00-860-812 Remove Electrical Power (P/B 201)
27-51-00-860-803 Extend the Trailing Edge Flaps (P/B 201)
27-51-00-860-804 Retract the Trailing Edge Flaps (P/B 201)
32-09-00-860-801 Put the Airplane in the Air Mode (P/B 201)
32-09-00-860-802 Return the Airplane to the Ground Mode (P/B 201)
36-00-00-860-801 Supply Pressure to the Pneumatic System (Selection) (P/B 201)

Zone Area
118 Electrical and Electronics Compartment - Right
212 Flight Compartment - Right
D. Procedure
SUBTASK 21-27-00-860-044
(1) Do this task: Supply Electrical Power, TASK 24-22-00-860-811.
SUBTASK 21-27-00-860-215
(2) Extend the trailing edge flaps to position 1. To extend the flaps, do this task: Extend the Trailing
Edge Flaps, TASK 27-51-00-860-803.
SUBTASK 21-27-00-860-082
WARNING
OBEY THE PROCEDURE THAT PUTS THE AIRPLANE IN THE AIR MODE. IF
YOU DO THE PROCEDURE INCORRECTLY, INJURIES TO PERSONNEL, AND
DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR.
(3) Do this task: Put the Airplane in the Air Mode, TASK 32-09-00-860-801.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
SUBTASK 21-27-00-860-045
WARNING
MAKE SURE YOU OBEY THE PROPER PROCEDURES FOR COMPRESSION
AND DECOMPRESSION WHEN YOU USE PERSONS IN A PRESSURIZED
AREA. PRESSURE CHANGES THAT CAUSE PAIN MUST NOT BE DONE. IF
YOU DO NOT OBEY THE PRECAUTIONS, INJURY TO PERSONS CAN
OCCUR.
(4) Do these steps to pressurize the airplane cabin to 2.0 Psi (13.79 kPa) differential pressure:
(a) Close all exterior doors.
(b) Make sure that the flight compartment sliding windows are closed.
(c) Do this task: Supply Pressure to the Pneumatic System (Selection),
TASK 36-00-00-860-801.
(d) Set the L PACK and R PACK switches on the P5-10 air conditioning panel to the AUTO
position.
(e) Set the R RECIRC FAN switch on the P5-10 air conditioning panel to the AUTO position.
(f) Set the CONT CAB, FWD CAB and AFT CAB temperature selectors on the P5-17 cabin
temperature control panel to the AUTO position.
(g) Put the Cabin Pressurization Switch on the Cabin Pressure Control Panel to the MAN
position.
(h) Begin to close the cabin pressurization outflow valve with the cabin pressurization valve
OPEN and CLOSE switch on the Cabin Pressure Control Panel:
1) Look at the VALVE position indicator to see the position of the valve.
WARNING
DO NOT ALLOW THE INDICATION ON THE CABIN CLIMB GAUGE TO
SHOW MORE THAN 1000 FEET PER MINUTE. WHEN YOU ALLOW A
RATE OF CABIN CLIMB OF MORE THAN 1000 FEET PER MINUTE,
DAMAGE TO THE AIRPLANE STRUCTURE OR INJURY TO PERSONNEL
CAN OCCUR.
(i) Slowly increase the cabin pressure with the OPEN/CLOSE toggle switch on the P5-6
panel so that the indication on the CABIN CLIMB gauge shows a rate of approximately
300 feet per minute.
1) Do not change the cabin pressure at a rate of more than 1000 feet per minute.
(j) Increase the cabin pressure until the cabin DIFF PRESS indicator on the Cabin Pressure
Control Panel shows a differential pressure of 2.0 psi (13.79 kPa).
SUBTASK 21-27-00-860-083
(5) Make sure that the L PACK and R PACK switches on the P5-10 Air Conditioning Panel are in
the AUTO position.
SUBTASK 21-27-00-860-084
(6) Make sure that the R RECIRC FAN switch, on the P5-10 Air Conditioning Panel, is in the
AUTO position.
SUBTASK 21-27-00-710-020
(7) Make sure that there is no air flow out of the equipment cooling overboard exhaust valve port:
(a) Put your hand at the valve exhaust port on the bottom of the airplane to feel for airflow.
NOTE: The exhaust port is just aft of the E/E bay access door.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
SUBTASK 21-27-00-860-096
WARNING
DO NOT ALLOW THE INDICATION ON THE CABIN CLIMB GAUGE TO SHOW
MORE THAN 1000 FEET PER MINUTE. WHEN YOU ALLOW A RATE OF
CABIN CLIMB OF MORE THAN 1000 FEET PER MINUTE, DAMAGE TO THE
AIRPLANE STRUCTURE OR INJURY TO PERSONNEL CAN OCCUR.
(8) Put the L PACK switch to HIGH.
NOTE: The cabin pressure can increase at more than 1000 feet per minute when the pack is
in the high flow mode. Manually opening the outflow valve will reduce the rate of cabin
pressurization.
(a) If necessary, operate the OPEN-CLOSE toggle switch on the P5-6 pressurization control
panel so that the CABIN CLIMB indication on the P5-16 cabin altitude and rate of climb
panel does not exceed 1000 feet per minute.
SUBTASK 21-27-00-860-181
(9) Put the R PACK switch to OFF.
SUBTASK 21-27-00-860-170
(10) Put the R RECIRC FAN switch to the OFF position.
SUBTASK 21-27-00-710-025
(11) Make sure that there is air flow out of the equipment cooling overboard exhaust valve port.
NOTE: The CABIN CLIMB indication on the P5-16 cabin altitude and rate of climb panel will
indicate that the cabin pressure is climbing.
SUBTASK 21-27-00-860-182
WARNING
DO NOT ALLOW THE INDICATION ON THE CABIN CLIMB GAUGE TO SHOW
MORE THAN 1000 FEET PER MINUTE. WHEN YOU ALLOW A RATE OF
CABIN CLIMB OF MORE THAN 1000 FEET PER MINUTE, DAMAGE TO THE
AIRPLANE STRUCTURE OR INJURY TO PERSONNEL CAN OCCUR.
(12) Put the R PACK switch to HIGH.
NOTE: The cabin pressure can increase at more than 1000 feet per minute when the pack is
in the high flow mode. Manually opening the outflow valve will reduce the rate of cabin
pressurization.
(a) If necessary, operate the MANUAL OPEN-CLOSE switch on the P5-6 pressurization
control panel so that the CABIN CLIMB indication on the P5-16 cabin altitude and rate of
climb panel does not exceed 1000 feet per minute.
SUBTASK 21-27-00-860-183
(13) Put the L PACK switch to OFF.
SUBTASK 21-27-00-710-040
(14) Make sure that there is airflow out of the equipment cooling overboard exhaust valve port.
NOTE: The CABIN CLIMB indication on the P5-16 cabin altitude and rate of climb panel will
indicate that the cabin pressure is climbing.
E. Put the Airplane Back to its Usual Condition
SUBTASK 21-27-00-860-050
(1) Put these switches to the AUTO position:
(a) L PACK
(b) R PACK
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(c) R RECIRC FAN
SUBTASK 21-27-00-860-051
(2) Slowly open the outflow valve to decrease the cabin pressure until the cabin DIFF PRESS
indicator shows a differential pressure of 0 psi.
SUBTASK 21-27-00-860-052
(3) Put the Cabin Pressurization Switch to the AUTO position.
SUBTASK 21-27-00-866-001
(4) Retract the trailing edge flaps to the full up position. To retract the flaps, do this task: Retract

(6) Do this task: Remove Conditioned Air Supplied by a Cooling Pack, TASK 21-00-00-800-804.

Remove Electrical Power, TASK 24-22-00-860-812.
21-27-00-700-807Smoke Clearance Mode - Operational TestPDF p. 536
10. Smoke Clearance Mode - Operational Test
NOTE: This procedure is a scheduled maintenance task.
A. General
(1) This task does an operational test of the equipment cooling overboard exhaust valve. The
interfaces of the exhaust fans, supply fans, recirculation fans, and smoke detection system
with the overboard exhaust valve system are also tested.
(2) The equipment cooling overboard exhaust valve will be referred to by the acronym OEV in this
test.
 043, 044, 083-103, 111-114, 121-129, 131, 132, 135, 138-169, 174-179, 182-187, 189-203, 205-209, 212-220,
223, 224, 231-236, 239-298, 301-304, 306, 308, 315-317, 322-341, 343, 346-999;  006, 007, 013, 014, 018-020,
056-063, 067-078, 081 POST SB 737-26A1122
(3) In the event of a forward cargo fire, the cargo smoke detectors will detect smoke and
annunciate to the flight crew of the forward cargo fire. The flight crew will then take the
appropriate action for smoke clearance from the flight deck which results in the following:
(a) Power to the E/E cooling supply normal and alternate fans is removed for 5 minutes
(b) The E/E cooling supply low flow sensor warning is inhibited for 5 minutes
(c) The OEV opens to the SMOKE position for the duration of the flight
(d) Power to the E/E cooling exhaust normal and alternate fans is removed for the duration
of the flight
(e) The E/E cooling exhaust low flow sensor warning is inhibited for the duration of the flight.
 ALL

E. Operational Test Requirements
SUBTASK 21-27-00-860-377
(1) If the operational test is not satisfactory, do a system fault isolation as follows:
(a) For the left or right recirculating fan, refer to FIM 21-25 TASK 802.
(b) For the alternate exhaust fan, M99, refer to FIM 21-27 TASK 805.
(c) For the normal exhaust fan, M98, see: FIM 21-27 TASK 806.
(d) For the alternate supply fan, M1323, refer to FIM 21-27 TASK 807.
(e) For the normal supply fan, M1322, refer to FIM 21-27 TASK 808.
(f) For the OEV, refer to FIM 21-27 TASK 809.
 043, 044, 083-103, 111-114, 121-129, 131, 132, 135, 138-169, 174-179, 182-187, 189-203,
205-209, 212-220, 223, 224, 231-236, 239-298, 301-304, 306, 308, 315-317, 322-341, 343, 346-999;
 006, 007, 013, 014, 018-020, 056-063, 067-078, 081 POST SB 737-26A1122
(g) If the supply fans do not shut off when commanded, refer to FIM 21-27 TASK 810.
(h) If the exhaust fans do not shut off when commanded, refer to FIM 21-27 TASK 811.

2. Equipment Cooling Air Filter Removal
(Figure 401)
NOTE: This procedure is a scheduled maintenance task.
A. General
(1) You must remove electrical power from the airplane before you remove an equipment cooling
air filter. This will make sure the electrical/electronic equipment does not receive electrical
power when the equipment cooling system is not in operation.
B. References
Reference Title

EN149 Class FFP2, or Better)

STD-6439 Coveralls - Hooded

F. Prepare for the Removal
SUBTASK 21-27-01-860-001
CAUTION
MAKE SURE YOU REMOVE ELECTRICAL POWER FROM THE AIRPLANE. IF
YOU SUPPLY ELECTRICAL POWER TO THE ELECTRICAL/ELECTRONIC
EQUIPMENT WHEN THE EQUIPMENT COOLING SYSTEM IS NOT IN
OPERATION, THE ELECTRICAL/ELECTRONIC EQUIPMENT CAN BECOME
TOO HOT. THIS CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE ELECTRICAL/ELECTRONIC
EQUIPMENT.
(1) Do this task: Remove Electrical Power, TASK 24-22-00-860-812.
SUBTASK 21-27-01-010-001
(2) Open the forward cargo compartment door (Open the Cargo Door, TASK 52-31-00-580-801).
SUBTASK 21-27-01-010-002
(3) Remove the forward right bulkhead liner in the forward cargo compartment. To remove the
liner, do this task: Forward Cargo Compartment Forward Bulkhead Liner - Removal,
TASK 25-52-16-000-801.
SUBTASK 21-27-01-940-001
WARNING
PUT ON THE PERSONAL PROTECTIVE EQUIPMENT BEFORE YOU TOUCH
THE FILTER. THE FILTER REMOVES SMALL PARTICLES (SMOKE, DUST,
LINT, FIBERS, POLLEN) AND INFECTIOUS MATERIALS (BACTERIA,
VIRUSES, MOLD SPORES, FUNGI) FROM THE AIR WHICH CAN CAUSE
ILLNESSES AND INJURIES TO PERSONS.
(4) Before you touch the equipment cooling air filter [2] put on the following personal protective
equipment listed below:
(a) hooded coveralls, STD-6439
(b) safety goggles, STD-6437
(c) particulate respirator, STD-6435
(d) protective gloves, G50140
SUBTASK 21-27-01-500-001
(5) Select a plastic bag, G00624 larger than the filer and tape suitable for sealing the bag closed.
G. Equipment Cooling Air Filter Removal
SUBTASK 21-27-01-010-003
(1) If it is necessary, close the forward cargo compartment door (TASK 52-31-00-580-802).
NOTE: The forward cargo compartment door can be lowered to provide access to remove the
equipment cooling air filter.
SUBTASK 21-27-01-020-001
(2) Release the latch assemblies [3] that are on the top and the bottom of the filter housing
assembly [1].
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
SUBTASK 21-27-01-020-002
WARNING
DO NOT LET THE FILTER TOUCH YOUR SKIN. DO NOT SHAKE OR HIT THE
FILTER. DO NOT LET THE FILTER FALL. DO NOT USE COMPRESSED AIR
TO CLEAN THE FILTER OR FILTER HOUSING. THIS CAN CAUSE THE
INFECTIOUS MATERIAL TO BECOME AIRBORNE. DISCARD THE FILTER IN
A PLASTIC DISPOSAL BAG. OBEY THESE INSTRUCTIONS TO PREVENT
INJURIES TO PERSONNEL.
(3) If possible, slide the plastic bag, G00624, over the filter when removing the equipment cooling
air filter [2] from the filter housing assembly [1] to minimize contamination. Seal the bag closed
with tape.
SUBTASK 21-27-01-800-001
WARNING
OBEY THE AIRLINE POLICY, LOCAL HEALTH DEPARTMENT, AND LAW
ENFORCEMENT REGULATIONS WHEN YOU DISCARD THIS MATERIAL.
OBEY THESE INSTRUCTIONS TO PREVENT INJURIES TO PERSONNEL.
(4) Discard the bag with the filter. Refer to the airline, local, health, safety and regulatory
procedures for disposal of material.
SUBTASK 21-27-01-010-004
(5) If necessary, open the forward cargo compartment door (Open the Cargo Door,
TASK 52-31-00-580-801).
H. Post-Filter Removal Cleanup
SUBTASK 21-27-01-670-002
WARNING
ISOPROPYL ALCOHOL IS POISONOUS AND FLAMMABLE. USE
PROTECTION EQUIPMENT. MAKE SURE THAT YOU USE ISOPROPYL
ALCOHOL IN AN AREA WITH AIRFLOW. IF YOU DO NOT OBEY, INJURY TO
PERSONNEL CAN OCCUR.
(1) Disinfect hard non-porous surfaces near the filter with a solution of 70% alcohol, B00130, or
Calla 1452 cleaner, B50280, or Matrix #3 cleaner, B50364.
NOTE: Follow the disinfectant manufacturer's instruction and refer to the Environmental
Protection Agency (EPA) List N for applicable contact/dwell time.
NOTE: Refer to the EPA List N or local health authority guidance for required contact/dwell
time for Isopropyl Alcohol to be used as a disinfectant.
SUBTASK 21-27-01-670-001
(2) Disinfect all tools used for filter replacement. Refer to the airline procedure and policies for the
disinfecting of tools.
SUBTASK 21-27-01-020-005
WARNING
DISCARD ALL PERSONAL PROTECTIVE EQUIPMENT AFTER YOU USE IT
ONE TIME. DO NOT TRY TO CLEAN IT. DISCARD THE EQUIPMENT IN A
PLASTIC DISPOSAL BAG. OBEY THESE INSTRUCTIONS TO PREVENT
INJURIES TO PERSONNEL.
(3) Remove the personal protective equipment and put them in a plastic bag, G00624. Seal the
bag closed with tape.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
WARNING
OBEY THE AIRLINE POLICY, LOCAL HEALTH DEPARTMENT, AND LAW
ENFORCEMENT REGULATIONS WHEN YOU DISCARD THIS MATERIAL.
OBEY THESE INSTRUCTIONS TO PREVENT INJURIES TO
PERSONNEL.
(a) Discard the bag with the personal protective equipment. Refer to the airline, local health,
safety and regulatory procedures for disposal of material.
SUBTASK 21-27-01-110-001
WARNING
CLEAN YOUR HANDS WITH SOAP AND FLUSH WITH HOT WATER. DIRTY
HANDS WITH CONTAMINATION CAN CAUSE DISEASE AND ILLNESSES TO
PERSONS.
(4) Clean your hands with soap and running hot water.

(b) Make sure that the normal fan operates.

(c) Examine the fan connections for leaks.

SUBTASK 21-27-02-710-002

NOTE: Put your hand on the fan to feel that it operates.
(c) Examine the fan connections for leaks.
NOTE: If you find a leak you must repair it.

 ALL

G. Equipment Cooling Exhaust Fan Installation
SUBTASK 21-27-04-420-001
(1) Put the equipment cooling exhaust fan [1] and sleeves [8] in their positions.
(a) Make sure that the AIRFLOW arrow on the equipment cooling exhaust fan [1] is pointed
to the inboard direction.
(b) Make sure that the fan impeller is aft of the fan check valve flappers so that the flow of air
is in the correct direction.
(c) Make sure that the electrical connector is oriented the same it was on the removed
equipment cooling exhaust fan [1].
SUBTASK 21-27-04-420-002
(2) Install the clamps [7] and tighten to 20 in-lb (2.3 N·m) - 25 in-lb (2.8 N·m).
SUBTASK 21-27-04-420-003
(3) For the normal equipment cooling exhaust fan [1], do these steps:
(a) Use cotton wiper, G00034, moist in solvent, B00184, or alcohol, B00130, to clean the
mating surfaces of the equipment cooling exhaust fan [1], washers [3], bonding
jumper [4], and bonding jumper [9].
(b) Install the screw [2], washers [3], bonding jumper [4], bonding jumper [9], and nut [5].
(c) Tighten the nut [5] to 32 in-lb (3.6 N·m) - 38 in-lb (4.3 N·m).
(d) Measure the electrical bonding resistance between the bonding jumper [4], bonding
jumper [9], and airplane structure (SWPM 20-20-00).
1) Use an intrinsically safe approved bonding meter, COM-1550.
2) Make sure that the electrical bonding resistance is 0.01 ohm (10.0 milliohm) or less.
SUBTASK 21-27-04-420-009
(4) For the alternate equipment cooling exhaust fan [1], do these steps:
(a) Use cotton wiper, G00034, moist in solvent, B00184, or alcohol, B00130, to clean the
mating surfaces of the equipment cooling exhaust fan [1], washers [3], and bonding
jumper [4].
(b) Install the screw [2], washers [3], bonding jumper [4], and nut [5].
(c) Tighten the nut [5] to 32 in-lb (3.6 N·m) - 38 in-lb (4.3 N·m).
(d) Measure the electrical bonding resistance between the bonding jumper [4] and airplane
structure (SWPM 20-20-00).
1) Use an intrinsically safe approved bonding meter, COM-1550.
2) Make sure that the electrical bonding resistance is 0.01 ohm (10.0 milliohm) or less.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
SUBTASK 21-27-04-420-004
(5) Connect the electrical connector [6] to the applicable equipment cooling exhaust fan [1].
NOTE: If identifying location decals are on the equipment cooling exhaust fan, carefully
remove the marker and relocate to ducting nearby to each location per approved
standard maintenance practices (TASK 20-30-11-910-801).
(a) Make sure that the clearance between the electrical connectors [6] wiring and alternate
equipment cooling exhaust fan [1] is 0.25 in. (6 mm) or more.
1) If the clearance is less than 0.25 in. (6 mm), do the following steps:
a) Loosen the clamps [7] for the alternate equipment cooling exhaust fan [1].
b) Slightly rotate the alternate equipment cooling exhaust fan [1] axially to
provide clearance of 0.25 in. (6 mm) or more.
c) Tighten the clamps [7] to 20 in-lb (2.3 N·m) - 25 in-lb (2.8 N·m).
H. Equipment Cooling Exhaust Fan Installation Test
SUBTASK 21-27-04-860-002
(1) Do this task: Supply Electrical Power, TASK 24-22-00-860-811.
SUBTASK 21-27-04-710-001
(2) Do these steps if you installed the normal equipment cooling exhaust fan [1]:
(a) Make sure that the EQUIP COOLING EXHAUST switch, on the equipment cooling panel,
is in the NORM position.
(b) Make sure that the normal equipment cooling exhaust fan [1] operates.
NOTE: You can put your hand on the fan to feel that it operates.
(c) Examine the fan connections for leaks.
1) If a leak is found, repair it.
SUBTASK 21-27-04-710-002
(3) Do these steps if you installed the alternate equipment cooling exhaust fan [1]:
(a) Make sure that the EQUIP COOLING EXHAUST switch, on the equipment cooling panel,
is in the ALTN position.
(b) Make sure that the alternate equipment cooling exhaust fan [1] operates.
NOTE: You can put your hand on the fan to feel that it operates.
(c) Examine the fan connections for leaks.
1) If a leak is found, repair it.
(d) Put the EQUIP COOLING EXHAUST switch, on the equipment cooling panel, to the
NORM position.

2. Equipment Cooling Exhaust Fan Cleaning
Figure 21-27-04-990-801
A. General
(1) The equipment cooling exhaust fans may not operate correctly if they are dirty.
(2) This procedure cleans only the impellers of the equipment cooling exhaust fans and the air
passages.
(3) You must do an overhaul of the equipment cooling exhaust fans if it is necessary to
disassemble them for a more thorough cleaning.
(4) This procedure is applicable for all of the fans in the equipment cooling system.
B. References

B00074 Solvent - Degreasing MIL-PRF-680

E. Preparation for Cleaning
SUBTASK 21-27-04-020-005
(1) Remove the equipment cooling exhaust fan by following this procedure:
(a) Equipment Cooling Exhaust Fan Removal, TASK 21-27-04-000-801
SUBTASK 21-27-04-930-001
(2) Make marks on the impellers so you can reinstall them in the same position they were in when
you removed them.
SUBTASK 21-27-04-030-001
(3) Remove the nut and washer at each impeller.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
SUBTASK 21-27-04-020-006
(4) Move the impeller from side to side to remove it from the rotor shaft.
NOTE: You can lightly hit the rotor shaft with a rubber mallet while you pull on the impeller to
make it easy to remove.
F. Cleaning the Equipment Cooling Exhaust Fan
SUBTASK 21-27-04-160-001
(1) Soak the impellers in Brulin Formula 815MX cleaner, B00039 or solvent, B00074 until
contamination loosens.
NOTE: Use the solvent, B00074 if the Brulin Formula 815MX cleaner, B00039 does not
completely clean the impellers.
SUBTASK 21-27-04-160-002
(2) Remove the contamination with a soft bristle brush, STD-123.
SUBTASK 21-27-04-160-003
CAUTION
MAKE SURE TO DRY THE MOTOR FULLY WITH WARM AIR OR IN AN OVEN
IF WATER GETS IN IT. IF THE MOTOR IS NOT FULLY DRIED BEFORE IT
OPERATES, DAMAGE CAN OCCUR.
(3) Flush the impellers fully with clean water if you used Brulin Formula 815MX cleaner, B00039.
SUBTASK 21-27-04-160-004
(4) Dry the impellers with a soft cloth or with dry, compressed air.
SUBTASK 21-27-04-420-005
(5) Install the keys and the impellers on the motor shaft.
NOTE: Use the marks on the impellers to install them.
SUBTASK 21-27-04-420-006
(6) Make sure the key is correctly engaged in each impeller.
SUBTASK 21-27-04-420-007
(7) Install the washer and the self-locking nut.
(a) Torque the nut to 40 in-lb (5 N·m) to 50 in-lb (6 N·m).
SUBTASK 21-27-04-420-008
(8) Install the equipment cooling exhaust fan by following this procedure:
(a) Equipment Cooling Exhaust Fan Installation, TASK 21-27-04-400-801

SUBTASK 21-31-00-860-003
CAUTION
MAKE SURE ONE OF THE EXTERNALS DOORS OR WINDOWS IS OPEN
BEFORE YOU CONTINUE WITH THE TEST. UNCONTROLLED
PRESSURIZATION OF THE CABIN CAN OCCUR WHEN THE OUTFLOW
VALVE IS CLOSED. THIS CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT.
(1) Make sure at least one exterior door or window is open or that the L and R PACK switches on
the P5 forward overhead panel are in the OFF position.
SUBTASK 21-31-00-860-004
(2) Set the mode selector switch on the P5-6 cabin pressure control module to the MAN position.
SUBTASK 21-31-00-710-001
(3) Make sure the MANUAL light on the P5-10 air conditioning module comes on.
SUBTASK 21-31-00-860-005
(4) Set the LIGHTS switch on the P2 center instrument panel to DIM.
SUBTASK 21-31-00-710-002
(5) Make sure the MANUAL light becomes dim.
SUBTASK 21-31-00-860-006
(6) Set the LIGHTS switch on the P2 center instrument panel to BRT.
SUBTASK 21-31-00-710-003
(7) Make sure the MANUAL light becomes bright.
SUBTASK 21-31-00-710-004
(8) Push and hold the CLOSE/OPEN toggle switch on the pressure control module to the CLOSE
position until the outflow valve is fully closed.
SUBTASK 21-31-00-710-005
(9) Make sure the outflow valve is fully closed.
SUBTASK 21-31-00-710-006
(10) Make sure the needle on the position indicator gage for the outflow valve is within
approximately two needle widths of the fully closed mark.
SUBTASK 21-31-00-710-007

position until the outflow valve is fully open.
SUBTASK 21-31-00-710-008
(12) Make sure the outflow valve is fully open.
SUBTASK 21-31-00-710-009

approximately two needle widths of the fully open mark.

 ALL

switches, on the P5 forward overhead panel, are OFF.

message:

GROUND TEST

DISPLAY TEST

message:

SYSTEM TEST

Table 504/21-31-00-993-804
DOORS OPEN?

 ALL

Row Col Number Name

E. Test the FLT ALT and LAND ALT Displays
SUBTASK 21-31-00-700-005
(1) Do these checks of the LCD segment displays on the cabin pressure control module:
(a) Do this task: Master Dim and Test - Operational Test, TASK 33-18-00-710-802.
(b) Make sure that all of the LCD segments (all eights) on the LAND ALT and FLT ALT
displays come on for two seconds and then go off for one second again and again.
SUBTASK 21-31-00-700-004
(2) Do a check of the cabin pressure control module LCD lighting:
(a) Rotate the PANEL light control knob on the upper center section of the P5 forward
overhead panel to the maximum BRIGHT position (fully clockwise).
(b) Make sure that both the FLT ALT and LAND ALT displays increase in intensity.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(c) Rotate the PANEL light control knob to the minimum BRIGHT position (fully
counterclockwise).
(d) Make sure that both the FLT ALT and LAND ALT displays decrease in intensity.
SUBTASK 21-31-00-700-003
(3) Do this check of the displays of the altitude range settings in the FLT ALT and LAND ALT
windows:
(a) Set altitudes in the FLT ALT window from -1000 to 42000.
(b) Make sure that all the digits are complete and clearly visible at each selection.
(c) Set altitudes in the LAND ALT window from -1000 to 14000.

(4) Visually inspect the installed copper tape on the cabin pressure controller to determine if any of
these conditions exist:
(a) Abrasions to the copper tape at the corners of the front cover
(b) Splitting/tearing of the copper tape at these locations:
1) Along the edges of the front cover at the juncture with the side covers
2) At the four corners of the front cover.
(c) Disbonding/peeling of the copper tape away from the controller front cover
(d) If any of the above conditions exist, replace all of the copper tape.
SUBTASK 21-31-01-420-004
(5) Replace damaged copper tape as follows:
(a) Remove all the installed tape.
(b) Clean the surfaces to be taped as follows:
1) Use a cotton wiper, G00034 that is moist with solvent, B00062 or Limonene solvent,
B00634 to clean the surface of tape residue.
2) Use a cotton wiper, G00034 to remove all traces of solvent from the surfaces to be
taped until the surfaces are dry.
(c) Install the 1-inch wide 3M 1181 copper foil tape, G50630 to the controller front cover and
the interfacing controller sides as shown on Figure 401 or Figure 402 :
1) Make sure the tape overlaps the front cover of the controller a minimum of 1.5 mm
and a maximum of 2.2 mm with the remainder of the tape applied to the sides of the
controller.
2) Make sure the tape blocks all optical openings into the controller where the
controller front cover interfaces with the sides of the controller.
3) Apply multiple layers of tape as necessary to make sure all openings into the
controller are blocked:
a) Make sure that all openings at the front cover corners are blocked.
4) Do not cover the BITE instruction label.
SUBTASK 21-31-01-410-002

SUBTASK 21-31-03-020-008
(1) Use care not to damage the antiskating foil on the forward and aft gates of the outflow valve
when you reach through the opening of the valve to disconnect electrical connectors or other
components (Figure 402).
NOTE: The purpose of the antiskating foil is to help reduce any noise made by the air as it
passes through the valve.
 ALL
SUBTASK 21-31-03-020-001
(2) Disconnect these electrical connectors from the aft outflow valve [1]:
NOTE: You can access the connectors through the valve door opening.
(a) ELACT 1 electrical connector [3]
(b) ELACT 2 electrical connector [2]
(c) feedback module connector 1 [5]
(d) feedback module connector 2 [6].
SUBTASK 21-31-03-020-002
(3) Remove the nut [7] and washer [8] that attach the bonding jumper [9] to the aft outflow
valve [1].
SUBTASK 21-31-03-020-003
(4) Disconnect the bonding jumper [9] from the aft outflow valve [1].
SUBTASK 21-31-03-020-010
(5) Loosen the three aft screws [12] until the three aft lugs [11] can be turned.
SUBTASK 21-31-03-020-009
(6) Turn the three aft lugs [11] so that they face inboard-to-outboard.
SUBTASK 21-31-03-860-002
WARNING
DO NOT PUT YOUR HANDS OR TOOLS IN THE OUTFLOW VALVE WHEN
THE VALVE IS IN OPERATION. IF YOU PUT YOUR HANDS OR TOOLS IN
THE OUTFLOW VALVE WHEN IT OPERATES YOU CAN CAUSE INJURY TO
PERSONS OR DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT.
(7) Do these steps to position the aft outflow valve [1] gates so that the valve can be moved
through the fuselage opening:
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(a) Close this circuit breaker:
F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-4
Row Col Number Name
F 6 C01269 PRESSURIZATION CONTROL MANUAL
(b) Put the mode select switch on the cabin pressure control module, on the P5 overhead
panel, to the MAN position.
(c) Position the aft outflow valve [1] as follows:
1) Use the service interphone system to make sure that there is communication
between the technician at the aft outflow valve location and the technician in the
flight deck.
2) Push and hold the CLOSE/OPEN toggle switch, on the P5-6 pressure control
module, to the CLOSE position until the technician at the aft outflow valve location
states that the valve is approximately in the specified position (View B-B,
Figure 401).
SUBTASK 21-31-03-860-003
(8) Open this circuit breaker and install safety tag:
F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-4
Row Col Number Name
F 6 C01269 PRESSURIZATION CONTROL MANUAL
SUBTASK 21-31-03-020-004
(9) Do these steps to remove the aft outflow valve [1]:
CAUTION
DO NOT APPLY TOO MUCH FORCE TO FORWARD ROW SCREWS AT
THE AFT OUTFLOW VALVE AFTER THEY STOPPED. TOO MUCH
FORCE APPLIED CAN CAUSE ROTATION OF THE LATCH LUGS. IF YOU
DO NOT OBEY, DAMAGE TO THE AIRCRAFT STRUCTURE CAN OCCUR.
(a) Turn the forward three screws [12] in the counterclockwise direction until they stop to
release forward lugs [11] without their rotation.
(b) Slowly push up and aft against the aft end of the aft outflow valve [1].
(c) Turn the aft outflow valve [1] as necessary until you can get to the manual motor
electrical connector [4].
(d) Disconnect the manual motor electrical connector [4].
(e) Lift and turn the aft outflow valve [1] so that it is diagonal to the skin opening of the
airplane and so that the valve motors are up.
(f) Carefully remove the aft outflow valve [1] through the skin opening of the airplane.
NOTE: Remove the aft outflow valve such that the valve motors come out last.
(g) Remove the gasket [10].
 ALL; OUTFLOW VALVES WITH JAGGED GATES
SUBTASK 21-31-03-210-001
(10) Visually examine the condition of the antiskating foil on the forward and aft gates of the aft
outflow valve [1] as follows (Figure 402):
 ALL
(a) If the antiskating foil is missing, you may make a decision to do one of these actions:
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
1) Remove any adhesive or dirt that remains on the valve gates and not replace the
foil as the outflow valve is functionally serviceable with the antiskating foil missing.

(8) Do these steps to install the aft outflow valve [1]:
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(a) Make sure that the three aft lugs [11] are turned so they face inboard to outboard.
NOTE: The lugs will be 1/4 turn away from the installed position.
(b) Put the aft outflow valve [1] through the skin opening on the airplane so that the motors
go in first with the valve diagonal to the skin opening.
NOTE: The motors will be on the inboard side of the skin opening.
(c) Set the aft outflow valve [1] down on the inside of the airplane so that you can connect
the manual motor electrical connector [4].
(d) Connect the manual motor electrical connector [4] to the aft outflow valve [1].
(e) Install the gasket [10] in its position on the airplane skin opening with the thinner rubber
side against the airplane (down).
(f) Do these steps to put the aft outflow valve [1] in its position:
1) Put the aft outflow valve [1] above the skin opening with the motors facing inboard.
2) While you tilt the aft outflow valve [1], put the forward end of the valve under the
three forward lugs [11], then lower the aft end of the valve.
3) Turn the three aft lugs [11] 90 degrees counterclockwise so that they face aft to
forward.
(g) Tighten the screws [12] to 55 in-lb (6.2 N·m) - 65 in-lb (7.3 N·m) as follows:
1) Tighten the screws [12] no more than one turn at a time in sequence (1 thru 6) as
shown (View D, Figure 401).
2) Continue to tighten the screws [12] until all of the latches are in contact with the
valve.
3) Use a torque screwdriver, STD-10994, set at 55 in-lb (6.2 N·m) - 65 in-lb (7.3 N·m)
with a bit, COM-10996, to tighten the screws no more than 1/2 turn at a time in the
sequence shown in (View D, Figure 401).
4) Continue to tighten the screws [12] in sequence until all latch screws [12] are
tightened to 55 in-lb (6.2 N·m) - 65 in-lb (7.3 N·m).
5) If a screw [12] does not turn when the final application of torque is applied, back that
screw [12] off one turn and tighten it to the final torque value.
WARNING
DO NOT PUT YOUR HANDS OR TOOLS IN THE OUTFLOW VALVE

TOOLS IN THE OUTFLOW VALVE WHEN IT OPERATES YOU CAN
CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONS OR DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT.

D. Positive Pressure Relief Valve System Test
NOTE: This test can only be done on one relief valve at a time. Do the test on the outboard relief
valve, then do the test again on the inboard relief valve.
SUBTASK 21-32-01-730-001
WARNING
DO NOT PUT YOUR HANDS OR TOOLS IN THE OUTFLOW VALVE WHEN
THE VALVE IS IN OPERATION. IF YOU PUT YOUR HANDS OR TOOLS IN
THE OUTFLOW VALVE WHEN IT OPERATES YOU CAN CAUSE INJURY TO
PERSONS OR DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT.
(1) Do these steps to do a test of the positive pressure relief valve:
(a) Put the pressure relief valve tester, SPL-6692, on the relief valve of the fuselage.
(b) Put the locating crossbar on the pressure relief valve tester, SPL-6692, forward of the
deflector tube on the relief valve and hold the fixture in position.
NOTE: The fixture is installed to make sure that the test fixture gasket is not on the
opening in the valve.
(c) Open the air pressure regulator on the pressure relief valve tester, SPL-6692, to start the
flow of air.
(d) Adjust the air pressure regulator so that the indication on the vacuum gage increases
2.21 psi/minute (15.24 kPa/minute) until the vacuum gage shows 7.76 psig (53.50 kPa).
WARNING
MANUALLY HOLD THE TEST FIXTURE AGAINST THE FUSELAGE.
WHEN THE VALVE OPENS, IT CAN CAUSE THE TEST FIXTURE TO
FALL. INJURIES TO PERSONNEL, AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT CAN
OCCUR.
(e) When the vacuum gage shows 7.76 psig (53.50 kPa), manually hold the test fixture
against the airplane fuselage.
(f) When the vacuum gage shows 7.76 psig (53.50 kPa), adjust the air pressure regulator to
increase the vacuum in 0.05 psi (0.34 kPa) increments.
(g) Stop the increase of vacuum for 10 seconds between each increase of 0.05 psi
(0.34 kPa).
(h) Continue the intermittent vacuum increases of 0.05 psi (0.34 kPa) until the valve opens
as noted by these indications:
1) The cracking point pressure of the valve occurs when the vacuum gauge needle
stops increasing, then suddenly decreases slightly, then increases slightly again
and then stabilizes.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(i) Monitor the indication on the vacuum gage when the valve opens.
(j) Make sure that the valve opens between 8.69 psig (59.92 kPa) to 9.09 psig (62.67 kPa)
(17.70 in/Hg - 18.50 in/Hg).
(k) If the pressure relief valve cracks open at a vacuum gauge indication greater than
9.09 psig (62.67 kPa) (18.50 in/Hg), make sure that there are no leaks anywhere on the
valve test fixture.
(l) Adjust the vacuum regulator valve to increase the differential pressure to approximately
7.5 psid (51.7 kPa) - 7.0 psid (48.3 kPa) (15.04 in/Hg - 14.02 in/Hg) at a rate not more
than 2.00 psig/minute (13.79 kPa/minute) (4.07 inches Hg/minute).
1) Make sure that the relief valve closes.
NOTE: The indication that the relief valve has closed is seen on the differential
pressure gauge when the gauge stops, and then starts to increase and then
becomes stable.
(m) Adjust the air pressure regulator to reduce the indication on the vacuum gage to 0 psig (0
kPa) (0 in/Hg) at a rate of 4.0 psig/minute (27.58 kPa/minute) (8.14 inches Hg/minute) or
slower.
(n) Close the pressure regulator on the pressure relief valve tester, SPL-6692.
(o) Remove the pressure relief valve tester, SPL-6692, from the airplane.
(p) Disconnect the Regulated Dry Filtered Air Source, STD-1114, from the pressure regulator.
SUBTASK 21-32-01-730-002
(2) Do the test for the other relief valve.
SUBTASK 21-32-01-860-002
(3) Remove the safety tags and close these circuit breakers:
F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-4
Row Col Number Name
F 3 C01270 PRESSURIZATION CONTROL AUTO 1
F 5 C01271 PRESSURIZATION CONTROL AUTO 2
F 6 C01269 PRESSURIZATION CONTROL MANUAL
21-32-01-700-802Positive Pressure Relief Valve - System Test with the Use of Test EquipmentPDF p. 706
3. Positive Pressure Relief Valve - System Test with the Use of  Test Equipment
(Figure 502)
NOTE: This procedure is a scheduled maintenance task.
A. Tools/Equipment
NOTE: When more than one tool part number is listed under the same "Reference" number, the
tools shown are alternates to each other within the same airplane series. Tool part numbers
that are replaced or non-procurable are preceded by "Opt:", which stands for Optional.
Reference Description
SPL-6692 Vacuum Tank - Pressure Relief Valve Tester
Part #: A21010-203 Supplier: 81205
Part #: GS15047-1 Supplier: 99167
Opt Part #: A21010-187 Supplier: 81205
Opt Part #: A21010-188 Supplier: 81205
Opt Part #: A21010-189 Supplier: 81205
Opt Part #: A21010-190 Supplier: 81205
STD-1114 Air Source - Regulated, Dry, Filtered 0-150 PSIG with Pressure
Gauge Range 0-100 PSIG, 1 PSIG Increment, and +/-1 PSI
Minimum Accuracy
B. Location Zones
Zone Area
146 Aft Cargo Compartment Equipment Bay - Right
C. Prepare for the Test
SUBTASK 21-32-01-860-003
(1) Open these circuit breakers and install safety tags:
F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-4
Row Col Number Name
F 3 C01270 PRESSURIZATION CONTROL AUTO 1
F 5 C01271 PRESSURIZATION CONTROL AUTO 2
F 6 C01269 PRESSURIZATION CONTROL MANUAL
SUBTASK 21-32-01-210-001
(2) Make sure there is no blockage or unwanted materials at these locations:
(a) The fuselage skin in the area of the relief valve.
(b) The overboard vent tube opening in the center of each relief valve.
(c) The ambient sense tube in the fuselage pedestal mount.
D. Positive Pressure Relief Valve System Test
NOTE: This test can only be done on one relief valve at a time. Do the test on the outboard relief
valve, then do the test again on the inboard relief valve.
SUBTASK 21-32-01-480-001
WARNING
DO NOT PUT YOUR HANDS OR TOOLS IN THE OUTFLOW VALVE WHEN
THE VALVE IS IN OPERATION. IF YOU PUT YOUR HANDS OR TOOLS IN
THE OUTFLOW VALVE WHEN IT OPERATES YOU CAN CAUSE INJURY TO
PERSONS OR DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT.
(1) Do these steps to connect the pressure relief valve tester, SPL-6692, to the relief valve:
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(a) Make sure that all the valves on the pressure relief valve tester, SPL-6692, are closed.
(b) Connect the Regulated Dry Filtered Air Source, STD-1114, to the quick-disconnect
connection on the pressure relief valve tester, SPL-6692.
(c) Adjust the air control valve on the pressure relief valve tester, SPL-6692, until the
indication on the pressure gage is 70 ±10 psi (482.6 ±68.9 kPa).
(d) Adjust the vacuum regulator valve until the differential pressure is approximately 2.0 psi
(13.8 kPa) (4.07 in/Hg).
1) Turn the vacuum regulator valve counter-clockwise to increase the vacuum
(differential pressure).
NOTE: The arrow on the vacuum regulator valve indicates an increase of pressure
not vacuum.
(e) Put and hold the vacuum head assembly over the relief valve.
(f) Open the vacuum head assembly valve.
1) Make sure that the vacuum head assembly is sealed to the airplane skin.
SUBTASK 21-32-01-730-003
(2) Do these steps to find the differential pressure when the relief valve opens:
(a) Adjust the vacuum regulator valve so the indication on the vacuum rate gage does not
exceed 2.4 psi/minute (16.5 kPa/minute).
WARNING
YOU MUST HOLD THE VACUUM HEAD ASSEMBLY MANUALLY
AGAINST THE AIRPLANE FUSELAGE WHEN THE DIFFERENTIAL
PRESSURE GAGE INDICATION IS 8.25 PSID (56.88 KPA). WHEN THE
VALVE OPENS, THE VACUUM HEAD ASSEMBLY CAN FALL FROM THE
FUSELAGE SURFACE. INJURY TO PERSONNEL OR DAMAGE TO
EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR.
(b) When the differential pressure gage shows 8.25 psid (56.88 kPa), manually hold the
vacuum head assembly against the fuselage.
(c) When the differential pressure gage shows 8.25 psid (56.88 kPa), adjust the vacuum
regulator valve to increase the differential pressure in 0.05 psid (0.345 kPa) increments.
(d) Stop the increase of vacuum for 10 seconds between each increase of 0.05 psid
(0.345 kPa).
(e) Continue the intermittent vacuum increases of 0.05 psid (0.345 kPa) until the relief valve
opens.
(f) Monitor the indication on the differential pressure gage when the relief valve opens.
NOTE: The indication that the relief valve has opened is seen on the differential pressure
gage when the pressure starts to decrease.
(g) Make sure that the valve opens at a differential pressure of 8.69 psid (59.92 kPa) to
9.09 psid (62.67 kPa) (17.7 to 18.5 in/Hg).
NOTE: When the valve opens the differential pressure will decrease to near 0 psid.
(h) If the relief valve opens at a differential pressure more than 9.09 psid (62.67 kPa) (18.51
in/Hg), make sure that there are no leaks at any of the tubing connections on the vacuum
tank assembly.
(i) Adjust the vacuum regulator valve to increase the differential pressure to approximately
7.5 psig (51.71 kPa) to 7.0 psig (48.26 kPa) (15.04 to 14.02 in/Hg) at a rate not more
than 2.00 psig/minute (13.79 kPa/minute) (4.07 inches Hg/minute).
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
1) Make sure that the relief valve closes.
NOTE: The indication that the relief valve has closed is seen on the differential
pressure gage when the gage stops, and then starts to increase and then
becomes stable.
SUBTASK 21-32-01-080-001
(3) Adjust the vacuum regulator valve fully clockwise and reduce the differential pressure to 0 psig
(0.0 kPa) (0 in/Hg), at a rate of 4.0 psig/min (27.58 kPa/min) (8.14 inches Hg/min) or slower.
SUBTASK 21-32-01-080-002
(4) Close the vacuum head assembly valve and remove the vacuum head assembly.
SUBTASK 21-32-01-730-004
(5) Do the test for the other relief valve.
SUBTASK 21-32-01-860-004
(6) Remove the safety tags and close these circuit breakers:
F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-4
Row Col Number Name
F 3 C01270 PRESSURIZATION CONTROL AUTO 1
F 5 C01271 PRESSURIZATION CONTROL AUTO 2
F 6 C01269 PRESSURIZATION CONTROL MANUAL

 ALL

WARNING
PUT ON THE PERSONAL PROTECTIVE EQUIPMENT BEFORE YOU TOUCH

LINT, FIBERS, POLLEN) AND INFECTIOUS MATERIALS (BACTERIA,
VIRUSES, MOLD SPORES, FUNGI) FROM THE AIR WHICH CAN CAUSE

SUBTASK 21-32-02-020-001
(1) Remove the cover [4] from the top of the positive pressure relief valve [1].
SUBTASK 21-32-02-020-002
(2) Remove the filter [3] and packing [2] from the positive pressure relief valve [1].
SUBTASK 21-32-02-020-003
WARNING
DO NOT LET THE FILTER TOUCH YOUR SKIN. DO NOT SHAKE OR HIT THE
FILTER. DO NOT LET THE FILTER FALL. DO NOT USE COMPRESSED AIR
TO CLEAN THE FILTER OR FILTER HOUSING. THIS CAN CAUSE THE
INFECTIOUS MATERIAL TO BECOME AIRBORNE. DISCARD THE FILTER IN
A PLASTIC DISPOSAL BAG. OBEY THESE INSTRUCTIONS TO PREVENT
INJURIES TO PERSONNEL.
(3) If possible, slide the plastic bag, G00624, over the filter [3] with the packing [2] when removing
from the positive pressure relief valve [1] to minimize contamination.
(a) Seal the bag closed with tape.
WARNING
OBEY THE AIRLINE POLICY, LOCAL HEALTH DEPARTMENT, AND LAW
ENFORCEMENT REGULATIONS WHEN YOU DISCARD THIS MATERIAL.
OBEY THESE INSTRUCTIONS TO PREVENT INJURIES TO
PERSONNEL.
(b) Discard the bag with the filter.
NOTE: Refer to the airline, local health, safety and regulatory procedures for the
disposal of material.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL

SUBTASK 21-32-02-080-001
WARNING
ISOPROPYL ALCOHOL IS POISONOUS AND FLAMMABLE. USE
PROTECTION EQUIPMENT. MAKE SURE THAT YOU USE ISOPROPYL
ALCOHOL IN AN AREA WITH AIRFLOW. IF YOU DO NOT OBEY, INJURY TO

(1) Disinfect the filter cover, filter housing and exterior surfaces of the valve with alcohol, B50073.
NOTE: Refer to the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) List N or local health authority

disinfectant.
SUBTASK 21-32-02-670-001

NOTE: Refer to the airline procedure and policies for the disinfecting of tools.
SUBTASK 21-32-02-020-004
WARNING
DISCARD ALL PERSONAL PROTECTIVE EQUIPMENT AFTER YOU USE IT
ONE TIME. DO NOT TRY TO CLEAN IT. DISCARD THE EQUIPMENT IN A
PLASTIC DISPOSAL BAG. OBEY THESE INSTRUCTIONS TO PREVENT
INJURIES TO PERSONNEL.
(3) Remove the personal protective equipment and put them in a plastic bag, G00624.
(a) Seal the bag closed with tape.
WARNING
OBEY THE AIRLINE POLICY, LOCAL HEALTH DEPARTMENT, AND LAW
ENFORCEMENT REGULATIONS WHEN YOU DISCARD THIS MATERIAL.
OBEY THESE INSTRUCTIONS TO PREVENT INJURIES TO
PERSONNEL.
(b) Discard the bag with the personal protective equipment.
NOTE: Refer to the airline, local health, safety and regulatory procedures for disposal of
material.
SUBTASK 21-32-02-110-001
WARNING
CLEAN YOUR HANDS WITH SOAP AND FLUSH WITH HOT WATER. DIRTY
HANDS WITH CONTAMINATION CAN CAUSE DISEASE AND ILLNESSES TO
PERSONS.
(4) Clean your hands with soap and running hot water.

(1) Do the steps which follow to install the spring [7] on the door assembly [6]:

 ALL

21-32-03-700-801Negative Pressure Relief Valve Adjustment/TestPDF p. 724
4. Negative Pressure Relief Valve Adjustment/Test
NOTE: This procedure is a scheduled maintenance task.
A. Tools/Equipment
Reference Description
STD-753 Scale - Push/Pull, 0-25 pound (0-11 kilogram) Capacity, 1/4 pound
(113 gram) Accuracy
B. Location Zones
Zone Area
142 Aft Cargo Compartment - Right
C. Procedure
SUBTASK 21-32-03-480-001
(1) On the external surface of the airplane, hold the push/pull scale 0-25 pound (0-11 kilogram),
STD-753 against the relief valve as shown in View A-A Figure 201.
(a) Put the push/pull scale 0-25 pound (0-11 kilogram), STD-753 at approximately the center
of the relief valve door and 2.92 ±0.20 in. (74.2 ±5.1 mm) above the lower edge of the
relief valve door.
SUBTASK 21-32-03-720-002
(2) Slowly push the push/pull scale 0-25 pound (0-11 kilogram), STD-753 against the relief valve
door.
(a) Keep the push/pull scale 0-25 pound (0-11 kilogram), STD-753 at approximately a 90°
angle to the relief valve door.
SUBTASK 21-32-03-720-003
(3) Make sure the relief valve door starts to open when the push/pull scale 0-25 pound (0-11
kilogram), STD-753 shows between 4 lbf (17.8 N) and 8 lbf (35.6 N).
SUBTASK 21-32-03-720-004
(4) Continue to push the relief valve door to the full open position.
(a) Make sure the door moves smoothly without any binding.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
SUBTASK 21-32-03-720-005
(5) Make sure the push/pull scale 0-25 pound (0-11 kilogram), STD-753 shows between 8 lbf
(35.6 N) and 10.5 lbf (46.7 N) when the relief valve door is in the full open position
(Figure 202).
NOTE: The door in the full open position is a minimum of 40° from its full closed position.
NOTE: The straight-line distance is a minimum of 5.7 in. (14.5 cm) from the closed position to
open the door fully.
SUBTASK 21-32-03-720-006
(6) Slowly release the relief valve door until it is in the closed position.
SUBTASK 21-32-03-080-001
(7) Remove the push/pull scale 0-25 pound (0-11 kilogram), STD-753.

WARNING

F. Cabin Altitude Warning Switch Functional Test
SUBTASK 21-33-00-720-021
(1) Do a test of the cabin altitude warning switch, S128, as follows:
(a) Remove the screen port assembly from the cabin altitude warning switch, S128.
(b) Install an adapter fitting and matching hose on the cabin altitude warning switch, S128:
NOTE: The female threads on the cabin altitude warning switch are 7/16-20-UNJF-3A
with a full thread depth of 0.438 in. (1.113 cm) minimum. The total port depth is
0.541 in. (1.374 cm) - 0.551 in. (1.400 cm). Any mating adapter should have
threads having a full thread depth of no greater than 0.438 in. (1.113 cm) and an
overall length that is less than 0.500 in. (1.270 cm) to avoid false test results.
1) Use one of the following adapters, or equivalent adapter, and matching hose to
connect to the cabin altitude warning switch:
NOTE: Adapters are considered to be equivalent as long as the mating side with
the switch is:
• Greater than or equal to 0.265 in. (0.673 cm) X 7/16-20-UNJF-3A and
less than or equal to 0.438 in. (1.113 cm) X 7/16-20-UNJF-3A for the
flareless end, or
• Less than or equal to 0.500 in. (1.270 cm) total with greater than or equal
to 0.265 in. (0.673 cm) X 7/16-20-UNJF-3A thread for AN4 flared end.
a) SAE J514 P/N 070220 90 Degree Straight Thread Elbow and appropriate
sized O-ring (Preferred).
<1> Use a Barfield Pitot Hose, or equivalent 25 ft (7.62 m) to 40 ft (12.19 m)
long hose, with #4 AN fitting to the adapter and quick disconnect (if
applicable) to the air data test set.
<2> Make sure that the flat side of the adapter is connected with the cabin
altitude warning switch.
NOTE: Do not connect the flared side of the adapter with the cabin
altitude warning switch. Connecting the flared side of the
adapter with the cabin altitude warning switch can bottom out
the cabin altitude warning switch, resulting in false test results.
b) SAE J514 P/N 070320 45 Degree Straight Thread Elbow and appropriate
sized O-ring (Preferred).
<1> Use a Barfield Pitot Hose, or equivalent 25 ft (7.62 m) to 40 ft (12.19 m)
long hose, with #4 AN fitting to the adapter and quick disconnect (if
applicable) to the air data test set.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
<2> Make sure that the flat side of the adapter is connected with the cabin
altitude warning switch.
NOTE: Do not connect the flared side of the adapter with the cabin
altitude warning switch. Connecting the flared side of the
adapter with the cabin altitude warning switch can bottom out
the cabin altitude warning switch, resulting in false test results.
c) SAE J514 P/N 070120 Straight Thread Connector Short and appropriate sized
O-ring (Preferred).
<1> Use a Barfield Pitot Hose, or equivalent 25 ft (7.62 m) to 40 ft (12.19 m)
long hose, with #4 AN fitting to the adapter and quick disconnect (if
applicable) to the air data test set.
<2> Make sure that the flat side of the adapter is connected with the cabin
altitude warning switch.
NOTE: Do not connect the flared side of the adapter with the cabin
altitude warning switch. Connecting the flared side of the
adapter with the cabin altitude warning switch can bottom out
the cabin altitude warning switch, resulting in false test results.
d) AS21900-4 (or MS21900-4) Flareless Tube to Flared Tube Adapter and
appropriate sized O-ring (Preferred).
<1> Use a Barfield Pitot Hose, or equivalent 25 ft (7.62 m) to 40 ft (12.19 m)
long hose, with #4 AN fitting to the adapter and quick disconnect (if

the cabin altitude warning switch, resulting in false test results.
e) P/N JUD321 Hose Fitting with MS28778-4 O-ring (Eaton Aerospace LLC,
Bethel, CT 02750) (Preferred).
<1> Use a Barfield Pitot Hose, or equivalent 25 ft (7.62 m) to 40 ft (12.19 m)
long hose, with #4 AN fitting to the adapter and quick disconnect (if
applicable) to the air data test set.
f) AN807-4D (or AS5180D04 or AS5180W04) Tube to Hose Adapter, AN924-4
nut and appropriate sized O-ring (on the mating side with the switch) and
spacer or washers (Alternate).
NOTE: This adapter can be used if the steps below are carefully followed.
This adapter is not preferred because if the AN924-4 nut is not
connected carefully as recommended below, this can bottom out the
cabin altitude warning switch, resulting in false test results.
<1> Use a Barfield Pitot Hose, or equivalent 25 ft (7.62 m) to 40 ft (12.19 m)
long hose, with quick disconnect (if applicable) to the air data test set.
<2> Make sure that the thread length, including fitting end after the
installation of AN924-4 nut and appropriate sized 7/16 spacer or
washers, is less than 0.500 in. (1.270 cm) to avoid false test results.
(c) Connect the air data model test set, COM-1914, or equivalent, to the adapter fitting.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL

altimeter.

3. Check of the Cabin Rate of Climb Indicator
A. Location Zones
Zone Area
212 Flight Compartment - Right
B. Cabin Rate of Climb Indicator Check
SUBTASK 21-33-00-212-001
(1) Get access to the cabin rate of climb indicator on the P5-16 cabin pressure control panel.
SUBTASK 21-33-00-710-003
(2) Do this check of the cabin rate of climb indicator:
(a) Open one of the cabin entry doors to make sure that the cabin is not pressurized.
(b) Turn the zero adjustment screw on the lower left corner of the gauge and make sure that
the pointer can be adjusted to a minimum of 400 ft/min on both sides of the zero
graduation.
(c) Reset the pointer to zero.

Zone Area

B. Preparation Check for Removal
SUBTASK 21-33-01-710-001
(1) Do this check to determine if the cabin rate of climb indicator requires replacement:
(a) Make sure that the cabin is not pressurized.
(b) Turn the zero adjustment screw on the lower left corner of the gauge to make sure that
the pointer can be adjusted to a minimum of 400 ft/min on both sides of the zero
graduation.
(c) Reset the pointer to zero.
SUBTASK 21-33-01-000-001
(2) If the indicator cannot be adjusted as noted in the previous step, continue with the removal
procedure.
C. Cabin Rate of Climb Indicator Removal
SUBTASK 21-33-01-860-001
(1) Open this circuit breaker:
F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-3
Row Col Number Name
E 10 C00328 OVERHEAD 5V SECONDARY
SUBTASK 21-33-01-020-001
CAUTION
HOLD THE INDICATOR WHEN YOU LOOSEN THE CLAMP. THE INDICATOR
CAN FALL WHEN THE CLAMP IS LOOSE. DAMAGE CAN OCCUR TO THE
INDICATOR IF IT FALLS.
(2) Loosen the clamp tension screw [1].
(a) If necessary, loosen the clamp mount screw [5].
SUBTASK 21-33-01-020-002
(3) Carefully pull the cabin rate of climb indicator [3] out of the P5-16 panel [4].
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
SUBTASK 21-33-01-020-003
(4) Disconnect the electrical connector [2] from the cabin rate of climb indicator [3].
SUBTASK 21-33-01-480-001

E. Cabin Altitude and Differential Pressure Indicator Installation
SUBTASK 21-33-02-080-001
(1) Remove the dust cap from the cabin pressure port on the back of the indicator.
SUBTASK 21-33-02-420-003
(2) If you are installing a cabin altitude and differential pressure indicator [6] that does not have a
quick-disconnect fitting already installed, do these steps:
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(a) Put a new packing [3] on the male quick-disconnect [2].
(b) Apply anti-seize compound, D50004 to the threads of the male quick-disconnect [2].
(c) Install the male quick-disconnect [2] on the cabin altitude and differential pressure
indicator [6].
(d) Tighten the male quick-disconnect [2] to a torque of 120 (± 12) inch-pounds [13.6 (± 1.36)
Nm].
SUBTASK 21-33-02-020-009
(3) Connect the static pressure hose [4] to the quick-disconnect [2] on the cabin altitude and
differential pressure indicator [6].
SUBTASK 21-33-02-420-001
(4) Connect the electrical connector [5] to the cabin altitude and differential pressure indicator [6].
SUBTASK 21-33-02-820-001
(5) Carefully push the cabin altitude and differential pressure indicator [6] into its position in the
P5-16 panel [7].
SUBTASK 21-33-02-420-002
(6) Tighten the clamp tension screws [1] 5 to 8 pound-inches (0.6 to 0.9 newton-meters).
NOTE: Hold the indicator [6] against the panel [7] while you tighten the screws [1].
SUBTASK 21-33-02-790-001
(7) If you removed or installed the quick-disconnect fitting on the cabin altitude and differential
pressure indicator [6] at any time during this maintenance, do this task: Alternate Static System
Low-range Leak Test, TASK 34-11-00-790-808.
(a) Note that if the replacement indicator came with the quick-disconnect installed or if the
quick-disconnect was never removed from the existing indicator during this maintenance,
it is not necessary to do the task: Alternate Static System Low-range Leak Test,
TASK 34-11-00-790-808.
SUBTASK 21-33-02-860-002
(8) Close this circuit breaker:
F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-3
Row Col Number Name
E 10 C00328 OVERHEAD 5V SECONDARY
SUBTASK 21-33-02-710-001
(9) Do this check of the cabin altimeter gauge:
(a) Open one of the main entry doors to make sure that the cabin is not pressurized.
(b) Set the barometric pressure for the pilot's altimeter to 29.92 inches of Hg.
(c) Observe the altitude on the pilot's altimeter.
(d) Compare the altitude on the pilot's altimeter to the altitude on the cabin altimeter.
(e) If the altitude on the cabin altimeter is within 1000 feet of the altitude on the pilot's
altimeter, the cabin altimeter is satisfactory.
(f) If the altitude on the cabin altimeter is not within1000 feet of the altitude on the pilot's
altimeter, then do these tasks to replace the gauge: Cabin Altitude and Differential
Pressure Indicator Removal, TASK 21-33-02-000-801 and Cabin Altitude and Differential
Pressure Indicator Installation, TASK 21-33-02-400-801.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
SUBTASK 21-33-02-710-002
(10) Do this check of the cabin differential pressure gauge:
(a) Observe the differential pressure on the DIFF PRESS gauge.
(b) If the differential pressure is within 0 (± 0.2) psid, the cabin differential pressure gauge is
satisfactory.
(c) If the differential pressure is not within 0 (± 0.2) psid, then do these tasks to replace the
gauge: Cabin Altitude and Differential Pressure Indicator Removal,
TASK 21-33-02-000-801 and Cabin Altitude and Differential Pressure Indicator
Installation, TASK 21-33-02-400-801.

Figure 401
A. Location Zones
Zone Area
212 Flight Compartment - Right
B. Procedure
SUBTASK 21-33-07-000-001
(1) Get access to the electrical connectors on the back of the P5-16 cabin altimeter and rate of
climb module on the P5 forward overhead panel:
(a) Loosen the 1/4-turn fasteners that hold the P5 forward overhead panel in position and let
the panel rotate downward.

fasteners that hold the module to the P5 forward overhead panel.

E. Prepare for the Test
NOTE: The emergency exit hatch heaters have over-temperature thermostats (Figure 501). The
thermostats will turn the heaters off very shortly after they come on when the airplane is on
the ground, in the air mode, with an air conditioning pack on. The exit hatch heaters will not
operate when the temperature is more than approximately 70 ±5°F (21 ±3°C) (when the
overheat thermostat is closed) or 50 ±7°F (10 ±4°C) (when the overheat thermostat is open
due to a previous overheat condition). In warm temperatures, the heater thermostats may
need to be cooled before the heaters will operate.

21-45-01-400-801Door Area Heater InstallationPDF p. 803
3. Door Area Heater Installation
(Figure 401 or Figure 402)
A. General
(1) Some of the ducts and equipment in the air distribution system are wrapped with insulation
material. CFR 14 Part 121.312 mandates that insulation material installed in the fuselage as a
replacement after September 2, 2005 must meet the flame propagation requirements of CFR
Part 25.856, effective September 2, 2003.
(2) Existing insulation material can be removed and re-installed if it is not damaged. Replacement
insulation material must meet the flame propagation requirement.
(3) Melamine foam insulation, G50449, BMS8-385, is the preferred foam insulation material that
meets the flame propagation requirement. BMS8-385 Type 4 is the preferred foam insulation
material that meets the flame propagation requirement. BMS 8-385 Type 6 and BMS 8-300
Type VIII insulation is optional to BMS8-385 Type 4.
(4) Air conditioning ducts with polyimide foam insulation, G02470, must be wrapped with tape,
G50327, tape, G51202, or tape, G50789, to meet the flammability/flame propagation
requirements. Wrap the tape, G50327, tape, G51202, or tape, G50789, across 100% of the
brown hypalon insulation surface on polyimide foam insulation, G02470.
(5) Do not use BMS8-39 polyurethane foam insulation for repairs due to the degradation in
flammability properties over time.
(6) When insulation material is removed and re-installed, any existing tape that does not meet the
flame propagation requirement must be removed or completely covered with tape that does
meet the requirement.
(a) Tape specifications BMS 5-157, Type I, Class 1, Grade B, composition MPVF and BMS
5-157, Type I, Class 2, Grade C, composition MPEEK are qualified tapes used to secure
insulation to ducts.

G. Door Area Heater Installation
SUBTASK 21-45-01-420-011
(1) Install the forward door area heater [3] between the flex ducts as follows:
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(a) Put the forward door area heater [3] in position with the electrical connector pointed down
and the flow arrow on the heater pointed in the same direction as the flow arrow on the
support structure.
(b) Install the free ends of the forward and aft flex ducts on the forward door area heater [3]
so that the routing of the flex ducts takes up any excess duct length as follows:
1) Use large radius bends to prevent kinking or twisting of the ducts.
2) Compress the flex duct between the support clamps.
(c) Make sure the flex ducts overlap the ends of the heater duct 1.00 ±0.13 in.
(2.54 ±0.33 cm).
(d) Move the clamps [1] and clamp [5] into position 0.38 ±0.13 in. (0.97 ±0.34 cm) from the
ends of the flex ducts.
(e) Tighten the clamps [1] and clamp [5] to 16.5 ±1.5 in-lb (19.0 ±1.7 kg-cm).
SUBTASK 21-45-01-420-001
(2) Install the aft door area heater [3] between the flex ducts as follows:
(a) Put the aft door area heater [3] in position with the electrical connector pointed down and
the flow arrow on the heater pointed in the same direction as the flow arrow on the
support structure.
(b) Install the free ends of the forward and aft flex ducts on the aft door area heater [3] so
that the ends of the flex ducts overlap the heater duct by 1.25 ±0.13 in. (3.18 ±0.34 cm).
(c) Move the clamp [1] and clamp [5] into position so they are 0.38 ±0.13 in. (0.97 ±0.34 cm)
from the ends of the heater duct.
(d) Tighten the clamp [1] and clamp [5] to 16.5 ±1.5 in-lb (19.0 ±1.7 kg-cm).
SUBTASK 21-45-01-420-006
(3) Install the two clamps [1].
SUBTASK 21-45-01-420-007
(4) Connect the electrical connector [2] to the door area heater [3].
SUBTASK 21-45-01-410-001
(5) If the aft door area heater was installed, do this step:
(a) Install the wire bundle mounting plate [8], washer [7], and nut [6].

• Turbine Inlet Overheat Switch

G. Pack Flow Control Valve Operational Test
SUBTASK 21-51-00-860-008
(1) Do these steps to make sure that the left pack and right pack flow control valves are closed
with the pack switches in the OFF position:
(a) Put the L PACK switch and R PACK switch, on the P5 air conditioning panel, in the OFF
position.
(b) Make sure that the visual position indicators on the left and right flow control and shutoff
valves actuator are in the closed position.
SUBTASK 21-51-00-860-009
(2) Do these steps to make sure that the left and right flow control valves are partially open with
the pack switches in the AUTO position:
(a) Make sure that either the BLEED 1 or BLEED 2 switch, on the P5-10 air conditioning
panel, is set to the ON position.
(b) Set the CONT CAB, FWD CAB, and AFT CAB temperature selectors, on the P5-17
temperature control module, to the AUTO (12:00 o'clock) position.
(c) Put the L PACK switch and R PACK switch in the AUTO position.
(d) Make sure that the visual position indicators on the left pack and right pack flow control
and shutoff valves move to a partially open position.
NOTE: The packs will operate.
(e) Put the L PACK and R PACK switches, on the P5-10 air conditioning panel, to the OFF
position.
(f) Allow the packs to cool.
SUBTASK 21-51-00-860-010
(3) Do these steps to make sure that the left pack and right pack flow control valves are
commanded to APU high flow mode with the pack switches in the HIGH position:
(a) Disconnect the electrical connector D392, from the left flow control and shutoff valve.
(b) Connect a digital/analog multimeter, COM-1793, between connector D392, pins 1 and 2
on the ships' wiring.
(c) Put the L PACK and R PACK switches, on the P5-10 air conditioning panel, in the HIGH
positions.
(d) Make sure that there is 28 (± 5) VDC between pins 1 and 2 of connector D392.
(e) Put the L PACK and R PACK switches, on the P5-10 air conditioning panel, to the OFF
position.
(f) Allow the packs to cool.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
 006, 007, 013, 014, 018-020, 043, 044, 056-063, 067-078, 081, 083-103, 111-114, 121-129, 131, 132, 135,
138-169, 174-179, 182-187, 189-203, 205-209, 212-220, 223, 224, 231-236, 239-298, 301-304, 306, 308, 315-317,
322-341, 343, 346-384 (Continued)
(g) Disconnect the electrical connector D394, from the right pack flow control valve.
(h) Connect a digital/analog multimeter, COM-1793, between connector D394, pins 1 and 2
on the ships' wiring.
(i) Put the L PACK and R PACK switches, on the P5-10 air conditioning panel, in the HIGH
positions.
(j) Make sure that there is 28 (± 5) VDC between pins 1 and 2 of connector D394.
(k) Put the L PACK and R PACK switches, on the P5-10 air conditioning panel, in the OFF
positions.
(l) If necessary, allow the packs to cool.
(m) Re-connect the electrical connector D392, to the left flow control and shutoff valve.
(n) Re-connect the electrical connector D394, to the right flow control and shutoff valve.
SUBTASK 21-51-00-710-003
(4) Do these steps to make sure that a pack in operation will go to the high flow mode when the
other pack shuts down:
(a) Put the airplane in the air mode, do this task: Put the Airplane in the Air Mode,
TASK 32-09-00-860-801.
(b) Retract the trailing edge flaps to the fully up position, do this task: Retract the Trailing
Edge Flaps, TASK 27-51-00-860-804.
(c) Put the L PACK switch to the AUTO position.
(d) Put the R PACK switch to the OFF position.
(e) Disconnect the connector D962, from the left flow control and shutoff valve.
(f) Connect a digital/analog multimeter, COM-1793, between connector D962, pins 1 and 2.
(g) Make sure that there is 0 (± 5) VDC between connector D962, pins 1 and 2.
1) This makes sure that the left pack is in the engine high flow mode.
(h) Re-connect the connector D962, to the left flow control and shutoff valve.
(i) Put the R PACK switch to the AUTO position.
(j) Put the L PACK switch to the OFF position.
(k) Disconnect the connector D964, from the right flow control and shutoff valve.
(l) Connect a digital/analog multimeter, COM-1793, between connector D964, pins 1 and 2.
(m) Make sure that there is 0 (± 5) VDC between connector D964, pins 1 and 2.
1) This makes sure that the R PACK is in the engine high flow mode.
(n) Re-connect the connector D964, to the right flow control and shutoff valve.
SUBTASK 21-51-00-860-038
(5) Return the airplane to the ground mode, do this task: Return the Airplane to the Ground Mode,
TASK 32-09-00-860-802.
SUBTASK 21-51-00-860-039
(6) If required, extend the trailing edge flaps to the fully extended position, do this task: Extend the
Trailing Edge Flaps, TASK 27-51-00-860-803.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL

138-169, 174-179, 182-187, 189-203, 205-209, 212-220, 223, 224, 231-236, 239-298, 301-304, 306, 308, 315-317,
322-341, 343, 346-384 (Continued)

(7) Put the L PACK and R PACK switches in the OFF position.

WARNING

DUCTS CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONNEL.
(1) To remove the compressor outlet duct, do these steps:
(a) Disconnect the flex hose from the duct.
(b) Remove the electrical connector [1] from the ram air control sensor.
(c) Remove the electrical connector [4] from the compressor discharge overheat switch.
(d) Remove the ground clip [32] that hold the bonding jumper [33] to the clamp on the duct.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(e) Remove the clamshell clamp [6] at the air cycle machine [5].
NOTE: Lift the latch pawls at the same time to release the clamp.
(f) Move the sleeve [7] to the compressor outlet duct [11].
(g) Remove the coupling [2] at the heat exchanger.
(h) Remove the compressor outlet duct [11].
(i) Remove and discard the packing [3] at the heat exchanger.
(j) Remove and discard the packings [8].
SUBTASK 21-51-00-860-071
(2) Remove the mix muff, do this task: High Pressure Water Separator Mix Muff Removal,
TASK 21-51-17-000-801.
(a) Remove the flexible duct [36] from the condenser as follows:
1) Loosen the clamps [37] that attach the flexible duct to the water separator
condenser.
2) Remove the flexible duct from the water separator condenser.
SUBTASK 21-51-00-210-006
(3) Do a check of the flexible duct [36] that is connected to the high pressure water separator
condenser for any of the conditions listed below:
(a) Fraying
(b) discoloration
(c) rips
(d) splits
(e) tears
(f) rupture defects.
(g) If any of the above conditions are found, discard the flexible duct [36].
SUBTASK 21-51-00-720-001
(4) Do the torque check of the air cycle machine [5] as follows:
CAUTION
TURN THE ROTATING COMPONENTS OF THE ACM ONLY IN THE
DIRECTION THAT THEY TURN WHEN IN OPERATION. IF YOU TURN
THE ACM ROTATING COMPONENTS IN THE INCORRECT DIRECTION,
YOU CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE FOIL AIR BEARINGS.
(a) Use a torque wrench on the nut to turn the turbine wheel in the direction of normal
rotation.
NOTE: Normal rotation is clockwise when viewed from the turbine end and
counterclockwise when viewed from the fan end.
(b) The torque necessary to turn the nut must not be more than 20 in-lb (2 N·m).
1) If the torque is more than specified, replacement of the ACM is required.
NOTE: Wheel rub, endplay is too tight, dirt on the bearings or shaft, components
not seated correctly, shaft surface finish, journal bearing set preload is too
high, or housing assembly misalignment are probable cause for incorrect
torque.
SUBTASK 21-51-00-420-003
(5) Install the flexible duct [36] as follows:
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(a) Loosely position the two clamps [37] onto the flexible duct [36].
(b) Install the flexible duct [36] onto the water separator condenser.
(c) Position the forward clamp [37] to retain the flexible duct onto the water separator
condenser.
(d) Tighten the forward clamp [37] to 15.0 ±2.0 in-lb (1.7 ±0.2 N·m).
NOTE: The aft clamp is connected in the installation of the HPWS Mix Muff in the next
step.
SUBTASK 21-51-00-860-072
(6) Do this task: High Pressure Water Separator Mix Muff Installation, TASK 21-51-17-400-801.
SUBTASK 21-51-00-420-004
(7) To install the compressor outlet duct, do these steps:
(a) Apply a light coat of grease, D00504, to the packing [3] and packings [8].
(b) Install the new packings [8] on the duct ends.
(c) Install the new packing [3] at the heat exchanger.
(d) Put the compressor outlet duct [11] into its position.
(e) Install the coupling [2] at the heat exchanger.
1) Do not tighten the coupling [2] fully.
(f) Move the sleeve [7] over the compressor outlet duct [11] connection.
(g) Install the clamshell clamp [6] over the compressor outlet duct [11] connection.
(h) Tighten the nut on the coupling [2] to 45.0 in-lb (5.1 N·m) - 50.0 in-lb (5.6 N·m).
(i) With hand force, gently push the compressor outlet duct in the direction of the adjacent
mix muff duct until the compressor outlet duct reaches the maximum flexed position.
(j) Make sure that there is a minimum clearance of 0.20 in. (5.1 mm) to the adjacent mix
muff duct when the compressor outlet duct is in the flexed position.
(k) Apply a light coat of Pure Nickel Special compound, D00006, to the threads of the flex
hose.
(l) Connect the flex hose to the duct.
(m) Install the electrical connector [1] for the ram air control sensor.
(n) Install the electrical connector [4] for the compressor discharge overheat switch.
(o) Install the ground clip [32] that hold the bonding jumper [33] to the clamp on the duct.

21-51-00-700-807Ground Pack Run Test - APU AUTO Flow ModePDF p. 876
7. Ground Pack Run Test - APU AUTO Flow Mode
A. General
(1) The objective of this task is to monitor the temperatures on the P5-17 panel while the packs
are operating on the ground. The data collected from this procedure can be utilized to trend the
health of the system and troubleshoot temperature control issues. The data collected over time
can also help operators set the threshold at which maintenance is performed on the
pack/system. For this exercise, if the Outside Air Temperature (OAT) is 75°F (24°C) or higher,
set the L/R packs to the full COLD setting. If the OAT is below 75°F (24°C), maintain the packs
at the 12 o’clock AUTO position for data collection.

G. Flow Control and Shutoff Valve Installation
SUBTASK 21-51-01-010-042-002
(1) Remove the covers from the duct openings.
SUBTASK 21-51-01-020-070-002
(2) Install the bonding jumper on the flow control and shutoff valve [26].
(a) Set the bonding jumper [30] on the flow control and shutoff valve.
(b) Install the screw [33], washers [34], and nut [35].
SUBTASK 21-51-01-980-005-002
(3) Put the flow control and shutoff valve [26] in its position.
SUBTASK 21-51-01-420-011-002
(4) Loosely install the two clamps [27].
SUBTASK 21-51-01-420-012-002
(5) Install the screw [32] and washer [31] that connect the bonding jumper [30] to the structure.
(a) Make sure that you install any other bonding jumpers that you disconnected for this
procedure.
SUBTASK 21-51-01-020-071-002
(6) Install the sense line on the flow control and shutoff valve [26].
(a) Install a new O-ring [28] on the reducer [29].
(b) Apply a layer of Pure Nickel Special compound, D00006, to the threads of the
reducer [29].
(c) Install the reducer [29] on the flow control and shutoff valve [26].
1) Tighten the reducer [29] to 140 ±7 in-lb (15.8 ±0.8 N·m).
(d) Install the B-nut on the sense line.
1) Tighten the B-nut on the sense line to 170 ±9 in-lb (19.2 ±1.0 N·m).

H. Flow Control and Shutoff Valve Installation Test
SUBTASK 21-51-01-860-050-002
(1) Do this task: Supply Pressure to the Pneumatic System with the APU,
TASK 36-00-00-860-803.
SUBTASK 21-51-01-860-051-002
(2) Make sure that the flow control valve is closed with the applicable pack switch in the OFF
position.
(a) Put the applicable L PACK switch or R PACK switch in the OFF position.
(b) Make sure that the position indicator on the flow control and shutoff valve is in the closed
position.
SUBTASK 21-51-01-860-052-002
(3) Make sure that the flow control valve is partially open with the applicable pack switch in the
AUTO position.
(a) Put the applicable L PACK switch or R PACK switch in the AUTO position.
(b) Make sure that the position indicator on the flow control and shutoff valve moves to a
partially open position.
SUBTASK 21-51-01-860-053-002
(4) Make sure that the left flow control valve is commanded to HIGH with the pack switch in the
HIGH position.
(a) Disconnect the electrical connector D392 from the left flow control valve.
(b) Connect a digital/analog multimeter, COM-1793, between the electrical connector D392,
pins 1 and 2.
(c) Put the L PACK switch in the HIGH position.
(d) Make sure that there is 28±5 VDC between the electrical connector D392, pins 1 and 2.
(e) Put the L PACK switch in the AUTO position.
(f) Connect the electrical connector D392 to the left flow control valve.
SUBTASK 21-51-01-740-001-002
(5) Do a BITE test on the left and right pack/zone temperature controllers (M1442 and M1443):
NOTE: This will clear any fault introduced during maintenance when power is interrupted.
(a) Do this task: Pack/Zone Temperature Controller BITE Test, TASK 21-61-00-700-806-002.
SUBTASK 21-51-01-790-005-002
(6) Make sure that there is no air leakage at the couplings or the sense line connections you
removed for this task.
SUBTASK 21-51-01-860-054-002
(7) Put the applicable L PACK switch or R PACK switch in the OFF position.
SUBTASK 21-51-01-860-055-002
(8) Do this task: Remove Pressure from the Pneumatic System, TASK 36-00-00-860-806.

F. Right Flow Control and Shutoff Valve Removal
SUBTASK 21-51-01-010-039-002
(1) To get access to the flow control and shutoff valve, remove the Air Cycle Machine (ACM)
(TASK 21-51-04-000-802-002).
SUBTASK 21-51-01-020-063-002
(2) Remove the mix muff duct [51].
(a) Hold the mix muff duct [51] while you remove the coupling [56].
(b) Remove the mix muff duct [51].
SUBTASK 21-51-01-010-040-002
(3) Remove the compressor inlet duct [52].
CAUTION
HOLD THE DUCT WHEN YOU LOOSEN THE CLAMP. THE DUCT CAN
FALL WHEN THE CLAMP IS LOOSE. THE DUCT CAN BE DAMAGED IF IT
FALLS.
(a) Remove the clamshell clamp [53].
1) Lift the three latch pawls at the same time to release the clamshell clamp [53].
(b) Move the sleeve [54] to the compressor inlet duct [52].
(c) Remove the compressor inlet duct [52].
(d) Remove and discard the seals [55].
SUBTASK 21-51-01-010-041-002
(4) Disconnect the sense lines that follow to allow removal of the shutoff valve.
(a) Remove the nut [58] and washer [59] that hold the air line and water line from the High
Pressure Water Separator (HPWS) to the trim air duct.
Config 2
EFFECTIVITY
 006, 007, 013, 014, 018-020, 043, 044, 056-063,
