223, 224, 231-236, 239-298, 301-304, 306, 308, 315-317,
322-341, 343, 346-384
(b) Open the B-nuts [57] on the air line and water line.
NOTE: The sense lines must be completely disconnected from the HPWS manifold to
allow movement of the sense lines.
(c) Open the B-nut [57] at the union on the lower sense line [60] to the ACM.
(d) Rotate the sense line down to allow clearance to remove the shutoff valve [61].
SUBTASK 21-51-01-020-064-002
(5) Disconnect the electrical connectors from the flow control and shutoff valve [61]:
• electrical connector D490
• electrical connector D964
• electrical connector D492
• electrical connector D394.
SUBTASK 21-51-01-020-065-002
(6) Remove the sense line from the flow control and shutoff valve [61].
(a) Loosen the B-nut on the sense line.
(b) Remove the reducer [64].
(c) Discard the O-ring [63].
SUBTASK 21-51-01-020-066-002
(7) Remove the screw [67] and washer [66] that connect the bonding jumper [65] to the structure.
SUBTASK 21-51-01-020-067-002
(8) Hold the valve [61] as you remove the clamps [62].
SUBTASK 21-51-01-020-068-002
(9) Carefully remove the flow control and shutoff valve [61].
NOTE: You may move the sense lines you disconnected to remove the shutoff valve. Be
careful not to damage the sense lines.
SUBTASK 21-51-01-020-069-002
(10) Remove the bonding jumper from the flow control and shutoff valve [61].
NOTE: You will have to install it on the new flow control and shutoff valve.
(a) Remove the nut [70], washers [69], and screw [68].
(b) Remove the bonding jumper [65] from the flow control and shutoff valve [61].
(c) Keep the bonding jumper [65], screw [68], washers [69], and nut [70] for installation on
the new valve [61].
SUBTASK 21-51-01-410-015-002
(11) Put covers on the duct openings to keep out unwanted materials.

(1) Remove the covers from the duct openings.
SUBTASK 21-51-01-420-014-003

SUBTASK 21-51-01-420-020-003

SUBTASK 21-51-01-420-015-003
(4) Do these steps to install the bonding jumper [35] on the flow control and shutoff valve [26]:
(a) Soak a cleaning wiper, G50262, with alcohol, B00068, or alcohol, B50073, until it is
saturated with the solvent.
(b) Clean all bonding surfaces of the valve bonding tab [36], washer [32] under the bonding
tab, and surface of the bonding jumper [35] with wiper, G50262.
(c) Use a clean wiper, G50262, to remove all traces of the solvent from the bonding
surfaces.
(d) Install the screw [33], washers [32], and nut [34] that connect the bonding jumper [35] to
the valve bonding tab [36] on the flow control and shutoff valve [26].
(e) Tighten the nut to 33 in-lb (3.7 N·m) - 40 in-lb (4.5 N·m).
(f) Measure the electrical bonding resistance between the surface of the valve bonding
tab [36] and surface of the bonding jumper [35]:
1) Use an intrinsically safe approved bonding meter, COM-1550.
2) Make sure that the resistance is 0.010 ohm (10 milliohm) or less.
SUBTASK 21-51-01-420-018-003

• D15818 electrical connector

NOTE: The running torque is the torque required to just turn the locknut on the trunnion. The
running torque should be 7 in-lb (0.8 N·m) - 10 in-lb (1.1 N·m).
(a) With an appropriate torque wrench, measure the torque that is required to turn the
locknut on the trunnion.
1) Make a record of this value.
SUBTASK 21-51-01-420-026-003

(a) Tighten the locknut to 5 in-lb (0.6 N·m) above the running torque.
NOTE: If the running torque was measured at 8 in-lb (0.9 N·m), the torque required will
be 13 in-lb (1.5 N·m).
(b) Make sure that the alignment of the valve flange on the adjoining duct flange is
satisfactory.
(c) Tighten the locknut to 60 +5 / -0 in-lb (6.8 +0.6 / -0.0 N·m).

SUBTASK 21-51-02-710-010
(1) Do this test of the ACAU [1]:
NOTE: If you replaced the Air Conditioning Accessory Unit (ACAU M324 or M1455) because it
had a defect, it is recommended that the complete adjustment/test procedure for the
affected system be performed. For example, if an ACAU was replaced to correct a
defect in the ram air system, then it is recommended that a test of the ram air system
be performed. If the ACAU is being replaced for any other reason you may do just the
test that follows:
(a) If you installed the M324 ACAU, do this test of the left pack overheat relay:
1) Make sure that the L and R PACK switches, on the P5-10 Air Conditioning Panel,
are set to OFF position.

6) Make sure that the left PACK light, on the P5-10 Air Conditioning Panel, comes on.
7) Make sure that the AIR COND and MASTER CAUTION lights, on the P7 glareshield
panel, come on.
8) Remove the jumper wire that was installed between pins 1 and 2 of connector D532
on the ships' wiring.

switch, S2.

21-51-03-160-811Heat Exchanger - Blowing Out Debris/Blockages with Nitrogen Gas/Compressed AirPDF p. 959
2. Heat Exchanger - Blowing Out Debris/Blockages with Nitrogen Gas/Compressed Air
(Figure 201, Figure 202)
NOTE: This procedure is a scheduled maintenance task.
A. General
(1)  recommends performing this clearing procedure using nitrogen gas/compressed air to
effectively clear blocked heat exchangers.
(2) This task includes instructions to blow out debris or contaminant blockages trapped within the
cool air side heat exchanger grills.
(a) This is an effective method for clearing debris/blockages, especially for aircraft operating
in challenging environments (cottonwood/bug season, etc.).
(b) This method does not clean/break down contaminants (dust, dirt, airborne particles,
pollen, etc.) baked onto the heat exchanger grills over time.

I. Heat Exchanger - Blowing Out Debris/Blockages with Nitrogen Gas/Compressed Air
SUBTASK 21-51-03-160-010
(1) To blow out debris/blockages with nitrogen gas/compressed air in the heat exchanger grills
with the cleaning wand, SPL-14922, do the following steps:
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
WARNING
COMPRESSED GAS CAN BE DANGEROUS. EYE PROTECTION IS
MANDATORY. APPLY DRY NITROGEN CAREFULLY IN DIRECTION AWAY
FROM EYES AND FACE AND OTHER PERSONNEL TO AVOID POSSIBLE
INJURY.
(a) Blow out contaminant blockages with compressed clean dry air, G50321, or nitrogen,
G00018 (Figure 202).
1) Connect one end of the cleaning wand, SPL-14922, air hose to either the 0-200psig
dry filtered regulated air source, STD-6452, or nitrogen source, STD-1290, outlet.
NOTE: The cleaning wand, SPL-14922, includes an air hose, air wand, water hose,
water wand, and soap injector.
2) Connect other end of the cleaning wand, SPL-14922, air hose to the cleaning wand,
SPL-14922, air wand inlet.
NOTE: The adjustable neck of the cleaning wand, SPL-14922, can be lengthened
or shortened by its number of beads. It is acceptable to adjust the length by
adding or removing the beads as necessary.
3) Adjust the regulator on compressed clean dry air, G50321, or nitrogen, G00018, to
supply a recommended pressure of 100 psi (689 kPa) maximum to the cleaning
wand, SPL-14922.
CAUTION
DO NOT TOUCH THE COOLING FINS OF THE HEAT EXCHANGERS
WITH THE TIP OF THE CLEANING WAND. DAMAGE TO THE
COOLING FINS OF THE HEAT EXCHANGERS CAN OCCUR.
4) Insert the cleaning wand, SPL-14922, through the plenum/diffuser access openings
and blow clean dry air, G50321, or nitrogen, G00018, through the cooling fins of the
primary and secondary heat exchangers.
a) Make sure that the cooling fins of the heat exchanger are not damaged when
the cleaning wand, SPL-14922, was inserted through the plenum/diffuser
access panel openings.
b) Squeeze the handle on the cleaning wand, SPL-14922, air wand to blow the
clean dry air, G50321, or nitrogen, G00018, through the heat exchangers until
all debris is blown out of the cooling fins.
<1> Make sure that the pressure gauge on the regulator does not indicate
more than 100 psi (689 kPa) when the cleaning wand, SPL-14922
operates.
<2> Blow the clean dry air, G50321, or nitrogen, G00018, through all the
areas of the heat exchangers.
<3> Make sure that dirt, sand, gravel or plant fiber is no longer being blown
out on the opposite side (inlet side) of the heat exchanger.
<4> Continue blowing the clean dry air, G50321, or nitrogen, G00018,
through the heat exchangers until debris is no longer detected being
blown out.
c) Make sure that all loose dirt, sand, gravel, and plant fiber is removed from the
ram air inlet that was blown out of the heat exchangers.
5) Remove the cleaning wand, SPL-14922, from the inside of the plenum/diffuser
access opening.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
6) Decrease the compressed clean dry air, G50321, or nitrogen, G00018, pressure to
0 psi (0 kPa).
7) Remove the cleaning wand, SPL-14922.
SUBTASK 21-51-03-160-011
(2) To blow out heat exchanger debris/blockage with nitrogen gas/compressed air with the heating
exchanger cleaning wand, SPL-10099, do the following steps:
WARNING
COMPRESSED GAS CAN BE DANGEROUS. EYE PROTECTION IS
MANDATORY. APPLY DRY NITROGEN CAREFULLY IN DIRECTION AWAY
FROM EYES AND FACE AND OTHER PERSONNEL TO AVOID POSSIBLE
INJURY.
(a) Attach the heating exchanger cleaning wand, SPL-10099, to the regulator on a clean dry
air, G50321, bottle or nitrogen, G00018, bottle.
(b) Adjust the regulator on a clean dry air, G50321, bottle or nitrogen, G00018, bottle to
supply a maximum of 80 psi (552 kPa) to the heating exchanger cleaning wand,
SPL-10099.
NOTE: If a clean dry air, G50321, bottle is used, the moisture contaminant or water
concentration in the air of 0.00002 grams maximum is not required.
CAUTION
DO NOT TOUCH THE COOLING FINS OF THE HEAT EXCHANGERS
WITH THE TIP OF THE CLEANING WAND. DAMAGE TO THE COOLING
FINS OF THE HEAT EXCHANGERS CAN OCCUR.
(c) Insert the heating exchanger cleaning wand, SPL-10099, through the plenum/diffuser
access openings and blow clean dry air, G50321, or nitrogen, G00018, through the
cooling fins of the primary and secondary heat exchangers:
1) Make sure that the cooling fins of the heat exchanger are not damaged when the
heating exchanger cleaning wand, SPL-10099, was inserted through the
plenum/diffuser access panel openings.
2) Blow the clean dry air, G50321, or nitrogen, G00018, through the heat exchangers
until all debris is blown out of the cooling fins.
a) Make sure that the pressure gauge on the heating exchanger cleaning wand,
SPL-10099, does not indicate more than 80 psi (552 kPa) when the wand
operates.
b) Blow the clean dry air, G50321, or nitrogen, G00018, through all the areas of
the heat exchangers.
c) Make sure that dirt, sand, gravel or plant fiber is no longer being blown out on
the opposite side (inlet side) of the heat exchanger.
d) Continue blowing the clean dry air, G50321, or nitrogen, G00018, through the
heat exchangers until debris is no longer detected being blown out.
3) Make sure that all loose dirt, sand, gravel, and plant fiber is removed from the ram
air inlet that was blown out of the heat exchangers.
(d) Remove the heating exchanger cleaning wand, SPL-10099, from the inside of the
plenum/diffuser access opening and decrease the clean dry air, G50321, or nitrogen,
G00018, pressure to 0 psi (0 kPa).
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL

(1) Examine the gasket [1] and gaskets [5] for damage.

I. Air Cycle Machine Inspection
NOTE:  recommends to do an inspection of the air cycle machine when you get access to
the fan wheel. This inspection makes sure that the component operates correctly and helps
to prevent a non-scheduled removal. If you remove the heat exchanger and plenum/diffuser
assembly to clean the off-wing heat exchanger and do not have ECS related problems, then
the air cycle machine inspection is not necessary.
SUBTASK 21-51-03-211-002
(1) When the secondary plenum/diffuser [23] is removed from the air cycle machine [39], do these
steps to inspect the impeller blade [74] of the air cycle machine [39]:
(a) Make sure that the chord length (width) of each tip of impeller blade [74] is a minimum of
0.38 in. (9.65 mm).
(b) Do a visual check that no impeller blade [74] is broken or cracked.
Config 2
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(c) Replace the air cycle machine [39] with a new or serviceable unit if the inspection is
unsatisfactory.

SUBTASK 21-51-03-200-003-002
(1) Make sure that the identification (ID) plates are installed on the primary and secondary plenum.
NOTE: The ID plates on the primary and secondary plenum assemblies contain the heat
exchange unit information. The configuration of the equipment is shown by the part
number, dash number, series number, and change number stamped on the
identification plate. It is necessary to order and install ID plates, if the new plenum
assemblies are supplied without ID plates.
(a) If the new plenum assembly will be installed, make sure that all applicable data from the
original identification plate are transferred.
NOTE: New assembly means full assembly (Plenum, Diffuser, and Heat Exchanger).
SUBTASK 21-51-03-420-019-002
(2) If it is necessary, do these steps to install the primary diffuser assembly [82] in the primary
plenum (Figure 402).
NOTE: The diffuser assembly with the fan bypass check valve is installed in the primary
plenum/diffuser assembly.
(a) If the bracket [92] is removed, do these steps:
1) Apply a smooth coat of Dow Corning Q4-2817 sealant, A50035, to the mating
surfaces of the bracket [92] and primary plenum.
2) Lubricate the threads of the bolts [90] with anti-seize compound, C00852.
3) Loosely install the bolts [90] and washers [91] to hold the bracket [92] in its place.

(b) Put the primary diffuser assembly [82] in its position in the primary plenum with the
smaller diameter end of the primary diffuser assembly [82] forward and with the fan
bypass check valve at the bottom with respect to the installed position on the aircraft.
1) Make sure that the smaller diameter end is forward when you install the primary
diffuser assembly [82].
(c) Lubricate the threads of the screws [81] and bolts [83] with anti-seize compound,

before the washer [84] contacts the bracket.
(e) Loosely install the screws [81] through the holes in the plenum into the aft brackets on
the primary diffuser assembly [82].
1) Find the run-on torque as the screws [81] are installed in the nutplate self-locking

a) Use a torque wrench to measure the torque required to turn the screw [81]

1) Find the run-on torque as the bolts [90] are installed in the nutplate self-locking

a) Use the torque wrench to measure the torque required to turn the bolt [90]

(5) Do these steps to join the primary plenum/diffuser [8] to the secondary plenum/diffuser [23]:
(a) Put the flexible duct [62] in its position on the end of the secondary plenum/diffuser [23].
(b) Carefully move the heat exchangers together while you align the diffusers and plenum
ducts to minimize misalignment.
(c) Move the ends of the flexible duct [62] over the ends of the plenums.

is no damage.

(b) If necessary, remove the bonding jumper [10] from the plenum/diffuser access panel [3].
NOTE: The bonding jumper removal is not necessary if the task can be completed with
the access panel moved to the side.
1) Remove the sealant that covers the jumper terminal and the head of the bolt [7] on
the plenum/diffuser access panel [3] (SWPM 20-20-00 and SWPM 20-20-10).
2) Remove the bolt [7], washers [8], and nut [9] that attaches the bonding jumper [10]
to the plenum/diffuser access panel [3].
 ALL; AIRPLANES WITH PLENUM/DIFFUSER ACCESS PANEL WITH NUTPLATE.
(c) If necessary, remove the bonding jumper [10] from the plenum/diffuser access panel [3].
NOTE: The bonding jumper removal is not necessary if the task can be completed with
the access panel moved to the side.
1) Remove the sealant that covers the jumper terminal and the head of the bolt [7] on
the plenum/diffuser access panel [3] (SWPM 20-20-00 and SWPM 20-20-10).

plenum/diffuser access panel [3].

NOTE: Gravity force keeps the door closed when the system is off.
SUBTASK 21-51-03-710-001
(4) Make sure that the fan bypass check valve door [5] moves freely, do the steps that follow:
(a) Lightly push the fan bypass check valve door [5] up until it hits the fan bypass check

(b) Operate the door through 3 cycles and examine the door for free movement.
SUBTASK 21-51-03-100-009
(5) If you see dirt or contamination, clean dirt or contamination with soap and water where the fan
bypass check valve door [5] and primary diffuser assembly [6] touch.
SUBTASK 21-51-03-400-001

21-51-03-160-807Heat Exchanger and Plenum/Diffuser Assembly Cleaning Using Backflush EquipmentPDF p. 1033
2. Heat Exchanger and Plenum/Diffuser Assembly Cleaning Using Backflush Equipment
(Figure 701)
NOTE: This procedure is a scheduled maintenance task.
A. General
(1)  notes that this procedure for cleaning with backflush equipment is not effective for
clearing blocked heat exchangers and less effective for dirty heat exchangers. To effectively
clear blocked heat exchangers, do this task: Heat Exchanger - Blowing Out Debris/Blockages
with Nitrogen Gas/Compressed Air, TASK 21-51-03-160-811.
(2) You can use either a ground air source or airplane pneumatic air to do this procedure. If you
use airplane pneumatic air, you must operate the APU.

I. Heat Exchanger and Plenum/Diffuser Assembly Cleaning Using Backflush Equipment
SUBTASK 21-51-03-020-002
CAUTION
DO NOT USE SOAP OR A DETERGENT SOLUTION TO CLEAN THE HEAT
EXCHANGERS. USE COLD WATER ONLY. SOAP OR A DETERGENT
SOLUTION CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE AIR CYCLE MACHINE.
(1) Use the backflusher, SPL-1607, to clean the heat exchanger.
NOTE: You must do these steps for each of the heat exchangers.
(a) Connect the air hose to the cleaning head.
(b) Connect the water supply hose to the cleaning head.
(c) If you use the airplane pneumatic system air for the air source, do this step:
1) Do this task: Supply Pressure to the Pneumatic System with the APU,
TASK 36-00-00-860-803.
(d) If you use a ground pneumatic air for the air source, do this step:
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
CAUTION
DO NOT SUPPLY MORE THAN 30 PSIG OF GROUND AIR
PRESSURE TO THE HEAT EXCHANGERS. TOO MUCH PRESSURE
CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE HEAT EXCHANGERS OR THE RAM
AIR EXIT DUCTS.
1) Start the ground air source and adjust the pressure regulator to a maximum of
30 psig (207 kPa).
WARNING
MAKE SURE THAT YOU CORRECTLY ATTACH THE HOSE ASSEMBLY
BEFORE YOU SUPPLY PRESSURE. WHEN YOU PUT PRESSURE ON
THE HOSE, THE ASSEMBLY CAN MOVE QUICKLY. IF YOU DO NOT
OBEY, INJURIES TO PERSONNEL AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT CAN
OCCUR.
(e) If installed, slowly open the air supply valve on the manifold of the cleaning tool.
(f) Slowly open the water supply valve on the 0 to 60 PSIG regulated cold water source,
STD-3926.
(g) If installed, slowly open the water supply valve on the manifold of the cleaning tool.
(h) Clean the heat exchanger for 5 minutes.
(i) Close the water supply valve on the 0 to 60 PSIG regulated cold water source,
STD-3926, and continue to supply air for an additional 2 minutes.
(j) If you use the airplane pneumatic system air, set the APU BLEED switch, on the P5-10
panel, to the OFF position.
(k) If you use a ground pneumatic air for the air source, set the valve on the ground
pneumatic cart to the OFF position.
WARNING
PUT ON GLOVES FOR PROTECTION FROM THE HOT WATER IN THE
HOSES. HOT WATER CAN BURN YOU.
(l) Disconnect the air hose from the cleaning head.
WARNING
PUT ON GLOVES FOR PROTECTION FROM THE HOT WATER IN THE
HOSES. HOT WATER CAN BURN YOU.
(m) Disconnect the water supply hose from the cleaning head.
(n) Do the steps above, as necessary, for the other heat exchangers.
SUBTASK 21-51-03-020-003
(2) If not already done, close the valve at the water source.
SUBTASK 21-51-03-030-001

21-51-03-160-809Heat Exchanger - Cleaning with Soap-Water-AirPDF p. 1048
3. Heat Exchanger - Cleaning with Soap-Water-Air
(Figure 702, Figure 703, Figure 704, Figure 705)
NOTE: This procedure is a scheduled maintenance task.
A. General
(1)  notes that this procedure for cleaning with soap-water-air is not effective for clearing
blocked heat exchangers and less effective for dirty heat exchangers. To effectively clear
blocked heat exchangers, do this task: Heat Exchanger - Blowing Out Debris/Blockages with
Nitrogen Gas/Compressed Air, TASK 21-51-03-160-811.
(2) This procedure can improve heat exchanger performance between scheduled maintenance
intervals when internal heat exchanger contamination is present (resulting in decreased
performance) due to local environment conditions.

I. Heat Exchanger Cleaning with Soap-Water-Air
SUBTASK 21-51-03-100-007
WARNING
MAKE SURE THAT YOU WEAR A FACE MASK, EYE PROTECTION, AND
WATER RESISTANT CLOTHING DURING THE OPERATION. PREVENT SOAP
AND HEAT EXCHANGER CONTAMINATION ON THE SKIN, EYES, AND HAIR.
IF YOU DO NOT OBEY INSTRUCTIONS, INJURY TO PERSONNEL CAN
OCCUR.
(1) To clean the heat exchangers, do the 3 steps that follow:
• Step 1: Soak with soap, B50026, and water, G50256, to remove dust or small particles.
• Step 2: Rinse off with high pressure clean water, G50256.
• Step 3: Blow off water, G50256, for a minimum of 2 minutes to protect the Air Cycle Machine
(ACM) from ingesting large water droplets.
WARNING
COMPRESSED GAS CAN BE DANGEROUS. EYE PROTECTION IS
MANDATORY. APPLY DRY NITROGEN CAREFULLY IN DIRECTION AWAY
FROM EYES AND FACE AND OTHER PERSONNEL TO AVOID POSSIBLE
INJURY.
(a) Soak with soap, B50026, and water, G50256, to remove dust/fine particle residue
(Figure 703).
1) Connect the cleaning wand, SPL-14922, soap injector to the cleaning wand,
SPL-14922, water wand water inlet.
a) Make sure that the lever on the cleaning wand, SPL-14922, water wand is
OFF (CLOSE).
2) Put the cleaning wand, SPL-14922, soap injector tube inlet into the soap container.
3) Connect one end of the cleaning wand, SPL-14922, water hose to the cleaning
wand, SPL-14922, soap injector.
a) Make sure that the lever on the cleaning wand, SPL-14922, soap injector is
OFF (CLOSE).
4) Connect the other end of the cleaning wand, SPL-14922, water hose to the water
cart.
5) If using clean dry air, G50321, (Optional – Not Required):
a) Make sure that one end of the cleaning wand, SPL-14922, air hose is
connected to either the 0-200psig dry filtered regulated air source, STD-6452,
or nitrogen source, STD-1290, outlet.
b) Connect the other end of the cleaning wand, SPL-14922, air hose to the
cleaning wand, SPL-14922, water wand air inlet.
c) Adjust the regulator on the 0-200psig dry filtered regulated air source,
STD-6452, or nitrogen source, STD-1290, to supply 50 psi (345 kPa)
maximum to the cleaning wand, SPL-14922.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
6) Insert the cleaning wand, SPL-14922, through the plenum/diffuser access openings
and spray the soap, B50026, and water, G50256, through the cooling fins of the
primary and secondary heat exchangers.
a) Make sure that you do not damage the cooling fins of the heat exchangers
when you put the cleaning wand, SPL-14922, through the plenum/diffuser
access panel openings.
NOTE: Since the cleaning wand, SPL-14922, uses an adjustable plastic tip to
blow air through the heat exchangers, the tip will not damage the
cooling fins upon making contact.
b) Move the lever on the cleaning wand, SPL-14922, water wand to ON (OPEN).
c) Move the lever on the cleaning wand, SPL-14922, soap injector to ON
(OPEN).
NOTE: Switching the order will most likely cause the user to get wet.
d) Spray the soap, B50026, and water, G50256, through the heat exchangers to
soak and to remove dust and small particles.
<1> Squeeze the handle on the cleaning wand, SPL-14922, air wand to
blow the clean dry air, G50321, or nitrogen, G00018, with soap,
B50026, and water, G50256, if clean dry air, G50321, or nitrogen,
G00018, is needed.
<2> Spray through all the areas of the heat exchangers.
7) Remove the cleaning wand, SPL-14922, from the plenum/diffuser access opening.
8) Decrease the 0-200psig dry filtered regulated air source, STD-6452, or nitrogen
source, STD-1290, pressure to zero psi (if clean dry air, G50321, or nitrogen,
G00018, is used, but not required).
9) Move the lever on the cleaning wand, SPL-14922, soap injector to OFF (CLOSE).
10) Move the lever on the cleaning wand, SPL-14922, water wand to OFF (CLOSE).
11) Remove the cleaning wand, SPL-14922, water hose from the cleaning wand,
SPL-14922, soap injector.
12) Remove the cleaning wand, SPL-14922, soap injector.
(b) Rinse with high pressure clean water, G50256 (Figure 704).
1) Make sure that the cleaning wand, SPL-14922, air hose is connected to the
cleaning wand, SPL-14922, water wand air inlet.
2) Connect the cleaning wand, SPL-14922, water hose to the cleaning wand,
SPL-14922, water wand water inlet.
3) Adjust the regulator on the 0-200psig dry filtered regulated air source, STD-6452, or
nitrogen source, STD-1290, to supply 50 psi (345 kPa) maximum to the cleaning
wand, SPL-14922.
NOTE: Vaporized clean dry air, G50321, is made with use of pressure over 100 psi.
4) Put the cleaning wand, SPL-14922, through the plenum/diffuser access opening.
5) Clean with strong pressure clean water, G50256, through the cooling fins of the
primary and secondary heat exchangers.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
a) Make sure that you do not damage the cooling fins of the heat exchangers
when you put the cleaning wand, SPL-14922, through the plenum/diffuser
access panel openings.
NOTE: Since the cleaning wand, SPL-14922, uses an adjustable plastic tip to
blow air through the heat exchangers, the tip will not damage the
cooling fins upon making contact.
b) Put the lever on the cleaning wand, SPL-14922, water wand to ON (OPEN) for
water, G50256, to start flowing.
c) Squeeze the handle on the cleaning wand, SPL-14922, water wand for clean
dry air, G50321, or nitrogen, G00018, to start flowing.
d) Wash through the heat exchangers with the strong pressure clean water,
G50256, to clean the soap, B50026.
<1> Clean all the areas of the heat exchangers.
6) Remove the cleaning wand, SPL-14922, from the plenum/diffuser access opening.
7) Decrease the 0-200psig dry filtered regulated air source, STD-6452, or nitrogen
source, STD-1290, pressure to zero psi.
8) Put the lever on the cleaning wand, SPL-14922, water wand to OFF (CLOSE).
9) Remove the cleaning wand, SPL-14922, water hose and cleaning wand,
SPL-14922, water wand air inlet.
(c) Blow off residual water, G50256, to protect the ACM (Figure 705).
1) Connect the cleaning wand, SPL-14922, air hose to the cleaning wand, SPL-14922,
air inlet.
2) Adjust the regulator on 0-200psig dry filtered regulated air source, STD-6452, or
nitrogen source, STD-1290, to supply 100 psi (689 kPa) maximum to the cleaning
wand, SPL-14922.
3) Put the cleaning wand, SPL-14922, through the plenum/diffuser openings.
4) Blow clean dry air, G50321, or nitrogen, G00018, through the cooling fins of the
primary and secondary heat exchangers to dry of remaining water, G50256.
a) Make sure that you do not damage the cooling fins of the heat exchangers
when you put the cleaning wand, SPL-14922, through the plenum/diffuser
access panel.
NOTE: Since the cleaning wand, SPL-14922, uses an adjustable plastic tip to
blow air through the heat exchangers, the tip will not damage the
cooling fins upon making contact.
b) Blow the clean dry air, G50321, or nitrogen, G00018, through the heat
exchangers until all remaining water, G50256, is blown out of the cooling fins.
<1> Make sure that the pressure gage on the regulator does not show more
than 100 psi (689 kPa) when you operate the cleaning wand,
SPL-14922.
<2> Blow the clean dry air, G50321, or nitrogen, G00018, through all the
areas of the heat exchangers.
<3> Make sure that water, G50256, is fully removed from the heat
exchanger.
<4> Blow clean dry air, G50321, or nitrogen, G00018, through the heat
exchangers until water, G50256, is not being blown out.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
5) Remove the cleaning wand, SPL-14922, from the plenum/diffuser access opening.
6) Decrease the 0-200psig dry filtered regulated air source, STD-6452, or nitrogen
source, STD-1290, pressure to zero psi.

SUBTASK 21-51-04-010-005-002
WARNING
DO NOT TOUCH THE COOLING PACK DUCTS WHEN THEY ARE HOT. HOT
DUCTS CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONNEL.
(1) Remove the compressor outlet duct [11].
(a) Disconnect the flex hose from the duct.
(b) Remove the electrical connector [1] from the control sensor for the ram air.
(c) Remove the electrical connector [4] from the overheat switch for the compressor
discharge.
(d) Remove the clamshell clamp [6] at the air cycle machine [5].
1) Lift the latch pawls at the same time to release the clamp [6].
(e) Move the sleeve [7] to the compressor outlet duct [11].
(f) Remove the coupling [2] at the heat exchanger.
(g) Remove the compressor outlet duct [11].
(h) Remove and discard the packing [3] at the heat exchanger.
(i) Remove and discard the packings [8].
SUBTASK 21-51-04-860-014-002
(2) Remove the High Pressure Water Separator (HPWS) mix muff (TASK 21-51-17-000-801).
SUBTASK 21-51-04-210-003
(3) Do a check of the flexible duct [36] that is connected to the high pressure water separator
condenser for all of the conditions listed below:
(a) fraying
(b) discoloration
(c) rips
(d) splits
(e) tears

 ALL
(f) rupture defects.
(g) If you find one or more of the above conditions, remove the flexible duct [36] from the
condenser as follows:
1) Loosen the clamp [37] that attaches the flexible duct [36] to the water separator
condenser.
2) Remove and discard the flexible duct [36] from the water separator condenser.
SUBTASK 21-51-04-020-002-002
(4) Disconnect the hoses and sense line from the air cycle machine [5].
(a) Remove the flex hose 1 [19] from the air cycle machine [5].
(b) Disconnect the flex hose 2 [23] from the air cycle machine [5].
(c) Disconnect the sense line [12] from the air cycle machine [5].
(d) If you will replace the air cycle machine [5], remove the unions [13] and O-rings [14].
1) Discard the O-rings [14].
SUBTASK 21-51-04-020-003-002
(5) Remove the air cycle machine [5].
(a) Remove the clamshell clamp [16].
1) Lift the latch pawls at the same time to release each clamp [16].
(b) Move the sleeve [17] away from the air cycle machine [5] and onto the adjacent duct.
(c) Remove and discard the O-rings [18].
(d) Disconnect the compressor inlet duct [9].
1) Remove the bolt [31] that holds the ground clip [32] to the air cycle machine [5].
2) Move the bonding jumper [33] away from the air cycle machine [5].
a) Do not remove the ground clip [32] from the bonding jumper [33].
3) Remove the bolts [29] that hold the compressor inlet duct [9] to the air cycle
machine [5].
4) Remove and discard the O-ring [30].
(e) Remove the bolts [21] and washers [22] that hold the air cycle machine [5] to the
secondary heat exchanger.

EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR.

3. Air Cycle Machine Installation
(Figure 401)
A. General
(1) This task is the installation of the Air Cycle Machine (ACM).
(2) Do the steps in the Cooling Pack Water Removal/Ice Protection System Inspection. If the water
removal paths are blocked, ice can be in the ACM. The ice can cause failure of the ACM.

SUBTASK 21-51-04-630-010-002
(3) If you replaced the air cycle machine [5] because of bearing failure or damage to the
compressor, do these steps:
(a) Disconnect the water drain lines from the bottom of the water extractors
(TASK 21-51-14-000-801).
1) Use compressed air to remove unwanted material from the water drain lines.
2) Connect the water drain lines to the bottom of the water extractors
(TASK 21-51-14-400-801).
(b) Disconnect the water line and the air line which are attached to the water spray nozzle
(TASK 21-51-16-000-801).
1) Use compressed air to remove unwanted material from the water and air lines.
2) Connect the water line and the air line which are attached to the water spray nozzle
(TASK 21-51-16-400-801).
(c) Remove the flex hose 1 [19] and flex hose 2 [23].
1) Use compressed air to remove unwanted material from the flex hoses.
2) Reconnect the flex hose 2 [23].
NOTE: You must install the flex hose 1 after you install the ACM.
SUBTASK 21-51-04-630-011-002
(4) If you replaced the air cycle machine [5] because of damage to the compressor, do these
steps:
(a) Examine the components that follow for damage or unwanted materials:

access panel.
3) Remove the plenum/diffuser access panels and the gaskets.

feature.

washer [22] contacts the air cycle machine [5].

run-on torque.
(p) Tighten the bolts [29] and bolt [31] to 22 in-lb (2.5 N·m) - 26 in-lb (2.9 N·m).

(d) Put the compressor outlet duct [11] into its position.
(e) Apply compound, D50320, to the bolt threads of the coupling [2].
(f) Install the coupling [2] at the heat exchanger.
1) Do not tighten the coupling [2] fully.
(g) Move the sleeve [7] on the connection for the compressor outlet duct [11].
(h) Install the clamp [6] on the connection of the compressor outlet duct [11].
(i) Tighten the nut on the coupling [2] to 45 in-lb (5.1 N·m) - 50 in-lb (5.6 N·m).
(j) With hand force, carefully push the compressor outlet duct [11] in the direction of the
adjacent mix muff duct until the compressor outlet duct [11] is at the position of maximum
flex.
Config 2

 ALL
(k) Make sure that there is a minimum clearance of 0.20 in. (5.1 mm) to the adjacent mix
muff duct when the compressor outlet duct [11] is at the position of maximum flex.

hose.
(m) Connect the flex hose to the compressor outlet duct [11].
(n) Install the electrical connector [1] for the control sensor for the ram air.
(o) Install the electrical connector [4] for the overheat switch for the compressor discharge.

F. Conditioned Air Check Valve Installation
SUBTASK 21-51-07-630-002-002
(1) Remove the duct covers.
SUBTASK 21-51-07-420-002-002
(2) Install the conditioned air check valve [1] as follows:
(a) Examine the gasket [7] on the flange of the bulkhead penetration duct assembly [15].
(b) Replace the gasket [7] if it is damaged or worn.
(c) Put the conditioned air check valve [1] in its position.
1) Make sure the check valve is installed in the same orientation as when it was
removed.
(d) Install the bolts [10], washers [8], and nuts [9] that attach the check valve [1] to the
bulkhead penetration duct assembly [15].
(e) Slide the forward end of the flexible duct [3] forward onto the aft end of the conditioned air
check valve [1].
(f) Position the individual clamps [14] so that these conditions are met:
1) Make sure the clamps are not installed on the duct bead.
2) Keep a 0.125 in. (3.175 mm) minimum distance between the clamps and the edge
of the flexible duct [3].
3) Make sure that the two forward clamps [14] are located forward of the bead on the
aft end of the check valve [1].
Config 2
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
4) Make sure the aft clamp [14] is located aft of the bead on the forward end of the
condenser outlet duct [16].
5) Make sure that the forward clamp [14] is located inside (aft) of the bead on the
flexible duct [3].
6) Make sure that the aft clamp [14] is located inside (forward) of the bead on the
flexible duct [3].
7) Install the brackets [13] that connect the clamps [14] together.
a) If necessary, reposition the clamps [14] axially so that the brackets [13] can be
installed.
b) Make sure that the clamps [14] are positioned so that the position
requirements are still met.
c) Install the washers [11] and nuts [12] that retain the brackets [13] to the
clamps [14].
d) Tighten the nuts [12] to 63 in-lb (7.1 N·m) - 67 in-lb (7.6 N·m).
(g) Install the nuts [4] on the clamps [14].
(h) Determine the run-on torque value of the nuts on the T-bolts for each nut and T-bolt
combination as follows:
1) Rotate the nut [4] onto the T-bolt until it is approximately one turn from seating and
at least 3 T-bolt threads are protruding from the top of the nut [4].
2) Measure the torque value required to turn the nut [4] the last revolution before it
seats.
3) Make a record of this torque value.
NOTE: The torque value must be between 2 in-lb (0.2 N·m) - 18 in-lb (2.0 N·m).
(i) Tighten the nuts [4] to 12 in-lb (1.4 N·m) - 14 in-lb (1.6 N·m) plus the run-on torque value
determined for each nut [4].
SUBTASK 21-51-07-020-004-002
(3) Do these steps to install the sense line:
(a) Install a new o-ring [6] on the union [5].
(b) Apply a layer of Pure Nickel Special compound, D00006, to the threads of the union [5].
(c) Install the union [5] in the check valve [1].
(d) Connect the sense line to the union [5].

(19) For the left high pressure water separator [1], disconnect these electrical connectors:
(a) Disconnect the electrical connector D3866 from the pack temperature sensor.
(b) Disconnect the electrical connector D3930 from the pack temperature bulb.
SUBTASK 21-51-08-020-002
(20) For the right high pressure water separator [1], disconnect these electrical connectors:
(a) Disconnect the electrical connector D3876 from the pack temperature sensor.
(b) Disconnect the electrical connector D3982 from the pack temperature bulb.
SUBTASK 21-51-08-020-003
(21) Do these steps to disconnect the two ducts from the reheater:
(a) Remove the bolts [13], washers [14], washers [15], and nuts [16].

SUBTASK 21-51-08-020-004
WARNING
BE CAREFUL WHEN YOU MOVE THE COMPONENT. THE COMPONENT IS
HEAVY. INJURIES TO PERSONS CAN OCCUR.
(22) To remove the high pressure water separator [1] from the airplane, do these steps:
(a) For the forward attach points do the steps that follow:
1) Remove the nut [21], washer [20], countersunk washer [19], and bolt [18].
2) Remove the bushing [22] from the bracket.
(b) For the aft attach points do the steps that follow:
1) Remove the nut [21], washer [20], countersunk washer [19], and bolt [23].
2) Remove the bushings [24] from the bracket.
(c) Carefully lower the high pressure water separator [1] from the Environmental Control
System (ECS) bay.

H. High Pressure Water Separator Installation
SUBTASK 21-51-08-480-002
(1) Remove the duct and line covers.
SUBTASK 21-51-08-420-001
WARNING
BE CAREFUL WHEN YOU MOVE THE COMPONENT. THE COMPONENT IS
HEAVY. INJURIES TO PERSONS CAN OCCUR.
(2) To install the high pressure water separator [1] assembly on the airplane, do these steps:
(a) Carefully position the high pressure water separator [1] in the Environmental Control
System (ECS) bay.
(b) For the forward attach points do the steps that follow:
1) Install the bushing [22] in the bracket.
2) Install the nut [21], washer [20], countersunk washer [19], and bolt [18].
a) Position the countersunk side of the countersunk washer [19] under the head
of the bolt [18].
(c) For the aft attach points do the steps that follow:
1) Install the bushings [24] in the bracket.
2) Install the nut [21], washer [20], countersunk washer [19], and bolt [23].
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
a) Position the countersunk side of the countersunk washer [19] under the bolt
head.
(d) For the right high pressure water separator [1] installation, make sure that there is a
minimum of 0.10 in. (2.54 mm) clearance between the supply duct to the trim air
Pressure Regulating and Shutoff Valve (PRSOV) and the water collection manifold.
1) If there is not a minimum of 0.10 in. (2.54 mm) clearance, do one of these steps to
provide the minimum clearance:
a) Reposition the supply duct to the trim air PRSOV.
b) Remove material from the water collection manifold.
SUBTASK 21-51-08-420-002
(3) Do these steps to connect the ducts to the reheater:
(a) Apply a thin coat of one of these lubricants to the new O-rings [17]:
1) Braycote Micronic 601EF grease, D50380
2) Braycote 601EF Grease, D50203
3) Braycote 815Z lubricant, D50268
4) Fluorolube GR-660 lubricant, D00548
5) Krytox 240AB grease, D50234
6) Krytox 240AZ grease, D50233
7) Krytox 240AC perfluoropolyether grease, D50063.
(b) Install the O-ring [17] on each of the duct.
(c) Install the bolts [13], washers [14], washers [15], and nuts [16].
SUBTASK 21-51-08-420-003
(4) Install the flexible duct [12] on the mix muff and the condenser.
SUBTASK 21-51-08-420-004
(5) Install the clamps [11] on the flexible duct [12].
(a) Apply Pure Nickel Special compound, D00006, to the T-bolt thread of the clamps [11].
(b) Tighten the clamps [11] to 13 in-lb (1.5 N·m) - 17 in-lb (1.9 N·m).
(c) Apply an approximately 0.125 in. (3.175 mm) wide torque stripe, G50411, or tamper-proof
putty/lacquer, G51905, to the clamps [11].
SUBTASK 21-51-08-400-001
(6) If it is necessary, do these steps to install the union [43]:
(a) Lubricate the new packing [44] with lubricant, D00602, or equivalent.
(b) Install the packing [44] on the union [43].
(c) Lubricate the threads of the union [43] with Pure Nickel Special compound, D00006.
(d) Install the union [43] on the high pressure water separator [1].
1) Torque the union [43] to 280 ±28 in-lb (31.6 ±3.2 N·m).
SUBTASK 21-51-08-420-005
(7) Install the de-icing hose [26] on the union [43].
(a) Torque the B-nut to 280 ±14 in-lb (31.6 ±1.6 N·m).
SUBTASK 21-51-08-420-014
(8) If it is necessary, do these steps to install the union [34]:
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(a) Lubricate the new packing [35] with lubricant, D00602, or equivalent.
(b) Install the packing [35] on the union [34].
(c) Lubricate the threads of the union [34] with Pure Nickel Special compound, D00006.
(d) Install the union [34] on the high pressure water separator [1].
1) Torque the union [34] to 170 ±17 in-lb (19.2 ±1.9 N·m).
SUBTASK 21-51-08-420-006
(9) Install the B-nut of the condensor outlet sense line [25] on the union [34].
(a) Torque the B-nut to 170 ±9 in-lb (19.2 ±1.0 N·m).
SUBTASK 21-51-08-420-007
(10) For the high pressure water separator [1] on the left cooling pack, install these electrical
connectors:
(a) Install the electrical connector D3866 on the pack temperature sensor.
(b) Install the electrical connector D3930 on the pack temperature bulb.
SUBTASK 21-51-08-420-008
(11) For the high pressure water separator [1] on the right cooling pack, install these electrical
connectors:
(a) Install the electrical connector D3876 on the pack temperature sensor.
(b) Install the electrical connector D3982 on the pack temperature bulb.
SUBTASK 21-51-08-420-009
(12) To install the coupling assembly on the condenser, do these steps:
(a) Put the retainer [10] over the duct bead and the bead on the condenser.
(b) Move the sleeve [8] and ring [9] over the retainer [10].
(c) Install the coupling [7].
1) Torque the coupling [7] to 100 ±5 in-lb (11.3 ±0.6 N·m).
SUBTASK 21-51-08-420-015
(13) If it is necessary, do these steps to install the unions [32] and union [30]:
(a) Lubricate the new packing [33] and new packing [31] with lubricant, D00602, or
equivalent.
(b) Install the packing [33] on the union [32].
(c) Install the packing [31] on the union [30].
(d) Lubricate the threads of the union [32] and union [30] with Pure Nickel Special
compound, D00006.
(e) Install the union [32] and union [30] on the high pressure water separator [1].
1) Torque the union [30] to 170 ±17 in-lb (19.2 ±1.9 N·m).
2) Torque the union [32] to 140 ±14 in-lb (15.8 ±1.6 N·m).
SUBTASK 21-51-08-400-002
(14) If it is necessary, do these steps to install the union [41] on the lower port of the manifold:
(a) Lubricate the new packing [42] with lubricant, D00602, or equivalent.
(b) Install the new packing [42] on the union [41].
(c) Lubricate the threads of the union [41] with Pure Nickel Special compound, D00006.
(d) Install the union [41] on the high pressure water separator [1].
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
1) Torque the union [41] to 170 ±17 in-lb (19.2 ±1.9 N·m).
SUBTASK 21-51-08-420-010
(15) Do these steps to connect the lines for the water spray nozzle to the manifold:
(a) Install the B-nut of the air line elbow [39] on the union [32].
1) Torque the B-nut of the air line elbow [39] to 170 ±9 in-lb (19.2 ±1.0 N·m).
(b) Install the B-nut of the water line elbow [40] on the union [41].
1) Torque the B-nut of the water line elbow [40] to 280 ±14 in-lb (31.6 ±1.6 N·m).
SUBTASK 21-51-08-210-001
(16) Make sure that there is not a plastic plug in the water overflow port in the water collection
manifold:
NOTE: This port must be open in the case the water spray nozzle becomes clogged.
(a) Remove the plastic plug if it is installed.
SUBTASK 21-51-08-420-016
(17) If it is necessary, do these steps to install the union [28]:
(a) Lubricate the new packing [29] with lubricant, D00602, or equivalent.
(b) Install the packing [29] on the union [28].
(c) Lubricate the threads of the union [28] with Pure Nickel Special compound, D00006.
(d) Install the union [28] on the high pressure water separator [1].
1) Torque the union [28] to 170 ±17 in-lb (19.2 ±1.9 N·m).
SUBTASK 21-51-08-420-011
(18) Install the B-nut of the sense line [2] on the union [28].
(a) Torque the B-nut of the sense line [2] to 170 ±9 in-lb (19.2 ±1.0 N·m).
SUBTASK 21-51-08-420-017
(19) Install the B-nut of the water extractor duct drain line [6] on the union [30].
(a) Torque the B-nut of the water extractor duct drain line [6] to 170 ±9 in-lb (19.2 ±1.0 N·m).
SUBTASK 21-51-08-420-012
(20) If removed, install the clamps [36], screw [37], washer [45], washer [46], spacer [38], and
nut [47] between the sense line [2] and water extractor duct drain line [6].
SUBTASK 21-51-08-420-013
(21) For the high pressure water separator [1] on the left cooling pack do this step:
(a) Install the clamps [36], screw [3], washers [4], and nut [5].

panel):
(a) Remove the DO NOT OPERATE tag, STD-858, and set the applicable L or R PACK

(b) Remove the DO NOT OPERATE tag, STD-858, and set the BLEED 1 and 2 switches to

SUBTASK 21-51-08-790-001
(5) Do a soap bubble test of all the applicable duct joints.
NOTE: No leakage is permitted.
(a) If there is leakage, do these steps:
1) Put the L PACK and R PACK switches in the OFF position.
WARNING
DO NOT TOUCH THE COOLING PACK DUCTS WHEN THEY ARE
HOT. HOT DUCTS CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONNEL.
2) Loosen the clamps.
3) Make sure that the ducts are aligned at the joints.
4) Tighten the clamps.
5) Put the L PACK and R PACK switches in the AUTO position.
6) Make sure that the leak has been repaired.

F. Standby Temperature Control Valve Removal
SUBTASK 21-51-11-020-001
WARNING
DO NOT TOUCH THE COOLING PACK DUCTS WHEN THEY ARE HOT. HOT
DUCTS CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONNEL.
(1) Disconnect the electrical connector [3] from the standby temperature control valve [1].
SUBTASK 21-51-11-020-002
(2) Do these steps to disconnect the four sense lines from the valve:
(a) Make a record of the sense line connections to make sure that they are installed in the
same locations.
(b) Remove the screw [15] and washer [16] that hold the sense line clamps to the structure.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(c) Remove the screw [5], washer [6], and nut [7] that hold the sense line clamps together.
(d) Remove the conditioned air check valve sense line [11].
(e) Remove the condenser outlet pressure sense line [9].
(f) Remove the ACM turbine muffler sense line [4].
(g) Remove the condenser inlet pressure sense line [10].
SUBTASK 21-51-11-020-003
(3) Remove the screw [14], washer [13], and nut [12] that hold the bonding jumper [2] to the
standby temperature control valve [1].
SUBTASK 21-51-11-020-004
(4) Hold the standby temperature control valve [1] when you remove the two clamps [8].
SUBTASK 21-51-11-160-001
(5) Carefully remove the standby temperature control valve [1] from its position between the ducts.
SUBTASK 21-51-11-020-005
(6) Remove the reducer [19] from the conditioned air check valve sense line [11] location.
SUBTASK 21-51-11-020-012
(7) Remove the unions [17] at the remaining three sense line locations.
SUBTASK 21-51-11-020-006
(8) Remove and discard the packing [20] from the conditioned air check valve sense line [11]
location.
SUBTASK 21-51-11-020-011
(9) Remove and discard the packings [18] at the remaining three sense line locations.

G. Standby Temperature Control Valve Installation
SUBTASK 21-51-11-420-001
(1) Install the reducer [19] on the standby temperature control valve [1], do these steps:
(a) Install a new packing [20] on the reducer [19].
(b) Apply a thin layer of Pure Nickel Special compound, D00006, to the threads of the
reducer [19].
(c) Install the reducer [19] on the standby temperature control valve [1].
SUBTASK 21-51-11-420-005
(2) Install the union [17] on the standby temperature control valve [1], do these steps:
(a) Install a new packing [18] on the union [17].
(b) Apply a thin layer of Pure Nickel Special compound, D00006, to the threads of the
union [17].
(c) Install the union [17] on the standby temperature control valve [1].
SUBTASK 21-51-11-160-002
(3) Carefully put the standby temperature control valve [1] into its position between the air ducts.
SUBTASK 21-51-11-020-007
(4) Install the clamps [8] that hold the valve to the ducts.
(a) Do not fully tighten the clamps.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
SUBTASK 21-51-11-420-002
(5) Do these steps to connect the bonding jumper to the valve:
(a) Put the bonding jumper [2] in its position on the standby temperature control valve [1].
(b) Install the screw [14], washer [13], and nut [12] that hold the bonding jumper [2] to the
valve.
1) Make sure that the bonding jumper [2], screw [14], washer [13], and nut [12] are
clean.
SUBTASK 21-51-11-420-003
(6) Install the electrical connector [3] on the standby temperature control valve [1].
SUBTASK 21-51-11-020-008
(7) To connect the four sense lines to the standby temperature control valve, do these steps:
(a) Make sure that the condenser inlet pressure sense line [10], ACM turbine muffler sense
line [4], condenser outlet pressure sense line [9], and conditioned air check valve sense
line [11] are installed in the positions they were before the removal.
(b) Install the condenser inlet pressure sense line [10].
(c) Install the ACM turbine muffler sense line [4].
(d) Install the condenser outlet pressure sense line [9].
(e) Install the conditioned air check valve sense line [11].
(f) Align the three sense line clamps and wire bundle clamp with the spacer plate nut on the
structure.
(g) Install the screw [15] and washer [16] that hold clamps to the spacer plate nut.
(h) Align the two sense line clamps and wire bundle clamp.
(i) Install the screw [5], washer [6], and nut [7] that hold the clamps together.
SUBTASK 21-51-11-420-004
(8) Tighten the clamps [8] to 55 in-lb (6.2 N·m) - 60 in-lb (6.8 N·m).
(a) Make sure that the loop bands do not touch.

21-51-11-710-801Standby Temperature Control Valve Primary Pneumatic Control - Operation CheckPDF p. 1137
2. Standby Temperature Control Valve Primary Pneumatic Control - Operation Check
A. General
(1) The primary function of the Standby Temperature Control Valve (STCV) is to monitor the
differential pressure between the inlet and outlet of the High Pressure Water Separator
(HPWS)'s Condenser and the Air Cycle Machine (ACM)'s Turbine Outlet and Condition Air
Check Valve. This task will make sure that the primary pneumatic control of the STCV is
working properly.
B. References
Reference Title
21-51-11-000-801 Standby Temperature Control Valve Removal (P/B 401)
21-51-11-400-801 Standby Temperature Control Valve Installation (P/B 401)
C. Tools/Equipment
NOTE: When more than one tool part number is listed under the same "Reference" number, the
tools shown are alternates to each other within the same airplane series. Tool part numbers
that are replaced or non-procurable are preceded by "Opt:", which stands for Optional.
Reference Description
SPL-21786 Standby Temperature Control Valve (STCV) Test Equipment
Part #: C21013-1 Supplier: 81205
STD-1290 Source - Nitrogen, 0-200 PSIG

SUBTASK 21-51-12-020-005
(1) Remove the water extractor drain lines and manifold, do these steps:

clamps [48].

SUBTASK 21-51-12-020-006

assembly.

EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
SUBTASK 21-51-12-020-007

SUBTASK 21-51-12-020-008
(4) Remove the plug [56] and packing [57] from the condenser [55].
(a) Discard the packing [57].
SUBTASK 21-51-12-480-002

SUBTASK 21-51-12-480-006
(1) Remove the duct and line covers.
SUBTASK 21-51-12-020-021
(2) Install the plug [56], do these steps:
(a) Apply a thin coat of one of these lubricants to the new packing [57].
1) Braycote Micronic 601EF grease, D50380
2) Braycote 601EF Grease, D50203
3) Braycote 815Z lubricant, D50268
4) Fluorolube GR-660 lubricant, D00548
5) Braycote 1729 grease, D50389
6) Krytox 240AB grease, D50234
7) Krytox 240AZ grease, D50233

SUBTASK 21-51-12-020-022
(3) Install the coupling [59], do these steps:
(a) Apply a thin coat of Molykote 44 grease, medium, D50104, to the new packings [58].
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(b) Install the packings [58] on the coupling [59].
(c) Install the coupling [59] in the duct of the reheater.
SUBTASK 21-51-12-020-023
(4) Install the condenser [55] on the frame assembly, do these steps:
(a) Put the condenser [55] in its position in the frame assembly.
(b) While the condenser [55] is put in the frame assembly, do these steps:
1) Move the hoses on the water extractors over the ducts on the condenser [55].
CAUTION
DO NOT CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE PACKING AT THE COUPLING
DURING CONDENSER INSTALLATION. THE DUCT OF THE
CONDENSER SETS ON THE COUPLING. DAMAGE TO THE
PACKING CAN CAUSE AIR LEAKS.
2) Put the duct of the condenser [55] over the coupling [59].
(c) Install the bolts [52] and washers [53].
(d) Install the bolt [44] and washers [43] that connect the condenser [55] to the support
assembly.
1) Make sure that one of the washers [43] is installed between the condenser [55] and
the support assembly.
(e) Install the clamps [42] on the water extractor hoses.
SUBTASK 21-51-12-020-024
(5) Install the water extractor drain lines and manifold, do these steps:
(a) Move the six hoses over the drain line ports of the water extractors.
(b) Install the screws [51], washers [50], and shim [49] that hold the manifold to the
condenser [55].
1) If a replacement manifold is installed, make sure to remove the plastic plug from the
overflow port of the water collection manifold.
(c) Install the clamps [41] that connect the drain line hoses to the water extractors.
(d) Put the drain line support clamps [48] on the condenser ducts.
(e) Align the drain line support clamps [48] with the clamp on the water extractor drain line.
(f) Install the screws [45], washers [46], and nuts [47] that connect the drain line support
clamps [48].
SUBTASK 21-51-12-410-003
(6) Do this task: High Pressure Water Separator Installation, TASK 21-51-08-400-802.

SUBTASK 21-51-13-480-003

(b) Put the packings [48] in their positions on the ducts.

F. Reheater Installation Test
SUBTASK 21-51-13-860-003
WARNING
MAKE SURE THAT PERSONNEL ARE CLEAR OF THE RAM AIR INLET AND
EXIT DOORS, LINKAGES AND ACTUATORS BEFORE YOU DO THIS TEST.
POSSIBLE INJURY TO PERSONNEL CAN OCCUR.
(1) Do this task: Supply Electrical Power, TASK 24-22-00-860-811.
SUBTASK 21-51-13-780-001
(2) To prepare for a leak check of the reheater [49] installation, do one of these steps, (a) or (b):
(a) Supply pneumatic pressure to the packs with the Auxiliary Power Unit (APU) as follows:
1) Supply pressure to the pneumatic system with the APU (TASK 36-00-00-860-803).
2) Make sure that the aft outflow valve and a passenger door are open.
3) Set the applicable L PACK or R PACK switch, on the P5-10 air conditioning panel,
to the AUTO position.
(b) Supply pneumatic pressure to the packs with an engine as follows:
1) Supply pressure to the pneumatic system with one or both engines
(TASK 36-00-00-860-804).
2) Make sure that the aft outflow valve and a passenger door are open.
3) Set the applicable L PACK or R PACK switch, on the P5-10 air conditioning panel,
to the AUTO position.
SUBTASK 21-51-13-790-001
(3) Do a soap bubble test of all the applicable duct joints.
NOTE: No leakage is permitted.
(a) If there is leakage, do these steps:
1) Put the L PACK and R PACK switches in the OFF position.
WARNING
DO NOT TOUCH THE COOLING PACK DUCTS WHEN THEY ARE
HOT. THE COOLING PACK DUCTS CAN BE HOT AND CAN CAUSE
INJURY TO PERSONS.

3) Set the applicable L PACK or R PACK switch, on the P5-10 air conditioning panel,
to the AUTO position.
(b) Supply pneumatic pressure to the packs with an engine as follows:
1) Supply pressure to the pneumatic system with one or both engines
(TASK 36-00-00-860-804).

3) Set the applicable L PACK or R PACK switch, on the P5-10 air conditioning panel,
to the AUTO position.

NOTE: No leakage is permitted.
(a) If there is leakage, do these steps:

 ALL

F. Water Spray Nozzle Installation
SUBTASK 21-51-16-420-001
(1) To install the water spray nozzle, do these steps:
(a) Put the water spray nozzle [1] in its position.
(b) Install the bolts [11], washers [8], and nuts [7].
SUBTASK 21-51-16-020-004
(2) To connect the water line to the water spray nozzle, do these steps:
(a) Install a new O-ring [6] on the union [5].
(b) Apply a thin layer of Pure Nickel Special compound, D00006, to the threads of the
union [5].
(c) Install the union [5] on the water spray nozzle.
(d) Connect the water line to the water spray nozzle.
SUBTASK 21-51-16-020-005
(3) To connect the air line to the water spray nozzle, do these steps:
(a) Install a new O-ring [9] on the union [10].
(b) Apply a thin layer of Pure Nickel Special compound, D00006, to the threads of the
union [10].
(c) Install the union [10] on the water spray nozzle.
(d) Connect the air line to the water spray nozzle.

H. Water Spray Nozzle Check
SUBTASK 21-51-16-860-021
(1) Do this task: Supply Pressure to the Pneumatic System with the APU,
TASK 36-00-00-860-803.
SUBTASK 21-51-16-860-012
(2) Set the L(R) PACK switches, on the P5-10 overhead panel, to the HIGH position.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
SUBTASK 21-51-16-860-013
(3) Set the trim air switch to the ON position.
SUBTASK 21-51-16-860-014
(4) Set the CONT CAB, FWD CAB, and AFT CAB zone temperature selectors to the AUTO-C
(fully cold) position.
SUBTASK 21-51-16-210-001
(5) Use a flashlight to see that a spray of air and water comes of the L(R) water spray nozzle.
NOTE: The quantity of water is a function of the air humidity and the pack air flow.
(a) Make sure that the water spray pattern from each spray nozzle is approximately the
same.
(b) Make sure that the water sprays are approximately circular and are continuous.
(c) If the water sprays are not satisfactory, do the following steps to examine these parts for
leakage or blockage:
1) The water collector manifold
2) The water extractor
3) The water extractor duct
4) The water spray nozzle
5) The air and water supply lines from the water extractor to the water spray nozzle.
SUBTASK 21-51-16-860-015
(6) Set the L(R) PACK switches to the OFF position.
SUBTASK 21-51-16-210-002
(7) Check the water collection manifold for leakage or blockage.
(a) Disconnect the water output port line [2] at the water collection manifold.
(b) Set the L(R) PACK switches, on the P5-10 overhead panel, to the HIGH position.
(c) Feel for air or water to come out of the hole in the water collection manifold where you
removed the line.
(d) If there is no air or water, examine the water collection manifold for leakage or blockage.
SUBTASK 21-51-16-420-002
(8) Connect the water output port line [2] at the water collection manifold.
SUBTASK 21-51-16-860-016
(9) Set the L(R) PACK switches to the OFF position.
SUBTASK 21-51-16-210-003
(10) Check the water extractor for leakage or blockage.
(a) Disconnect the water drain lines [1] at each water drain nipple of the water extractors.
(b) Set the L(R) PACK switches, on the P5-10 overhead panel, to the HIGH position.
(c) Feel for air or water to come out of the hole in the water extractor where you removed the
line.
(d) If there is no air or water, examine the water extractor for leakage or blockage.
SUBTASK 21-51-16-420-003
(11) Connect the water drain lines [1] at each water drain nipple of the water extractors.
SUBTASK 21-51-16-860-017
(12) Set the L(R) PACK switches to the OFF position.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
SUBTASK 21-51-16-210-004
(13) Check the water extractor duct for leakage or blockage.
(a) Disconnect the drain line [3] at the water extractor duct.
(b) Set the L(R) PACK switches, on the P5-10 overhead panel, to the HIGH position.
(c) Feel for air or water to come out of the hole in the water extractor duct where you
removed the line.
(d) If there is no air or water, examine the water extractor duct for leakage or blockage.
SUBTASK 21-51-16-420-004
(14) Connect the drain line [3] at the water extractor duct.
SUBTASK 21-51-16-110-001
(15) If the water spray nozzle is blocked or clogged, do the steps that follow to clean the nozzle:
(a) Remove the nozzle from the airplane, do this task: Water Spray Nozzle Removal,
TASK 21-51-16-000-801.
(b) Soak the nozzle assembly in solvent degreasing solvent, B50126.
(c) Use compressed air to blow out loose particles from the nozzle.
(d) Do steps (b) and (c) again if necessary to clean the inner areas of the nozzle.
(e) Use a soft bristle brush, STD-123, to remove external particles from the nozzle.
(f) Soak the nozzle in general detergent, B50117, and water, G50256, to remove the solvent.
(g) Dry the nozzle with compressed air.
(h) Examine the nozzle to make sure that there is no external damage.
(i) Use a low pressure air source of between to 0.5 psi (34.5 mBar) - 1 psi (69 mBar) to blow
air through the nozzle.
1) Make sure that air flows freely through the air inlet and water inlet.
(j) Install the nozzle, do this task: Water Spray Nozzle Installation, TASK 21-51-16-400-801.

CAN FALL WHEN THE CLAMP IS LOOSE. THE MIX MUFF CAN BE
DAMAGED IF IT FALLS.
(e) Loosen the clamp [11] that attaches the mix muff [16] to the air cycle machine.
(f) Remove the mix muff [16].
(g) Remove and discard the O-ring [12].

SUBTASK 21-51-17-020-003
(2) To install the mix muff [16], do these steps:
(a) Lubricate the new O-ring [12] with lubricant, D00602.
(b) Install the new O-ring [12].
(c) Put the mix muff [16] into its position between the ducts.
1) Hold the mix muff [16] in position when you install the clamps.
NOTE: The duct connections are not self aligning.
(d) Install the clamp [11] that holds the mix muff [16] to the air cycle machine.
1) Do not fully tighten the clamp [11].
(e) Install the clamp [13] that holds the mix muff [16] to the temperature control duct.
1) Do not fully tighten the clamp [13].
(f) Move the flexible duct [15] on the mix muff [16].
(g) Install the clamps [14] on the flexible duct [15].
1) Tighten the clamps [14] to 13 in-lb (1.5 N·m) - 17 in-lb (1.9 N·m).
(h) Tighten the clamp [11] and clamp [13] to 60 in-lb (6.8 N·m) - 65 in-lb (7.3 N·m).
1) Make sure that the loop bands do not touch.

G. Compressor Outlet Duct Installation
SUBTASK 21-51-17-020-004
(1) To install the compressor outlet duct [3], do these steps:
(a) Apply a light coat grease, D00504, or Molykote 44 grease, medium, D50104, to the
O-ring [5] and O-rings [8].
(b) Install the new O-ring [5].
(c) Install the new O-rings [8] on the duct ends.
(d) Put the compressor outlet duct [3] into its position.
1) Hold the compressor outlet duct [3] in position when you install the clamps.
NOTE: The duct connections are not self aligning.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(e) Apply compound, D50320, to the bolt threads of the clamp [4].
(f) Install the clamp [4] that holds the compressor outlet duct [3] to the heat exchanger.
1) Do not fully tighten the clamp [4].
(g) Move the sleeve [7] over the duct ends.
(h) Install the clamshell clamp [6].
1) Push the two halves of the clamshell clamp [6] together until the three latch pawls
are latched.
(i) Tighten the clamp [4] to 45 in-lb (5.1 N·m) - 50 in-lb (5.6 N·m).
(j) With hand force, gently push the compressor outlet duct in the direction of the adjacent
mix muff duct until the compressor outlet duct reaches the maximum flexed position.
(k) Make sure that there is a minimum clearance of 0.20 in. (5.1 mm) to the adjacent mix
muff duct when the compressor outlet duct is in the flexed position.
(l) Install the electrical connector [2] on the ram air control temperature sensor.
(m) Install the electrical connector [1] on the compressor outlet overheat switch.
(n) Apply a light coating of Pure Nickel Special compound, D00006, to the threads of the
hose [9].
(o) Reconnect the hose [9] to the compressor outlet duct [3].

(1) Install the ram air inlet actuator [15] as follows:

(b) Attach the actuator [15] to the support [18] as follows:
1) Make sure that the bushings [28] are installed in the support [18].
2) Install the bolt [17], washer [16], washer [9], and nut [12]:
a) Put the countersunk side of the washer [16] under the head of the bolt [17].
(c) Install the bonding jumper [5] to the ground tab [19] on the actuator [15] as follows:
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
 315-317, 322-341, 343, 346-999
1) Clean the mating surfaces of the screw [1], washer [3], washers [4], nut [6], and
ground tab [19] as follows:
a) Use a sealant removal tool, COM-2481, and sealant removal tool handle,
COM-4746, to remove the majority of the adhesive.
b) Use a cotton wiper, G00034, soaked in solvent, B00666, solvent, B00184, or
solvent, B00148, until all the adhesive is removed as follows:
<1> Pour the solvent onto the wiper to avoid contamination of the solvent
container.
<2> Wipe or scrub the surface to be cleaned with the solvent soaked wiper.
<3> Immediately wipe the cleaned surfaces with a clean cotton wiper,
G00034.
c) Use a clean cotton wiper, G00034, to remove all excess solvent that may
remain on the parts.
d) Repeat the cleaning action until no discoloration shows on the wiper.
e) Dry surface before the solvent evaporates.
2) Install the screw [1], washer [3], bonding jumper [5], washers [4], and nut [6] to the
ground tab [19].
NOTE: It is permissible to install the bonding jumper terminal on both sides of the
ground tab with the fastener head and nut in both directions.

F. Ram Air Inlet Deflector Door Installation
SUBTASK 21-51-22-420-001
(1) Put the ram air inlet deflector door [1] in its position.
SUBTASK 21-51-22-420-002
(2) Install the bolts [2] and the washers [3] that attach the hinge of ram air inlet deflector door [1] to
the airplane.
SUBTASK 21-51-22-100-001
(3) Prepare the mating surfaces (SWPM 20-20-00).
(a) Do abrasive cleaning procedure for mating surface of deflector door [1], washers [6], and
bonding jumper [7].
(b) Do the solvent cleaning procedure for the mating surfaces of the terminal of deflector
door [1], washers [6], and bonding jumper [7].
SUBTASK 21-51-22-420-003
(4) Do the steps that follow to install the bonding jumper [7]:
(a) Install the washer [6].
(b) Put the bonding jumper [7] in its position and install the screw [4].
(c) Tighten the screw [4] to 32 in-lb (3.6 N·m) - 38 in-lb (4.3 N·m).
SUBTASK 21-51-22-760-001
(5) Measure the electrical bonding resistance between the bonding jumper [7] and the structure.
(a) Use an intrinsically safe approved bonding meter, COM-1550.
(b) Make sure that the electrical bounding resistance is not greater than 0.001 ohms (1
milliohms).
SUBTASK 21-51-22-640-001
(6) Apply PR-1776M Class B Sealant, A50345, on the terminal of bonding jumper [7], washer [6],
and screw [4].
SUBTASK 21-51-22-420-004
(7) Install the bolt [9], washer [10], washer [8], and nut [11] that attach the ram air inlet deflector
door [1] to the links.
(a) Make sure that the spring is in its position on the support assembly and around the
inboard link (Figure 401).
(b) Make sure that the links are in the correct positions (View A-A, Figure 401).
SUBTASK 21-51-22-820-004
(8) If it is necessary, adjust the air inlet deflector door [1] (TASK 21-51-22-400-803).

F. Ram Air Inlet Deflector Door Shaft Assembly Installation
SUBTASK 21-51-22-420-005
(1) Do these steps to install the shaft [48]:
NOTE: You must remove the link [49] from the shaft assembly before you can install the
shaft [48] into the ram air inlet.
(a) Remove the nut [33], washer [32], and bolt [31], that attach the links [49] to the shaft [48].
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(b) Remove the links [49] from the shaft [48].
(c) Put the links [49] in their positions.
1) Make sure that the inboard and outboard links are opposite for the left and right
side.
NOTE: The circular edge of each link should point down after the installation.
(d) Do a abrasive clearing procedure for surfaces contacting mating parts, shafts and
crankarms or collars (TASK 20-10-34-120-801).
(e) Do a solvent clearing procedure for surfaces contacting mating parts, shafts and
crankarms or collars (TASK 20-10-34-110-802).
(f) Apply Loctite 7471 Primer T Activator, A50086, and Loctite 641 compound, A50463, to
surfaces contacting mating parts, shafts and crankarms or collars.
1) Air dry primer/activator for five minutes minimum prior to the application of retaining
compounds.
2) Cover locking surfaces with retaining compound by a continuous fillet visible at the
parting line of the assembled joint.
a) Remove excess material.
3) Do not move joined parts to handling, vibration or shock until cured.
4) Cure parts for one hour, if temperature is or more than 70°F (21°C).
a) Cure parts for 72 hours, if temperature is 40°F (4°C) - 70°F (21°C).
NOTE: Locking materials do not cure sufficiently at temperatures below 40°F
(4°C).
(g) Install the bushing [47], washer [35], bolt [36], and washer [35].
1) Make sure that the links [49] are in the correct positions (View A-A, Figure 402).
(h) While you hold the links [49], insert the shaft [48] into the ram air inlet in an outboard
through the spring [50] and the holes in the top ends of the links [49].
1) Make sure that you insert the shaft [48] so that the end without the hole goes in first.
(i) Install the bolt [31], washer [32], and nut [33] that attach the links [49] to the shaft [48].
(j) Make sure that the spring [50] is in its position on the support assembly and around the
inboard link.
1) Make sure that shaft assembly rotates freely and not bind.
CAUTION
DO NOT LUBRICATE THE BEARING WITH GREASE OR WD-40. IF YOU
LUBRICATE, THE BEARING LINER CAN SWELL, DECREASING THE
CLEARANCE AND LEADING TO INCREASED ROTATIONAL BREAK￾AWAY TORQUE.
(k) Install the bolts [54], washers [52], and nuts [51] that attach the bearing support
assembly [53] and spring [50] to the support assembly.
SUBTASK 21-51-22-420-025
(2) Do these steps to install the arm assembly [40]:
(a) Put the arm assembly [40] in its position on the end of the shaft [48].
(b) Install the bolt [38], washer [39], washer [43], and nut [44].
(c) Put the link extension [37] in its position and install the bolt [42], washer [41], washer [45],
and nut [46].
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
SUBTASK 21-51-22-820-005
(3) If it is necessary, adjust the air inlet deflector door (TASK 21-51-22-400-803).

to the arm [2] on the deflector door shaft assembly [16].
(d) Adjust the length of the tie rod assembly [1] until the over-travel stop on either the inboard
or outboard link [25] just touches the applicable inboard or outboard clevis [26].

EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
1) Rotate the rod [14] one full turn in the shortening direction.

follows (View A-A, Figure 501):
1) Apply the force through the axis of the bolt in a plane approximately parallel to the
surface of the ram air inlet deflector door.
(g) As you apply the force, make sure that the smaller of the two gaps (either inboard or
outboard) measures 0.010 in. (0.25 mm) - 0.03 in. (0.76 mm) between the over-travel
arm of the link [25] and clevis [26] (View A-A, Figure 501).
NOTE: The gaps at the inboard and outboard links may be different.
(h) If the smaller gap is not within 0.010 in. (0.25 mm) - 0.03 in. (0.76 mm), adjust the tie rod
assembly [1] in 1/4 turn increments until you get the specified gap.

2. Ram Air Inlet Door Linkage Inspection
(Figure 601)
A. General
(1) This task has the steps to inspect the ram air inlet door linkage inspection.
B. References
Reference Title

21-51-21-400-801 Ram Air Inlet Actuator Installation (P/B 401)
C. Tools/Equipment
Reference Description
STD-7173 Gage - Force, 0-50 lbs. capacity
D. Prepare for the Inspection
SUBTASK 21-51-22-020-030
(1) Disconnect the actuator from the arm assembly [31] (TASK 21-51-21-000-801).
E. Ram Air Inlet Door Linkage Inspection
SUBTASK 21-51-22-710-001
(1) Use a force gage, STD-7173, to check the bearings in the ram air inlet door linkages assembly.
(a) Connect the force gage, STD-7173, to the arm assembly [31].
(b) Pull the force gage, STD-7173, to rotate the arm assembly [31].
1) Make sure that the direction of the force is perpendicular to the arm assembly [31].
(c) Record the initial force (lbf or N) required to move the ram air inlet linkage assembly and
share the results with .
NOTE: Although a maximum force required has not yet been determined, preliminary
data shows that an initial force over 20 lbf (89 N), may indicate that the
self-lubricating bearings within the ram air inlet linkage assembly may be
degraded.
F. Put the Airplane Back to Its Usual Condition
SUBTASK 21-51-22-420-026
(1) Connect the actuator to the arm assembly [31] (TASK 21-51-21-400-801).

E. Ram Air Inlet Modulation Panels Removal
NOTE: The ram air inlet modulation panels have a forward panel and an aft panel. It is necessary to
remove the forward panel before you can remove the aft panel.
SUBTASK 21-51-23-020-001
(1) Remove the forward modulation panel [1] as follows:
(a) Remove the bolts [3] that attach the forward end of the aft modulation panel [2] to the aft
end of the forward modulation panel [1].
NOTE: Let the forward modulation panel come down. This will permit access to the bolts
and washers that attach the forward end of the forward modulation panel to the
ram air inlet forward fairing support.
(b) Hold the panel while removing bolts and washers. After the last bolt is removed the
forward panel will fall out of the airplane.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(c) Remove the bolts [4] and washers [5] from the forward hinge on the forward modulation
panel [1].
CAUTION
MAKE SURE THAT YOU HOLD THE PANEL WHEN YOU REMOVE BOLTS
AND WASHERS. IF YOU DO NOT OBEY, THE FORWARD PANEL WILL
FALL OUT OF THE AIRPLANE WHEN YOU REMOVE THE LAST BOLT.
(d) Remove the forward modulation panel [1] from the ram air inlet.
SUBTASK 21-51-23-020-002
(2) Remove the aft modulation panel [2] as follows:
(a) If it is necessary, disconnect the ram air inlet actuator arm from the shaft of the aft
modulation panel [2] (TASK 21-51-21-000-801).
(b) Disconnect the clevis assemblies [8] from the aft modulation panel [2]:
1) Remove the nut [12], washers [10], bushing [11], and bolt [9] that connect each
clevis assembly [8] to the aft modulation panel [2].
(c) Pull the aft modulation panel [2] out of the ram air inlet.

jumper.

bonding jumper [30], and washer [31].

(e) Install the bolts [43] and washers [44], do these steps:

the transition duct [2], bolts [43], and washers [44].
2) Apply coating, C00767, to the transition duct [2] surface.
a) Make sure that the new anti-static coating overlapping the original anti-static
coating by a minimum of 0.10 in. (2.54 mm).
b) Let coating, C00767, air dry for a minimum of 20 minutes.
3) Install the bolts [43] and washers [44].
4) Measure the electrical bonding resistance between the bolts [43] and anti-static
coating of the transition duct [2] (SWPM 20-20-00).
a) Use a digital/analog multimeter, COM-1793.
b) Make sure that the electrical bonding resistance is 300,000 ohm or less.
c) The measurement point on the duct surface must be more than 0.25 in.
(6.35 mm) away from the bolt [43].
d) If it is necessary, remove a small area of the surface finish to get access to the
anti-static coating of the transition duct [2].
e) If the resistance measurement is not satisfactory, disassemble the bonding
connection, clean the mating surfaces, and repeat the bonding connection
installation.
f) If it is necessary, put a thin coating of primer, C00766, on the surface of the
transition duct [2] after the measurement is completed.

21-51-24-340-801Resin Damage - Fiberglass DuctsPDF p. 1323
2. Resin Damage - Fiberglass Ducts
A. General
(1) This procedure gives instructions for the repair of a fiberglass ram air duct with an application
of resin.
(2) A resin damage repair is applicable when there are no holes or punctures in the ram air duct
but one of these defects are present:
(a) Exposed fibers
(b) Soft areas from impact damage
(c) Delamination
(d) Loss of resin or voids

SUBTASK 21-51-24-860-009

Removal, TASK 21-51-24-000-801
SUBTASK 21-51-24-840-002
(3) Do these steps to prepare the damaged area of the duct:
WARNING
DO NOT GET METHYL ETHYL KETONE (MEK) IN YOUR MOUTH OR
EYES, OR ON YOUR SKIN. DO NOT BREATHE THE FUMES FROM MEK.
PUT ON A PROTECTIVE SPLASH GOGGLE AND GLOVES WHEN YOU
USE MEK. KEEP MEK AWAY FROM SPARKS, FLAME AND HEAT. MEK IS
A POISONOUS AND FLAMMABLE SOLVENT WHICH CAN CAUSE
INJURIES TO PERSONS OR DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT.
(a) Use the solvent, B00148 and a cotton wiper, G00034 to clean the duct repair area.
(b) Sand the damaged area to remove any unwanted contamination from the duct.
(c) Use the solvent, B00148 and a cotton wiper, G00034 to clean the duct joint area.
SUBTASK 21-51-24-840-003
(4) Prepare the applicable resin:
(a) Ram air inlet duct repair - resin, G50400
(b) Ram air exhaust duct repair - resin, G02451
F. Repair the Air Conditioning Duct
SUBTASK 21-51-24-340-001
(1) Use resin, G50400 to repair the damaged area of the ram air inlet duct:
(a) Use a brush, STD-122 or hypodermic syringe, STD-854 to apply the resin to the
damaged area of the duct.
(b) Apply a thin, smooth layer of the resin to the damaged area of the duct.
(c) Put a piece of solid parting film, G50104 on the duct and press lightly to remove any
bubbles or any wrinkles and to remove unwanted resin.
(d) Remove the solid parting film, G50104 from the duct and remove any unwanted resin
with a wiping cloth.
(e) Do one of these steps to cure the resin:
1) Permit the resin, G50400 to cure for a minimum of 30 minutes at 150°, ± 10° F.
2) Permit the resin, G50400 to cure for 24 hours at room temperature (70° F
minimum).
SUBTASK 21-51-24-340-002
(2) Use resin, G02451 to repair the damaged area of the ram air exhaust duct.
(a) Use a brush, STD-122 or hypodermic syringe, STD-854 to apply the resin to the
damaged area of the duct.
(b) Apply a thin, smooth layer of the resin to the damaged area of the duct.

bubbles or any wrinkles and to remove unwanted resin.

21-51-24-340-803Structural Repair - Fiberglass DuctsPDF p. 1331
4. Structural Repair - Fiberglass Ducts
(Figure 801)
A. General
(1) This procedure gives instructions for making a structural repair to a fiberglass air conditioning
duct.
(2) A structural repair is applicable when the damage to the air conditioning duct is a cut or a hole
that is more than 0.25 in. (6.35 mm) wide and more than 3 in. (76.2 mm) long but less than 5
percent of the total surface area of the duct. If the damage is more than 5 percent of the total
surface area of the duct, then replace the duct section.

(a) Attach a vacuum bag, STD-94, to hold the repair layers and to keep the duct shape.
1) Allow the resin to cure for 24 hours at 75 ±5°F (24 ±3°C).
2) Cure for a minimum of 2 - 2.5 hours under a minimum of 20 in/Hg (68 kPa) at
170 ±10°F (77 ±6°C).
NOTE: Moisture protection is not necessary during 170 ±10°F (77 ±6°C) cure.
SUBTASK 21-51-24-340-041
(11) To cure resin, G02451, do these steps (SRM 51-30-10):
(a) Attach a vacuum bag, STD-94, to hold the repair layers and to keep the duct shape.
1) Cure for a minimum of 3 hours under a minimum of 22 in/Hg (75 kPa) at 150 ±5°F
(66 ±3°C).
2) Decrease the temperature at a maximum rate of 5°F (3°C) for each minute.
3) Below 125°F (52°C), remove the vacuum bag, STD-94, without damage to the
cured layers.
SUBTASK 21-51-24-340-038
(12) If necessary, sand the patch on the outer duct surface to get a correct fit.
(a) Keep a wall thickness of 0.045 in. (1.143 mm) - 0.065 in. (1.651 mm) in this area.
NOTE: Wrinkles, creases, and unwanted resin are not permitted in this area. Sand these
items flush where necessary.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
SUBTASK 21-51-24-340-039
(13) Use a brush, STD-122, to seal exposed fabric with a layer of resin.
SUBTASK 21-51-24-340-040
(14) Let the resin cure.
SUBTASK 21-51-24-840-014
(15) Remove the solid parting film, G50104, the cardboard or aluminum, and the adhesive tape you
used to support the repair.

CAUTION
MAKE SURE TO FOLLOW THE STEPS TO ADJUST THE LOUVERS TO THE
