SUBTASK 21-51-27-820-002
(9) Do one of the following steps to set the louvers to the flight fully closed position:
NOTE: The preferred steps use rigging clips. The alternate steps use non-metallic shims.
(a) Use rigging clips of gap tool, SPL-20203, to set the louvers to the flight fully closed
position as follows (Figure 402):
1) Move the actuator drive arm [16] to turn the exhaust louvers until a rigging clip can
be inserted on the forward and mid louvers.
2) Insert one rigging clip on the forward louver, and insert another rigging clip on the
mid louver.
3) Position the rigging clips with slight separation between them.
4) Manually turn the louvers to the closed position until one of the rigging clips touches
the adjacent louver.
NOTE: This position of the exhaust louvers is the flight fully closed position with the
louvers set at approximately 12 degrees.
5) Make sure that the rigging clip that touched the adjacent louver does not become
loose or fall out during the connection of the actuator rod end [17] to the actuator
drive arm [16].
(b) Use non-metallic shims of gap tool, SPL-20203, or non-metallic shims, G51239, to set
the louvers to the flight fully closed position as follows (Figure 403):
NOTE: Non-metallic shims can be machined or sanded to get a completed dimension of
0.680 ±0.010 in. (17.272 ±0.254 mm) thick x 7 in. (177.8 mm) long x 2 in.
(50.8 mm) wide. Multiple thinner laminations can be bonded together to get the
correct thickness.

1) Move the actuator drive arm [16] to turn the exhaust louvers until a shim
(0.680 ±0.010 in. (17.272 ±0.254 mm) thick x 7 in. (177.8 mm) long x 2 in.
(50.8 mm) wide) can be inserted between each pair of louvers.
2) Insert one shim between the forward and mid louvers, and insert another shim
between the mid and aft louvers.
3) Position the shims with slight separation between them.
4) Manually turn the louvers to the closed position until one of the shims is caught
between the louvers.
NOTE: This position of the exhaust louvers is the flight fully closed position with the
louvers set at approximately 12 degrees.
5) Make sure that the shim that was caught between the louvers does not become
loose or fall out during the connection of the actuator rod end [17] to the actuator
drive arm [16].

SUBTASK 21-51-27-020-011
(1) Disconnect the rod end [17] of the actuator from the Link - Stowage SRADA, SPL-14767, as

(a) Remove the locknut, washers, and bolt that retain the rod end [17] to the Link - Stowage

SUBTASK 21-51-27-020-012
(2) Disconnect the Link - Stowage SRADA, SPL-14767, from the actuator drive arm [16] as
follows:

retain the Link - Stowage SRADA, SPL-14767, to the actuator drive arm [16].
SUBTASK 21-51-27-020-013
(3) Remove the Link - Stowage SRADA, SPL-14767.
I. Exit Louvers Reactivation
SUBTASK 21-51-27-020-014
(1) Remove the nut, washers, and bolt that attach the most forward louver drive arm to the most
forward hole in the link assembly.
SUBTASK 21-51-27-420-009
(2) Move the link assembly until the hole in the most forward louver drive arm aligns with the
second most forward hole in the link assembly.
EFFECTIVITY
 349-999
SUBTASK 21-51-27-420-010
(3) In the same order that they were just removed, install the bolt, washers, and nut through the
hole in the most forward louver drive arm and the second most forward hole in the link
assembly.
J. Ram Air Exhaust Actuator Rod End Reconnect and Adjustment
SUBTASK 21-51-27-860-018
(1) Make sure that the rod end [17] of the SRADA [2] is not attached to the actuator drive arm [16].
SUBTASK 21-51-27-860-019
(2) Extend the trailing edge flaps to position 1, do this task: Extend the Trailing Edge Flaps,
TASK 27-51-00-860-803.
SUBTASK 21-51-27-860-020
(3) Do this task: Put the Airplane in the Air Mode, TASK 32-09-00-860-801.
SUBTASK 21-51-27-860-021
(4) Retract the left and right trailing edge flaps to the flaps fully up position, do this task: Retract
the Trailing Edge Flaps, TASK 27-51-00-860-804.
SUBTASK 21-51-27-820-003
(5) Do one of the following steps to set the louvers to the flight fully closed position:
NOTE: The preferred steps use rigging clips. The alternate steps use non-metallic shims.
(a) Use rigging clips of gap tool, SPL-20203, to set the louvers to the flight fully closed
position as follows (Figure 402):
1) Move the actuator drive arm [16] to turn the exhaust louvers until a rigging clip can
be inserted on the forward and mid louvers.
2) Insert one rigging clip on the forward louver, and insert another rigging clip on the
mid louver.
3) Position the rigging clips with slight separation between them.
4) Manually turn the louvers to the closed position until one of the rigging clips touches
the adjacent louver.
NOTE: This position of the exhaust louvers is the flight fully closed position with the
louvers set at approximately 12 degrees.
5) Make sure that the rigging clip that touched the adjacent louver does not become
loose or fall out during the connection of the actuator rod end [17] to the actuator
drive arm [16].
(b) Use non-metallic shims of gap tool, SPL-20203, or non-metallic shims, G51239, to set
the louvers to the flight fully closed position as follows (Figure 403):
NOTE: Non-metallic shims can be machined or sanded to get a completed dimension of
0.680 ±0.010 in. (17.272 ±0.254 mm) thick x 7 in. (177.8 mm) long x 2 in.
(50.8 mm) wide. Multiple thinner laminations can be bonded together to get the
correct thickness.
1) Move the actuator drive arm [16] to turn the exhaust louvers until a shim
(0.680 ±0.010 in. (17.272 ±0.254 mm) thick x 7 in. (177.8 mm) long x 2 in.
(50.8 mm) wide) can be inserted between each pair of louvers.
2) Insert one shim between the forward and mid louvers, and insert another shim
between the mid and aft louvers.
3) Position the shims with slight separation between them.
EFFECTIVITY
 349-999
4) Manually turn the louvers to the closed position until one of the shims is caught
between the louvers.
NOTE: This position of the exhaust louvers is the flight fully closed position with the
louvers set at approximately 12 degrees.
5) Make sure that the shim that was caught between the louvers does not become
loose or fall out during the connection of the actuator rod end [17] to the actuator
drive arm [16].
SUBTASK 21-51-27-420-011
(6) Connect the rod end [17] of the ram air exhaust actuator [2] to the actuator drive arm [16] as
follows:
(a) If the hole in the rod end [17] does not align with the holes in the actuator drive arm [16],
do these steps:
1) Remove the lockwire from the jamnut on the rod end [17].
2) Adjust the length of the rod end [17] by ±0.125 in. (3.2 mm) until the holes in the rod
end [17] and actuator drive arm [16] align.
3) Hold the rod end [17] and tighten the jam nut until it is seated against the rod end.
4) Tighten the jamnut to 110 ±10 in-lb (12.4 ±1.1 N·m).
5) Install lockwire to keep the jamnut in position.
(b) Put the countersunk side of the washer [10] under the head of the bolt [9].
(c) Put the bolt [9] through the actuator drive arm [16], bushing [19], rod end [17] of the
actuator drive shaft and the spacer [18] in the inboard direction.
(d) Install the washer [11] and nut [12].
SUBTASK 21-51-27-080-003
(7) Remove the rigging clips of gap tool, SPL-20203, or shims of gap tool, SPL-20203, or shims,
G51239, from the louvers.

 ALL

B. Tools/Equipment

tools shown are alternates to each other within the same airplane series. Tool part numbers
that are replaced or non-procurable are preceded by "Opt:", which stands for Optional.

SPL-1552 Kit - Heater Probes, TEMPCAL
Part #: BH24944-7 Supplier: 98869
SPL-3924 Tester - Thermo Switch, K-Type Thermocouple Switches
Part #: H394R Supplier: 98869
Opt Part #: H294 Supplier: 98869
Opt Part #: H394 SERIES Supplier: 98869
C. Location Zones
Zone Area
192 Lower Wing-To-Body Fairing - Under Wing Box
D. Compressor Discharge Overheat Switch - Functional Test (Method I)
SUBTASK 21-51-40-020-009
(1) Remove the compressor discharge overheat switch, do this task: Compressor Discharge
Overheat Switch Removal, TASK 21-51-40-000-801.
(a) Re-connect the electrical connector to the compressor discharge overheat switch.
SUBTASK 21-51-40-480-003
(2) Prepare K-Type thermocouple switch tester, SPL-3924, and TEMPCAL heater probe kit,
SPL-1552, to test the compressor discharge overheat switch.
NOTE: Use the correct heater probe to test overheat switch part number 572756–1.
SUBTASK 21-51-40-710-013
(3) Use the test equipment to increase the temperature of the compressor discharge overheat
switch as follows:
(a) Set the test temperature on the tester to 370 ±5°F (188 ±3°C).
(b) Increase the test temperature on the tester at a rate of not more than 2°F (1°C) per
minute to 390 ±10°F (199 ±6°C).
(c) Move the tester POWER switch to the ON position.
SUBTASK 21-51-40-710-014
(4) When the temperature reaches 390 ±10°F (199 ±6°C), make sure that these lights come on:
(a) PACK light, on the P5-10 panel.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(b) MASTER CAUTION light, on the pilots' glareshield.
SUBTASK 21-51-40-710-015
(5) Remove the heat from the compressor discharge overheat switch probe.
SUBTASK 21-51-40-710-016
(6) Let the compressor discharge overheat switch probe cool down at a rate of not more than 2°F
(1°C) per minute.
NOTE: The compressor discharge overheat switch will reset when the probe temperature is
350°F (177°C).
SUBTASK 21-51-40-710-017

D. Turbine Inlet Thermal Switch - Functional Test (Method I)
SUBTASK 21-51-41-020-007
(1) Remove the turbine inlet thermal switch, do this task: Turbine Inlet Overheat Switch Removal,
TASK 21-51-41-000-801.
(a) Re-connect the electrical connector to the turbine inlet thermal switch.
SUBTASK 21-51-41-480-002
(2) Prepare the K-Type thermocouple switch tester, SPL-3924, and TEMPCAL heater probe kit,
SPL-1552, to test the turbine inlet thermal switch.
NOTE: Use the correct heater probe to test overheat switch part number 572757–1.
SUBTASK 21-51-41-710-013
(3) Use the test equipment to increase the temperature of the turbine inlet thermal switch as
follows:
(a) Set the test temperature on the tester to 190 ±5°F (88 ±3°C).
(b) Increase the test temperature on the tester at a rate of not more than 2°F (1°C) per
minute to 210 ±10°F (99 ±6°C).
(c) Move the tester POWER switch to the ON position.
SUBTASK 21-51-41-710-014
(4) Make sure that these lights come on, when the temperature of the turbine inlet thermal switch
probe get to 210 ±10°F (99 ±6°C).
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(a) PACK light, on the P5-10 panel.
(b) MASTER CAUTION light, on the pilots' glareshield.
SUBTASK 21-51-41-710-015
(5) Remove the heat from the turbine inlet thermal switch probe.
SUBTASK 21-51-41-710-016
(6) Let the turbine inlet thermal switch probe become cool down at a rate of not more than 2°F
(1°C) per minute.
NOTE: The reset temperature for the turbine inlet thermal switch is 170°F (77°C).
SUBTASK 21-51-41-710-017
(7) Push the TRIP RESET light, on the P5-10 panel.
SUBTASK 21-51-41-710-018
(8) Push the MASTER CAUTION reset button, on the P7 glareshield panel.
SUBTASK 21-51-41-710-019
(9) Make sure that the MASTER CAUTION light goes off.
SUBTASK 21-51-41-420-008
(10) Install the turbine inlet thermal switch, do this task: Turbine Inlet Overheat Switch Installation,
TASK 21-51-41-400-801.

A. General
(1) This task provides instructions to clean the left pack pressure sensor, right pack pressure
sensor, and sense lines.
B. References
Reference Title

D. Prepare for the Cleaning
SUBTASK 21-51-45-000-001
(1) Remove the pack pressure sensor [5].
(a) Do this task: Pack Inlet Pressure Sensor Removal, TASK 21-51-45-000-801.
SUBTASK 21-51-45-000-002
(2) Remove the sense line [6] as follows:
(a) Remove the three clamps [7].
1) Remove the screw [8] and washers [9] that secure the clamps [7] to the structure.
2) Remove the clamps [7].
(b) Disconnect the sense line [6] from the duct connector [10] as follows:
1) Use a second wrench to hold the duct connector [10] when you disconnect the
sense line [6].
(c) Remove the sense line [6].
SUBTASK 21-51-45-000-003
(3) Remove the sense line [12] and sense line [18] as follows:
(a) Remove the clamp [15] and clamps [21].
1) Remove the screw [13], washer [14], screw [19], and washer [20] that secure
clamp [15] and each clamps [21] to the structure.
2) Remove the clamp [15] and clamps [21].
(b) Disconnect the sense line [18] from the duct connector [10] as follows:
1) Use a second wrench to hold the duct connector [10] when you disconnect the
sense line [18].
EFFECTIVITY
 385-999
(c) Remove the sense line [12] and sense line [18].
(d) If it is necessary, disconnect the nut [17] from the union [16] to disconnect sense line [18]
from sense line [12].
E. Pack Inlet Pressure Sensor Sense Line Cleaning
SUBTASK 21-51-45-100-002
(1) If it is necessary, remove any ice buildup in the pack pressure sensor [5].
SUBTASK 21-51-45-100-003
(2) If it is necessary, remove any ice buildup in the sense line with warm water, G50256.
SUBTASK 21-51-45-100-004
(3) Blow air, G02314, through the sense line weep hole [11] with compressed air.
(a) Make sure that there is no debris, dirt, or unwanted materials in the sense line.
F. Put the Airplane Back to Its Usual Condition
SUBTASK 21-51-45-400-001
(1) Install the sense line [6] as follows:
(a) Connect the sense line [6] to the duct connector [10] as follows:
1) Use a second wrench to hold duct connector [10] when you tighten the sense
line [6].
2) Tighten the B-nut on the sense line [6] to 160 in-lb (18 N·m). - 180 in-lb (20 N·m).
(b) Install the clamps [7].
1) Install the clamps [7] with the screws [8] and washers [9].
SUBTASK 21-51-45-400-003
(2) Install the sense line [12] and sense line [18] as follows:
(a) If it was disconnected, reconnect the nut [17] to the union [16].
(b) Connect the sense line [18] to the duct connector [10] as follows:
1) Use a second wrench to hold duct connector [10] when you tighten the sense
line [18].
2) Tighten the B-nut on the sense line [18] to 160 in-lb (18 N·m) - 180 in-lb (20 N·m).
(c) Install the clamp [15] and clamps [21].
1) Install the clamp [15] with the screw [13] and washer [14].
2) Install the clamps [21] with the screws [19] and washers [20].
SUBTASK 21-51-45-400-002
(3) Install the pack pressure sensor [5].
(a) Do this task: Pack Inlet Pressure Sensor Installation, TASK 21-51-45-400-801.
(b) Tighten the B-nuts on the sense line [6] and sense line [12] to 90 in-lb (10 N·m). -
100 in-lb (11 N·m).

SUBTASK 21-51-51-160-001
(1) Remove any foreign material from between the connector pins and around the thermistor
beads as follows:

(b) Use MicroCare fiber wipes, G50637 to remove all traces of the isopropyl alcohol.

E. Resistance Check Procedure
SUBTASK 21-51-51-700-001
(1) Use a digital thermometer, COM-3955 or equivalent, to measure the temperature adjacent to
the applicable mix manifold temperature sensor.
(a) Write down the temperature.
SUBTASK 21-51-51-760-001
(2) Use the digital/analog multimeter, COM-1793 (preferred) to measure resistance between the
following pin connections.
NOTE: An equivalent meter can be used as long as the digital multimeter minimizes
self-heating of the sensor element. The instrument must limit the current through the
sensor to less than 100 microamperes when set to the 10K ohms scale. If you use
resistance measuring instruments without this current-limiting feature you will get an
error in resistance value due to self-heating of the sensor element.
 006, 007, 013, 014, 018-020, 043, 044, 056-063, 067-078, 081, 083-103, 111-114, 121-129, 131,
132, 135, 138-169, 174-179, 182-187, 189-203, 205-209, 212-220, 223, 224, 231-236, 239-298, 301-304,
306, 308, 315-317, 322-341, 343, 346-384
SUBTASK 21-51-51-700-002
(3) For the right mix manifold temperature sensor, measure the resistance from pin A7 to pin B7
on connector D3860A for the right pack/zone temperature controller (WDM 21-51-22).
 385-999
SUBTASK 21-51-51-700-005
(4) For the right mix manifold temperature sensor, measure the resistance from pin F9 to pin F10
on connector D15816B for the right pack/flow temperature controller (WDM 21-51-12).

 ALL

 385-999

SUBTASK 21-51-51-700-004
(7) Write down the resistance in Ohms that you measure.
(a) For the mix manifold temperature sensors, find the temperature on (Figure 501) that is
nearest to the temperature that you wrote down.
(b) Compare the permitted range of resistance for that temperature to the resistance you
wrote down.
(c) If the resistance is out of range, replace the sensor. To replace the sensor,
These are the tasks:
Mix Manifold Temperature Sensor Removal, TASK 21-51-51-000-803,
Mix Manifold Temperature Sensor Installation, TASK 21-51-51-400-802.

C. Preparation for the Resistance Test
SUBTASK 21-51-52-864-001
(1) Do this task: Remove Pressure from the Pneumatic System, TASK 36-00-00-860-806.
SUBTASK 21-51-52-020-005
(2) To do a test of the left pack temperature sensor, remove the left pack/zone temperature
controller as follows:
(a) Do this task: Pack/Zone Temperature Controller - Removal, TASK 21-61-20-000-801 or
Pack Flow Temperature Controller - Removal, TASK 21-61-17-020-801.
SUBTASK 21-51-52-020-006
(3) To do a test of the right pack temperature sensor, remove the right pack/zone temperature
controller as follows:
(a) Do this task: Pack/Zone Temperature Controller - Removal, TASK 21-61-20-000-801 or
Pack Flow Temperature Controller - Removal, TASK 21-61-17-020-801.
SUBTASK 21-51-52-800-001
(4) Decrease the temperature in the pack bay until it agrees with the external ambient
temperature.
D. Sensor Resistance Check Procedure
SUBTASK 21-51-52-700-001
(1) Measure the temperature adjacent to the applicable pack temperature sensor in the pack bay:
(a) Use a digital thermometer, COM-3955 or equivalent, to measure the temperature
adjacent to the applicable pack temperature sensor.
(b) Record the temperature for later use.
SUBTASK 21-51-52-700-002
(2) Use the digital/analog multimeter, COM-1793 (preferred) to measure resistance between
connector pins.
NOTE: Use an equivalent meter only if it gives a minimum quantity of heat to the sensor
element. Make sure that the meter can give a limit of current through the sensor
element of less than 100 microamperes. If the meter gives more than this limit of
current, it could give too much heat to the sensor element. Too much heat on the
sensor element can give an incorrect resistance value.
SUBTASK 21-51-52-700-003
(3) For the Pack Zone Temperature Controller:
(a) Measure the resistances for the left pack zone temperature sensor T471 as follows:
1) Measure the resistance from pin A6 to B6 on connector D3858A for the pack zone
temperature controller (WDM 21-51-12).
2) Measure the resistance from pin D11 to D12 on connector D3860A for the pack
zone temperature controller (WDM 21-51-13).
(b) Measure the resistances for the right pack zone temperature sensor T474 as follows:
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
1) Measure the resistance from pin D11 to D12 on connector D3858A for the pack
zone temperature controller (WDM 21-51-23).
2) Measure the resistance from pin A6 to B6 on connector D3860A for the pack zone
temperature controller (WDM 21-51-22).
SUBTASK 21-51-52-700-004
(4) For the Pack Flow Temperature Controller:
(a) Measure the resistances for the left pack flow temperature sensor T471 as follows:
1) Measure the resistance from pin J9 to J10 on connector D15814B for the pack flow
temp controller (WDM 21-51-12).
2) Measure the resistance from pin 22 to 16 on connector D15816C for the pack flow
temp controller (WDM 21-51-13).
(b) Measure the resistances for the right pack flow temperature sensor T474 as follows:
1) Measure the resistance from pin J9 to J10 on connector D15816B for the pack flow
temp controller (WDM 21-51-12).
2) Measure the resistance from pin 22 to 16 on connector D15814C for the pack flow
temp controller (WDM 21-51-13).
SUBTASK 21-51-52-700-005
(5) Make a record of the resistances for each sensor that you measured.
SUBTASK 21-51-52-700-006
(6) Find the temperature on Figure 501 that is nearest to the temperature that you recorded.
SUBTASK 21-51-52-700-007
(7) Compare the serviceable range of resistance for that temperature to the resistance you
recorded.
(a) The serviceable range of resistance is between the two parallel lines on the graph.
SUBTASK 21-51-52-960-001
(8) If the resistance does not agree with the serviceable range, replace the sensor:
(a) To replace the sensor, do these tasks: Pack Temperature Sensor Removal,
TASK 21-51-52-000-801 and Pack Temperature Sensor Installation,
TASK 21-51-52-400-801.
E. Put the Airplane Back to Its Usual Condition
SUBTASK 21-51-52-420-005
(1) Install the applicable pack/zone temperature controller Pack/Zone Temperature Controller -
Installation, TASK 21-61-20-400-801 or Pack Flow Temperature Controller - Installation,
TASK 21-61-17-400-801.

position.

position.

21-61-00-740-801-002Pack Flow Temperature Controller BITE TestPDF p. 1483
3. Pack Flow Temperature Controller BITE Test
(Figure 502)
A. General
(1) This task does a BITE test on the pack flow temperature controller.
(2) The BITE test does a check on the following components:
(a) Pack Flow Temperature Controller (PFTC)
(b) Flight deck temperature sensor
(c) Zone temperature sensor
(d) Standby zone sensor
(e) Flight deck duct sensor
(f) Pack temperature sensor
(g) Standby pack temperature sensor
(h) Mix manifold temperature sensor
(i) Flight deck sensor
(j) Zone selector
(k) Standby selector
(l) Pack inlet pressure
(m) Pack flow sensor
(n) Flow control valve
(o) Temperature control valve
(p) Flight deck trim valve
(q) Zone trim valve
(r) Standby temperature control valve
(s) Flight deck sensor
(t) SRADA control
(u) SRADA inlet
(v) SRADA exit
(w) SRADA ram sensor
(3) There are two identical PFTC located on the E3-3 rack.
(4) If the PFTC shows FAULT on the front panel display, there is a fault currently being detected
by the controller. There may also be faults recorded in the FAULT HISTORY mode of the
PFTC.
(5) This BITE procedure must be done on both PFTC.
(6) The steps that follow provide a summary of the function of the buttons on the front of the
PFTC:
(a) ON/OFF button
1) The ON/OFF button will activate or de-activate the BITE functions on the PFTC.
(b) MENU button
Config 2
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
 385-999 (Continued)
1) The MENU button will display the BITE menus in the PFTC. If you push the MENU
button, you will go up to the previously displayed MENU.
2) You can select DOWN or NO at a MENU item to go to the next MENU item.
3) You can only select DOWN to go to the next item if it is not a MENU item.
(c) YES button
1) If you select YES at a MENU item, you will go to details of the item.
2) Used to respond YES to questions on the PFTC.
(d) NO button
1) You can select NO at a MENU item to go to the next item.
2) If you keep selecting NO, you will get to END OF LIST.
3) Used to respond NO to questions on the PFTC.
(e) UP button
1) Used to scroll up through the menu or the results of a BITE test.
(f) DOWN button
1) If you keep selecting DOWN, you will get to END OF LIST.
2) Used to scroll down through the menu or the results of a BITE test.
(7) The BITE has five modes of operation as listed below:
(a) Manual press ON/OFF
(b) EXISTING FAULTS
(c) FAULT HISTORY
(d) GROUND TEST
(e) OTHER FUNCTIONS
(8) The steps that follow provide a summary of the main menu selections:
(a) Manual press ON/OFF
1) Manually pressing the ON/OFF button will power the front panel displays.
(b) EXISTING FAULTS
1) The EXISTING FAULTS main menu selection provides a list of all faults that are
currently detected by the PFTC.
a) Maintenance action is required to resolve those maintenance messages that
show in the EXISTING FAULTS.
(c) FAULT HISTORY
1) The FAULT HISTORY state is activated by selecting the DOWN arrow button or NO
button when the front panel display is showing EXISTING FAULTS or scrolling
up/down from the front panel display MENU button.
2) Fault memory is read and Flight Leg Fault Records are displayed in reverse
chronological order; that is, the last fault on the last flight leg is displayed first and

F. BITE Procedure for EXISTING FAULTS
SUBTASK 21-61-00-740-003-002
(1) If the front panel display is blank, then do these steps:
(a) Push the ON/OFF button on the front panel.
(b) If EXISTING FAULTS does not show, do these steps:
1) Push UP to go to TOP OF LIST.
2) Push MENU to go up in the menu list.
SUBTASK 21-61-00-740-004-002
(2) Push the YES button on the front panel.
SUBTASK 21-61-00-740-007-002
(3) Find and record the existing faults as follows:
NOTE: The text of the fault will be the same as one of the maintenance messages listed in the
applicable BITE Message Index in the Fault Isolation Manual (FIM). These existing
faults are referred to as maintenance messages.
(a) Make a record of the existing fault (maintenance message).
(b) Make a record of each fault detail (fault number) for the maintenance message as
follows:
Config 2
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
 385-999 (Continued)
1) Push the YES button on the PFTC front panel to see the fault details (fault
numbers) for the maintenance message.
NOTE: The fault details for a maintenance message will be the same as one or
more of the fault numbers that are listed in the PFTC Fault Number List.
The number of fault details (fault numbers) varies with each maintenance
message.
2) Make a record of the fault detail (fault number) for the maintenance message.
3) Push the DOWN arrow button on the PFTC front panel to find the next fault detail
(fault number).
NOTE: When the end of the list is reached, END OF LIST will show for two
seconds and the PFTC will return to the maintenance message.
(c) Push the DOWN arrow button on the PFTC front panel to find the next maintenance
message in the EXISTING FAULTS list.
NOTE: If there are no more faults, the display will show END OF LIST for two seconds,
then the previous maintenance message will show.
SUBTASK 21-61-00-740-006-002
(4) Push the MENU button on the PFTC front panel.
SUBTASK 21-61-00-740-008-002
(5) Refer to the applicable BITE Message Index in the FIM to find the fault isolation task for the
applicable maintenance message.

SUBTASK 21-61-00-740-010-002
(1) Make a record of all the faults in each flight leg:
(a) Push the DOWN arrow button on the PFTC front panel until FAULT HISTORY shows.
(b) Push the YES button on the PFTC front panel.
1) Make sure that the PFTC front panel display shows FLIGHT LEG XX.
NOTE: XX is the last flight leg that faults were recorded in history.

leg as follows:
NOTE: FLIGHT LEGS will not be displayed if there are no faults recorded in FAULT
HISTORY.
1) Push the YES button on the PFTC front panel.
2) Find and record each fault in the flight leg fault list as follows:
NOTE: The text of the fault will be the same as one of the maintenance messages
listed in the applicable BITE Message Index in the FIM. These faults are
referred to as maintenance messages.
a) Make a record of the fault (maintenance message).
b) Make a record of each fault detail (fault number) for the maintenance message
as follows:

(fault numbers) for the maintenance message.

two seconds and the PFTC will return to the maintenance
message.
c) Push the DOWN arrow button on the PFTC front panel to find the next fault

recorded in the last (most recent) flight leg.

4. Cabin Temperature Control and Indication - Operational Test
A. General
(1) This task does an operational test of the cabin temperature control and indication components.
B. References
Reference Title
21-00-00-800-803 Supply Conditioned Air with a Cooling Pack (P/B 201)
21-00-00-800-804 Remove Conditioned Air Supplied by a Cooling Pack (P/B 201)
C. Tools/Equipment
Reference Description
STD-1122 Thermometer - Alcohol/Mercury (or equivalent meter meets task
requirements)
D. Location Zones
Zone Area
212 Flight Compartment - Right
E. Procedure
SUBTASK 21-61-00-710-013-002
(1) Do this task: Supply Conditioned Air with a Cooling Pack, TASK 21-00-00-800-803.
SUBTASK 21-61-00-860-026-002
(2) Do these steps at the P5-17 Cabin Temperature Panel:
(a) Put the CONT CAB temperature selector to the full COLD position.
(b) Put the FWD CAB and AFT CAB temperature selectors to the AUTO (12:00) position.
(c) Let the pack operate for 1 to 3 minutes to let the output temperature become stable.
SUBTASK 21-61-00-710-014-002
(3) Do these steps to check temperature indication for the forward passenger cabin:
(a) Use a thermometer, STD-1122, to measure the ambient temperature in the forward
passenger cabin near the cabin temperature sensor panel.
(b) Put the AIR TEMP selector on the P5-17 Cabin Temperature Panel to the FWD PASS
CABIN position.
(c) Make sure that the temperature shown on the indicator is approximately the same as the
ambient temperature in the forward passenger cabin.
(d) Move the FWD CAB temperature selector to the fully WARM position.
(e) Make sure that the temperature indicator shows an increase in temperature.
(f) Move the FWD CAB temperature selector to the AUTO (12:00) position.
(g) Let the pack operate for 1 to 3 minutes to let the output temperature become stable.
SUBTASK 21-61-00-710-015-002
(4) Do these steps to check temperature indication for the aft passenger cabin:
(a) Use a thermometer, STD-1122, to measure the ambient temperature in the aft passenger
cabin near the cabin temperature sensor panel.
Config 2
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(b) Put the AIR TEMP selector on the P5-17 Cabin Temperature Panel to the AFT PASS
CABIN position.
(c) Make sure that the temperature shown on the indicator is approximately the same as the
ambient temperature in the aft passenger cabin.
(d) Move the AFT CAB temperature selector to the fully WARM position.
(e) Make sure that the temperature indicator shows an increase in temperature.
(f) Move the AFT CAB temperature selector to the full COLD position.
(g) Let the pack operate for 1 to 3 minutes to let the output temperature become stable.
SUBTASK 21-61-00-710-016-002
(5) Do these steps to check temperature control for the control cabin:
(a) Put the CONT CABIN temperature selector to the AUTO (12:00) position.
(b) Let the pack operate for 1 to 3 minutes to let the output temperature become stable.
(c) Put the AIR TEMP selector on the P5-17 Cabin Temperature Panel to the SUPPLY DUCT
CONT CAB position.
(d) Make a record of the temperature shown on the indicator.
(e) Move the CONT CAB temperature selector to the fully WARM position.
(f) Make sure that the temperature indicator shows an increase in temperature.
(g) Move the CONT CAB and AFT CAB temperature selectors to the AUTO (12:00) position.

SUBTASK 21-61-04-860-051-002

F. Resistance Check Procedure
SUBTASK 21-61-04-700-007-002
(1) Use a digital thermometer, COM-3955 or equivalent, to measure the temperature adjacent to
the applicable duct temperature sensor.
(a) Write down the temperature.
SUBTASK 21-61-04-760-002-002
(2) Use a digital/analog multimeter, COM-1793 to measure resistance between the following pin
connections.
NOTE: The digital multimeter must be specifically selected to minimize self-heating of the
sensor element. The instrument must limit the current through the sensor to less than
100 microamperes. If you use resistance measuring instruments without this
current-limiting feature you will get an error in resistance value due to self-heating of
the sensor element.
Config 2
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
 006, 007, 013, 014, 018-020, 043, 044, 056-063, 067-078, 081, 083-103, 111-114, 121-129, 131,
132, 135, 138-169, 174-179, 182-187, 189-203, 205-209, 212-220, 223, 224, 231-236, 239-298, 301-304,
306, 308, 315-317, 322-341, 343, 346-384
SUBTASK 21-61-04-700-008-002
(3) For the control cabin duct temperature sensor, measure the resistance from pin A5 to pin B5
on connector D3860A for the zone temperature controller No. 2 (WDM 21-61-11).
SUBTASK 21-61-04-700-009-002
(4) For the forward cabin duct temperature sensor, measure the resistance from pin C6 to pin C7
on connector D3860A for the zone temperature controller No. 2 (WDM 21-61-13).
SUBTASK 21-61-04-700-010-002
(5) For the control cabin backup duct temperature sensor, measure the resistance between pin A5
and pin B5 on connector D3858A for the zone temperature controller No. 1 (WDM 21-61-12).
SUBTASK 21-61-04-700-011-002
(6) For the aft cabin duct temperature sensor, measure the resistance from pin C6 to pin C7 on
connector D3858A for the zone temperature controller No. 1 (WDM 21-61-14).
 385-999
SUBTASK 21-61-04-700-013-002
(7) For the control cabin duct temperature sensor, measure the resistance from pin E9 to pin E10
on connector D15816B for the right pack flow temperature controller (WDM 21-61-11).
SUBTASK 21-61-04-700-014-002
(8) For the forward cabin duct temperature sensor, measure the resistance from pin B8 to pin B9
on connector D15816B for the right pack flow temperature controller (WDM 21-61-13).
SUBTASK 21-61-04-700-015-002
(9) For the control cabin backup duct temperature sensor, measure the resistance between pin E9
and pin E10 on connector D15814B for the left pack flow temperature controller (WDM
21-61-12).
SUBTASK 21-61-04-700-016-002
(10) For the aft cabin duct temperature sensor, measure the resistance from pin B8 to pin B9 on
connector D15814B for the left pack flow temperature controller (WDM 21-61-14).
 ALL
SUBTASK 21-61-04-700-012-002
(11) Write down the resistance in Ohms that you measure.
(a) For the duct temperature sensors for the control cabin, the passenger cabin, the SC or
the MDCC, find the temperature on Figure 504 that is nearest to the temperature that you
wrote down.
(b) Compare the permitted range of resistance for that temperature to the resistance you
wrote down.
(c) If the resistance is out of range, replace the sensor. To replace the sensor,
These are the tasks:
Duct Temperature Limit Sensor Removal, TASK 21-61-04-000-803-002,
Duct Temperature Limit Sensor Installation, TASK 21-61-04-400-803-002.
Config 2
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL

E. Flight Compartment Zone - Cabin Temperature Sensor Assembly Filter Removal
SUBTASK 21-61-06-020-001
(1) Remove the filter [1] for the cabin temperature sensor assembly in the flight compartment as
follows (Figure 201):
(a) Remove the screws [2] that attach the grille [3] to the aft ceiling in the flight compartment.
(b) Remove the grille [3] and filter [1].
WARNING
DO NOT LET THE FILTER TOUCH YOUR SKIN. DO NOT SHAKE OR HIT
THE FILTER. DO NOT LET THE FILTER FALL. DO NOT USE
COMPRESSED AIR TO CLEAN THE FILTER OR FILTER HOUSING. THIS
CAN CAUSE THE INFECTIOUS MATERIAL TO BECOME AIRBORNE.
DISCARD THE FILTER IN A PLASTIC DISPOSAL BAG. OBEY THESE
INSTRUCTIONS TO PREVENT INJURIES TO PERSONNEL.
(c) If it is possible, slide plastic bag, G00624, over the filter when removing the filter [1] from
the grille [3] to minimize contamination.
(d) Seal the bag closed with tape.
WARNING
OBEY THE AIRLINE POLICY, LOCAL HEALTH DEPARTMENT, AND LAW
ENFORCEMENT REGULATIONS WHEN YOU DISCARD THIS MATERIAL.
OBEY THESE INSTRUCTIONS TO PREVENT INJURIES TO
PERSONNEL.
(e) Refer to the airline, local health, safety and regulatory procedures for the disposal of
material.

G. Cabin Temperature Sensor Assembly Grille Cleaning
SUBTASK 21-61-06-110-003
(1) Prepare a cleaning solution of water and general purpose household detergent cleaner,
B00541, or Brulin Formula 815MX cleaner, B00039.
(a) Follow the mixing instructions for the cleaner.
SUBTASK 21-61-06-110-004
(2) Clean the grille with the cleaning solution.
SUBTASK 21-61-06-100-005
(3) If the cleaning solution did not remove all dirt or contamination from the grille, clean the grille
with cotton wiper, G00034, that is moist with alcohol, B00130.
SUBTASK 21-61-06-100-006
(4) Flush the grille with clean water until all of the cleaning solution or alcohol has been removed.
SUBTASK 21-61-06-100-007
(5) Dry the grille with cotton wiper, G00034.
H. Post-Filter Removal Cleanup
SUBTASK 21-61-06-670-003
WARNING
ISOPROPYL ALCOHOL IS POISONOUS AND FLAMMABLE. USE
PROTECTION EQUIPMENT. MAKE SURE THAT YOU USE ISOPROPYL
ALCOHOL IN AN AREA WITH AIRFLOW. IF YOU DO NOT OBEY, INJURY TO
PERSONNEL CAN OCCUR.
(1) Disinfect the air grille [3] and air grilles [22] with a solution of 70% alcohol, B00130.
NOTE: Follow the manufacturer’s instruction and refer to the local health authority guidance
for required contact/dwell time.
(a) Use pre-moistened cotton wiper, G00034.
1) Make sure that the wiper is not over-saturated not to let the alcohol drips and soaks
into crevices or porous surfaces.
SUBTASK 21-61-06-670-001
(2) Disinfect all tools used for filter replacement.
NOTE: Refer to the airline procedure and policies for the disinfecting of tools.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
SUBTASK 21-61-06-020-006
WARNING
DISCARD ALL PERSONAL PROTECTIVE EQUIPMENT AFTER YOU USE IT

PLASTIC DISPOSAL BAG. OBEY THESE INSTRUCTIONS TO PREVENT
INJURIES TO PERSONNEL.
(3) Remove the personal protective equipment, put them in plastic bag, G00624, with any used
wipers and seal the bag closed with tape.
WARNING

PERSONNEL.

NOTE: Refer to the airline, local health, safety and regulatory procedures for disposal of
material.

D. Cabin Temperature Sensor Assembly Filter Cleaning
SUBTASK 21-61-06-110-001
(1) Prepare a cleaning solution of water and general purpose household detergent cleaner,
B00541, or Brulin Formula 815MX cleaner, B00039.
(a) Follow the mixing instructions for the cleaner.
SUBTASK 21-61-06-110-002
(2) Clean the air inlet grille and the filter with the cleaning solution.
NOTE: It is not necessary to clean a new filter.
SUBTASK 21-61-06-100-004
(3) If the cleaning solution did not remove all dirt deposits or contamination from the air inlet grille,
then clean the grille with a cotton wiper, G00034, that is moist with alcohol, B00130.
SUBTASK 21-61-06-100-001
(4) Flush the grille and the filter with clean water until you remove all traces of the cleaning
solution or alcohol, B00130.
SUBTASK 21-61-06-100-002
(5) Dry the grille with cotton wiper, G00034.
SUBTASK 21-61-06-100-003
(6) Dry the filter with compressed air or the cotton wiper, G00034.
E. Put the Airplane Back to Its Usual Condition
SUBTASK 21-61-06-420-001
(1) Install the filter for the temperature sensor assembly in the flight compartment
(TASK 21-61-06-400-801).
SUBTASK 21-61-06-420-002
(2) Install the filter for the temperature sensor assembly in the passenger compartment
(TASK 21-61-06-400-801).

(Figure 401)
A. Location Zones
Zone Area
212 Flight Compartment - Right
B. Prepare for the Removal
SUBTASK 21-61-07-840-005-002
(1) Open these circuit breakers and install safety tags:
F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-4
Row Col Number Name
C 5 C00263 AIR CONDITIONING PACK CONT VALVES R
C 6 C00262 AIR CONDITIONING PACK CONT VALVES L
SUBTASK 21-61-07-860-010-002
(2) Put the L PACK switch and R PACK switch, on the P5-10 air conditioning panel, to the OFF
position.
C. Cabin Temperature Selector Removal
SUBTASK 21-61-07-010-002-002
(1) Do these steps to get access to the electrical connector [1] on the back of the cabin
temperature panel [3] (P5-17).
(a) Loosen the 1/4-turn fasteners that hold the aft end of the P5 forward overhead panel in
place.
NOTE: The forward end of the P5 panel is hinged. The aft end of the P5 panel will rotate
downward when the fasteners are loose.
(b) Release the safety latch and carefully lower the P5 forward overhead panel to the open
position.
SUBTASK 21-61-07-020-007-002
(2) Do the steps that follow to remove the cabin temperature selector [2] from the cabin
temperature panel [3] (P5-17):
(a) Disconnect the electrical connector [1] from the cabin temperature selector [2].
(b) Loosen the setscrew that hold the knob [6] to the cabin temperature selector [2].
(c) Remove the knob [6] from the cabin temperature selector [2].
(d) Remove the nut [5] and washer [4] from the cabin temperature selector [2].
Config 2
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(e) Carefully pull the cabin temperature selector [2] out of the cabin temperature panel [3]
(P5-17).

D. Cabin Temperature Selector Installation
SUBTASK 21-61-07-420-005-002
(1) To install the cabin temperature selector [2] in the cabin temperature panel [3] (P5-17), do
these steps:
(a) Carefully push the cabin temperature selector [2] into its position in the cabin temperature
panel [3] (P5-17).
1) Make sure that the pin on the front of the cabin temperature selector [2] is in the slot
on the P5-17 panel.

F. Trim Air Check Valve Installation
SUBTASK 21-61-09-420-001
(1) Install the trim air check valve [5] as follows:
(a) Install the orifice plate [14] using one of the two methods below:
1) Method 1, install the orifice plate [14] un-bonded to the outlet side of the trim air
check valve [5].
2) Method 2, install orifice plate [14] bonded to the outlet side of the trim air check
valve [5].
NOTE: Bonding is optional and not required for proper operation.
a) If bonding is preferred, bond the orifice plate [14] to the trim air check valve [5]
as follows:
<1> Use wiper, G50262, moist in alcohol, B00130, to clean the mating
surfaces of the orifice plate [14] and trim air check valve [5].
<a> If it is necessary, use clean wiper, G50262, to remove remaining
solvent.
<2> Clean the mating surface of the orifice plate [14] with 150 grit abrasive
paper, G02428.
<a> Use wiper, G50262, moist in alcohol, B00130, to clean the
mating surface of the orifice plate [14].
<b> If it is necessary, use clean wiper, G50262, to remove remaining
solvent.
<3> Apply PR 1204 primer, A50126, or Dow Corning PR-1204 prime coat,
C50242, to mating surfaces of the orifice plate [14] and trim air check
valve [5].
<a> Let the primer dry for a minimum of 60 minutes at 65°F (18.3°C)
- 100°F (37.8°C).
<4> Apply Dow Corning 3145 RTV adhesive, A00281, to the mating
surfaces of the orifice plate [14] and trim air check valve [5].
<5> Attach the orifice plate [14] to the outlet flange of the trim air check
valve [5].
<a> Make sure that the orifice plate [14] is centered on the outlet
flange of trim air check valve [5].
<6> Apply the pressure to the bonding surfaces.
<a> Make sure that there is no squeeze out.
<7> Let adhesive dry under pressure for a minimum of 24 hours at 65°F
(18.3°C) - 100°F (37.8°C) and at more than 30 percent relative
humidity.
(b) Put the trim air check valve [5] in its position.
1) Make sure that the flow arrow on the trim air check valve [5] points in the forward
direction.
2) Make sure that the ports of the trim air check valve [5] point up.
(c) Move the clamps [6] to the duct connections.
(d) Tighten the nuts on the two clamps [6] to 55 in-lb (6 N·m) - 60 in-lb (7 N·m).
1) Make sure that the loop bands do not touch.

D. Trim Air Check Valve Inspection
SUBTASK 21-61-09-200-001
(1) Inspect the trim air check valve for these defects:
(a) The valve body [1] has cracks or corrosion.
(b) The valve flappers [2] do not move freely.
(c) The valve flappers [2] do not touch the valve body equally.
(d) There are carbon particles at the valve flappers [2] and body interface.
(e) The valve flappers [2] are bent.
(f) The stop pin tube [3] has cracks or deterioration.
(g) If the trim air check valve has one or more of the defects, replace the trim air check valve.
SUBTASK 21-61-09-420-002

C. Cabin Temperature Sensor Removal
SUBTASK 21-61-10-860-036
(1) Remove the cabin temperature sensor [1] in the flight compartment as follows (Figure 201 or
Figure 202):
(a) Loosen the access panel on the aft ceiling lining in the flight compartment and let it hang
on the straps.
NOTE: The access panel on the aft ceiling lining is held in position by hook and loop
strips.
(b) Disconnect the electrical connector (D10958) from the sensor [1].
(c) Remove the screws [2] and washers [3] that attach the sensor [1] to the temperature
sensor assembly.
(d) Remove the sensor [1].
 006, 007, 013, 014, 018-020, 043, 044, 056-063, 067-078, 081, 083-103, 111-114, 121-129, 131,

SUBTASK 21-61-10-860-037
(2) Remove the cabin temperature sensor [35] for passenger compartment zone as follows
(Figure 201 or Figure 202):
(a) Lower the Passenger Service Unit (PSU) at each end of the bullnose cover:
NOTE: The PSUs must be lowered to get access to the fasteners that retain the
closeouts for the bullnose cover.
1) Release the latches that hold the PSUs in position:
a) Put a blunt-ended metal rod, approximately 1/16-inch diameter, into the
access holes in the bottom of the PSU until the latch releases.
2) Lower the PSU.
(b) Remove the bullnose cover [21] to get access to the temperature sensor assembly [30]
as follows:
1) Do these steps to loosen the closeouts [27] at the ends of the bullnose cover [21]:
a) Open the stowage bin [24] door and remove the screws [22] and washers [23].
b) Remove the screws [25] through the applicable hole in the MCD/PSU rail [26].
c) Move the closeouts [27] to the adjacent bins to release them from the edges of
the bullnose cover [21].
2) Push inboard on the clips [28] to release the bullnose cover [21] from the MCD/PSU
rail [26].
NOTE: The notches in the outboard flange of the MCD/PSU rail show the locations
of the clips.
3) Turn the bullnose cover [21] inboard to remove it.
(c) Disconnect the electrical connector [36], electrical connector [37], and electrical
connector [38].
(d) Remove the access plug [31].
(e) Remove the screws [33] and washers [32].
(f) Remove the screws [29].
(g) Remove the temperature sensor assembly [30] and washers [34].

B. Preparation for Cabin Temperature Sensor Cleaning
SUBTASK 21-61-10-020-008
(1) Remove the temperature sensor for the flight compartment. To remove the temperature sensor,
do this task: Cabin Temperature Sensor Removal, TASK 21-61-10-000-802.
SUBTASK 21-61-10-020-009
(2) Remove the temperature sensor for the passenger compartment. To remove the temperature
sensor, do this task: Cabin Temperature Sensor Removal, TASK 21-61-10-000-802.
C. Cabin Temperature Sensor Cleaning
SUBTASK 21-61-10-100-002
(1) Do these steps to clean the temperature sensor:
(a) Prepare a cleaning solution of a commercially available mild liquid detergent diluted with
water in accordance with the instructions on the detergent container.
(b) Clean the sensor with a cotton wiper, G00034 that is moist with the cleaning solution.
(c) If the cotton wiper, G00034 with the cleaning solution did not remove all dirt deposits or
contamination from the sensor, clean the sensor with a cotton wiper, G00034 that is moist
with alcohol, B00130.
(d) Flush the sensor with clean water until all traces of the detergent solution or alcohol are
removed.
(e) Dry the sensor with dry, clean cotton wiper, G00034.
D. Put the Airplane Back to Its Usual Condition
SUBTASK 21-61-10-420-008
(1) Install the flight compartment temperature sensor. To install the flight compartment temperature
sensor, do this task: Cabin Temperature Sensor Installation, TASK 21-61-10-400-802.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
SUBTASK 21-61-10-420-009
(2) Install the passenger compartment temperature sensor. To install the temperature sensor, do
this task: Cabin Temperature Sensor Installation, TASK 21-61-10-400-802.

E. Flight Compartment Cabin Temperature Sensor Fan Removal
SUBTASK 21-61-11-020-001
(1) Remove the cabin temperature sensor fan [3] in the flight compartment as follows (Figure 401):
(a) Lower the access panel on the forward end of the aft ceiling panel [7] in the flight
compartment.
NOTE: The access panel is held in position with hook and loop strips. This panel will give
the access to the electrical connectors on the cabin temperature sensor
assembly.
(b) Disconnect the electrical connector [1] and electrical connector [2] (D10958 and D10956)
from the cabin temperature sensor assembly.
(c) To remove the aft ceiling panel [7] in the flight compartment, do this task: Flight
Compartment Aft Ceiling Panel Removal, TASK 25-11-21-000-806.
(d) Attach tags to each of the fan wires [4] to show its correct location for later installation.
(e) Remove the compound from the screws [5] with wiper, G50262, soaked in aliphatic
naphtha, B50079, or aliphatic naphtha, B50078, or solvent, B00316.
(f) Remove the screws [5] and washers [6].
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(g) Disconnect the fan wires [4] from the terminal board [13] on the fan [3].
1) Do not remove the ground wire from the metal flange [9].
(h) Remove the four clamps [10], washers [11], and screws [12] that attach the fan [3] to the
cabin temperature sensor assembly.
(i) Remove the fan [3] from the cabin temperature sensor assembly.

 006, 007, 013, 014, 018-020, 043, 044, 056-063, 067-078, 081, 083-103, 111-114, 121-129, 131,

(1) Remove the cabin temperature sensor fan [44] or fan [59] in the passenger compartment as

(a) Lower the PSU at each end of the bullnose cover [21]:
NOTE: The PSU must be lowered to get access to the screws that retain the closeouts
for the bullnose cover.
1) Release the latches that hold the PSU in position:
a) Put a blunt-ended metal rod, approximately 1/16-inch diameter, into the
access holes in the bottom of the PSU until the latches release.
2) Lower the PSU.
(b) Remove the bullnose cover [21] to get access to the cabin temperature sensor
assembly [36] as follows:
1) Do these steps to loosen the closeouts [27] at the ends of the bullnose cover [21]:
a) Open the stowage bin [24] door and remove the screws [22] and washers [23].
b) Remove the screws [25] through the applicable hole in the movable class
divider/passenger service unit [26].
c) Move the closeouts [27] to the adjacent bins to release them from the edges of
the bullnose cover [21].
2) Push inboard on the clips [28] to release the bullnose cover [21] from the movable
class divider/passenger service unit [26].
NOTE: The notches in the outboard flange of the Moveable Class Divider
(MCD)/PSU rail show the locations of the clips.
3) Turn the bullnose cover [21] inboard to remove it.
(c) If the fan [44] is installed, do these steps (View E, Figure 402):
1) Disconnect the electrical connector [29], electrical connector [31], and electrical
connector [32].
2) Remove the access plug [33].
3) Remove the screws [34] and washers [35].
4) Remove the screws [30].
5) Remove the temperature sensor assembly [36] and washers [37].
6) Attach a tag to each fan wire [45] to show its correct location for later installation.
7) Remove the compound from the screws [42] with wiper, G50262, soaked in aliphatic
naphtha, B50079, or aliphatic naphtha, B50078, or solvent, B00316.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL

8) Remove the screws [42] and washers [43].
9) Disconnect the fan wires [45] from the terminal board [46] on the fan [44].
a) Do not remove the bonding jumper [47] from the flange [40].
10) Remove the screws [38], washers [39], and clamps [41] which attach the fan [44] to

11) Remove the fan [44] from the assembly:

SUBTASK 21-61-11-420-001
(1) Install the cabin temperature sensor fan [3] in the flight compartment as follows (Figure 401):
(a) Put the fan [3] in its position with the other components of the temperature sensor
assembly.
(b) Install the clamps [10], washers [11], and screws [12] to attach the fan [3] to the cabin
temperature sensor assembly.
NOTE: The orientation of the screws on the temperature sensor fan can vary. Either
direction of the fastener is acceptable.
(c) Install the fan wires [4] on the fan terminal board [13] with the screws [5] and washers [6].
NOTE: Use the tags on the fan wires to put the fan wires in the correct locations.
1) Clean the mating surfaces on the terminal board [13] with wiper, G50262, soaked in
aliphatic naphtha, B50079, or aliphatic naphtha, B50078, or solvent, B00316.
2) Wipe dry with wiper, G50262, before solvent evaporates.
a) If it is necessary repeat steps to completely remove contaminants.
b) Coat 0.05 ±0.03 in. (1.3 ±0.8 mm) thick of compound, A50589, on the fan
wires [4].
NOTE: Coatings that are thinner than 0.04 in. (1.0 mm) are difficult to remove
in-service and should be avoided.
(d) To install the aft ceiling panel [7] in the flight compartment, do this task: Flight
Compartment Aft Ceiling Panel Installation, TASK 25-11-21-400-806.
(e) Connect the electrical connector [1] and electrical connector [2] (D10958 and D10956) to
the temperature sensor and the fan [3].
(f) To install the access panel, lift it to its position and push firmly to make sure the hook and
loop strips are fully engaged.

SUBTASK 21-61-12-630-002
(1) Remove the covers from the duct openings and make sure that there is no unwanted materials
inside the duct.
SUBTASK 21-61-12-420-006
(2) If you removed the trim air duct [3] that penetrates through the pressure bulkhead, do these
steps to reinstall it (Figure 401):
(a) Open this access panel:
Number Name/Location
821 Forward Cargo Door
(b) Remove the aft bulkhead liner in the forward cargo compartment
(TASK 25-52-17-000-801).
(c) Slide the trim air duct [3] through the pressure bulkhead hole.
(d) Support the trim air duct [3].
(e) Loosely install the aft coupling [11] in the mix manifold bay to connect trim air duct [3] to
trim air duct [12].
SUBTASK 21-61-12-100-002
(3) Use a clean wiper and solvent, B00083, to clean the pressure seal support [3A] area on the
trim air duct [3] that penetrates through the pressure bulkhead (Figure 401).
SUBTASK 21-61-12-420-008
(4) Slide the pressure seal [5] onto the trim air duct [3].
SUBTASK 21-61-12-420-009
(5) For installation of the pressure seal [5], do the following steps (Figure 401):
(a) Push the pressure seal [5] to the mating surface of the pressure bulkhead.
(b) Apply antiseize compound, D00010, to the threads of the bolt [7].
(c) Install the two seal ring havles [6] on the pressure seal [5] with the twelve bolts [7] and
washers [8].
NOTE: The two bolts at 11 and 12 o'clock positions attach the duct overheat sensor to
the pressure bulkhead and are longer than the other bolts. The duct overheat
sensor support bracket must be installed on top of the seal ring half [6].
(d) Tighten the bolts [7] to 32.5 ±2.5 in-lb (3.67 ±0.28 N·m) in the sequence shown in
Figure 401.
(e) Install the clamp [9] loosely to the pressure seal [5].
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(f) Do these steps to tighten the clamp [9]:
1) Turn the torque wrench to tighten the clamp [9] and observe the torque needed to
turn the nut on the clamp T-bolt before the clamp becomes tight.
NOTE: The observed torque should be 8.5 ±6.5 in-lb (0.96 ±0.73 N·m). This torque
is referred to as run-on torque.
2) Add the observed run-on torque to 20 ±2 in-lb (2.26 ±0.23 N·m). For example, if the
run-on torque needed to turn the T-bolt nut was 10 in-lb (1 N·m), then the torque
needed to tighten the clamp is 30 ±2 in-lb (3.39 ±0.23 N·m). This is the calculated
torque needed to tighten the clamp.
3) Tighten the clamp [9] to the torque calculated in the previous step.
4) Wait a minimum of 2 hours, then retighten the clamp [9] to the torque calculated in
the previous step.
SUBTASK 21-61-12-420-013
(6) For the flight deck zone trim air pressure seal (in left ECS bay), install the flight deck zone trim
air modulating valve [1] (TASK 21-61-21-400-801).
(a) Align the flight deck zone trim air ducts [3] and trim air duct [12].
(b) Tighten the coupling [11] to 57.5 ±2.5 in-lb (6.5 ±0.3 N·m).
1) Make sure that the loop bands do not touch.
2) Make sure that the clearance between the retainers is 0.050 in. (1.270 mm) -
0.310 in. (7.874 mm).
SUBTASK 21-61-12-420-016
(7) For the aft zone trim air pressure seal (in right ECS bay), install the aft zone trim air modulating

D. Prepare for the Flight Compartment Temperature Sensor Assembly Housing Cleaning
SUBTASK 21-61-14-020-024
(1) Remove the cabin temperature assembly housing for the flight compartment. To remove the
housing, do this task: Flight Compartment Temperature Sensor Assembly Housing Removal,
TASK 21-61-14-000-802.
E. Procedure
SUBTASK 21-61-14-160-001
(1) Prepare a weak solution of general purpose household detergent cleaner, B00541 mixed with
warm water, G50256.
(a) Obey the instructions on the detergent container.
SUBTASK 21-61-14-160-002
(2) Clean the inner and external surfaces of the housing with a cotton wiper, G00034 that is moist
with the cleaning solution.
SUBTASK 21-61-14-160-003
(3) If the cotton wiper, G00034 with the cleaning solution did not remove all dirt deposits or
contamination, clean the housing with a cotton wiper, G00034 that is moist with alcohol,
B00130.
SUBTASK 21-61-14-160-004
(4) Wipe the housing with a cotton wiper, G00034 that is moist with clean water until all of the
detergent solution or alcohol are removed.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
SUBTASK 21-61-14-160-005
(5) Dry the housing with a dry, clean cotton wiper, G00034.

(a) Examine the temperature sensor [14] for unwanted material.

D. Procedure
SUBTASK 21-61-14-160-006
(1) Prepare a weak solution of general purpose household detergent cleaner, B00541 mixed with
warm water, G50256.
(a) Obey the instructions on the detergent container.
SUBTASK 21-61-14-160-007
(2) Clean the inner and external surfaces of the duct with a cotton wiper, G00034 that is moist with
the cleaning solution.
SUBTASK 21-61-14-160-008
(3) If the cotton wiper, G00034 with the cleaning solution did not remove all dirt deposits or
contamination, clean the duct with a cotton wiper, G00034 that is moist with alcohol, B00130.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
SUBTASK 21-61-14-160-009
(4) Wipe the duct with a cotton wiper, G00034 that is moist with clean water until all of the
detergent solution or alcohol are removed.
SUBTASK 21-61-14-160-010
(5) Dry the duct with a dry, clean cotton wiper, G00034.

SUBTASK 21-61-14-210-002

valve [1] and access door structure, tubes, and clamps [7].

SUBTASK 21-62-00-860-001
(1) Do this task: Supply Pressure to the Pneumatic System with the APU, TASK 36-00-00-860-803
or Supply Pressure to the Pneumatic System with an External Ground Air Source,
TASK 36-00-00-860-802.
SUBTASK 21-62-00-860-002
(2) Make sure that these circuit breakers are closed:
F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-4
Row Col Number Name
C 5 C00263 AIR CONDITIONING PACK CONT VALVES R
C 6 C00262 AIR CONDITIONING PACK CONT VALVES L
D 9 C01172 AIR CONDITIONING TRIM AIR PRESS
SUBTASK 21-62-00-860-003
(3) Do these steps, on the P5-10 air conditioning panel:
(a) Set the L RECIRC switch to the AUTO position.
(b) Set the R RECIRC switch to the AUTO position.
(c) Set the L PACK switch to the AUTO position.
(d) Set the R PACK switch to the OFF position.
(e) Set the BLEED APU switch to the ON position.
(f) Set the BLEED 1 switch to the OFF position.
(g) Set the BLEED 2 switch to the OFF position.
(h) Set the ISOLATION VALVE switch to the OPEN position.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
SUBTASK 21-62-00-860-004
(4) Do these steps, on the P5-17 cabin temperature panel:
(a) Set the TRIM AIR switch to the OFF position.
(b) Set the AIR TEMP selector to the L PACK position.
(c) Set the CONT CAB selector to the full WARM position.
(d) Set the FWD CAB selector to the full WARM position.
(e) Set the AFT CAB selector to the full WARM position.
SUBTASK 21-62-00-860-005
(5) Operate the pack for 3 to 5 minutes to let the output temperature become stable.
SUBTASK 21-62-00-970-001
(6) Make a record of the temperature shown on the AIR TEMP gage, on the P5-17 panel, for the L
PACK.
SUBTASK 21-62-00-860-006
(7) Do these steps, on the P5-17 cabin temperature panel:
(a) Set the CONT CAB selector to the full COLD position.
(b) Set the FWD CAB selector to the full COLD position.
(c) Set the AFT CAB selector to the full COLD position.
SUBTASK 21-62-00-970-002
(8) Make sure that the temperature shown on the AIR TEMP gage, on the P5-17 panel, for the L
PACK decreases.
SUBTASK 21-62-00-860-007
(9) Set the TRIM AIR switch to the ON position.
SUBTASK 21-62-00-860-008
(10) Operate the pack for 3 to 5 minutes to let the output temperature become stable.
SUBTASK 21-62-00-970-003
(11) Make a record of the temperature shown on the AIR TEMP gage for the L PACK.
SUBTASK 21-62-00-860-009
(12) Set the AIR TEMP selector to the FWD SUPPLY DUCT position.
SUBTASK 21-62-00-970-004
(13) Make a record of the temperature shown on the AIR TEMP gage for the FWD SUPPLY DUCT.
SUBTASK 21-62-00-860-010
(14) Move the FWD CAB temperature selector to the full WARM position.
SUBTASK 21-62-00-970-005
(15) Make sure that the temperature shown on the AIR TEMP gage for the FWD SUPPLY DUCT
increases.
SUBTASK 21-62-00-860-011
(16) Move the AIR TEMP selector to the L PACK position.
SUBTASK 21-62-00-970-006
(17) Make sure that the L PACK temperature stays approximately the same.

 ALL

SUBTASK 21-62-01-020-004
(5) Do these steps to remove the hose assembly:
(a) Loosen the B-nut to disconnect the hose assembly from the trim air pressure regulating
and shutoff valve [1].
(b) Remove the union [6] from the trim air pressure regulating and shutoff valve [1].
(c) Remove and discard the packing [7].
SUBTASK 21-62-01-020-005
WARNING
DO NOT TOUCH THE COOLING PACK DUCTS WHEN THEY ARE HOT. THE
DUCTS CAN BE HOT AND CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONS.
(6) To remove the shutoff valve, do these steps:
(a) Loosen the two clamps [2].
(b) Move the clamps [2] to the adjacent ducts.
(c) Remove the trim air pressure regulating and shutoff valve [1] from the Environmental
Control System (ECS) bay.

G. Trim Air Pressure Regulating and Shutoff Valve Installation
SUBTASK 21-62-01-420-001
(1) To install the trim air pressure regulating and shutoff valve [1], do these steps:
(a) Put the trim air pressure regulating and shutoff valve [1] in its position between the ducts.
1) Make sure that the flow arrow on the trim air pressure regulating and shutoff
valve [1] points in the forward direction.
(b) Rotate the trim air pressure regulating and shutoff valve [1] to make sure that there is a
minimum distance of 0.75 in. (1.90 cm) between the trim air pressure regulating and
shutoff valve [1] and bottom of the keel beam.
1) Make sure that there is a minimum clearance of 0.15 in. (0.38 cm) between the
structure, tubes, and clamps [2].
(c) Loosely install the clamps [2].
SUBTASK 21-62-01-420-002
(2) To install the sense line on the trim air pressure regulating and shutoff valve [1], do these
steps:
(a) Install a new packing [7] on the union [6].
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(b) Apply a thin layer of Pure Nickel Special compound, D00006, to the threads of the
union [6].
(c) Install the union [6] on the trim air pressure regulating and shutoff valve [1].
(d) Install the sense line on the union [6]:
1) Make sure that you install the same end of the sense line to the trim air pressure
regulating and shutoff valve [1] as you noted at the removal.
NOTE: Some sense lines have different end fittings.
SUBTASK 21-62-01-020-006
(3) Do these steps to install the hose assembly:
(a) Install a new packing [7] on the union [6].
(b) Apply a thin layer of Pure Nickel Special compound, D00006, to the threads of the
union [6].
(c) Install the union [6] on the trim air pressure regulating and shutoff valve [1].
(d) Install the sense line on the trim air pressure regulating and shutoff valve [1].
 006, 007, 013, 014, 018-020, 043, 044

pressure regulating and shutoff valve [1].
(c) Measure the electrical bonding resistance between the trim air pressure regulating and

1) Use an intrinsically safe approved bonding meter, COM-1550.

less.

H. Trim Air Pressure Regulating and Shutoff Valve Operational Check
SUBTASK 21-62-01-860-005
(1) Remove the safety tag and close this circuit breaker:
F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-4
Row Col Number Name
D 9 C01172 AIR CONDITIONING TRIM AIR PRESS
SUBTASK 21-62-01-860-006
(2) Do this task: Supply Pressure to the Pneumatic System (Selection), TASK 36-00-00-860-801.
SUBTASK 21-62-01-860-007
(3) Do these steps, on the P5-10 air conditioning panel:
(a) Set the L and R PACK switches to the AUTO position and remove the
DO-NOT-OPERATE tags.
(b) Set the BLEED 1 and 2 switches to the ON position and remove the DO-NOT-OPERATE
tags.
(c) Set the BLEED APU switch to the ON position and remove the DO-NOT-OPERATE tag.
SUBTASK 21-62-01-860-008
(4) Do these steps, on the P5-17 Cabin Temperature Panel:
(a) Set the TRIM AIR switch to the ON position and remove the DO-NOT-OPERATE tag.
(b) Set the CONT CAB selector to the fully WARM position and remove the
DO-NOT-OPERATE tag.
(c) Set the FWD CAB selector to the fully COLD position and remove the
DO-NOT-OPERATE tag.
(d) Set the AFT CAB selector to the fully COLD position and remove the DO-NOT-OPERATE
tag.
SUBTASK 21-62-01-860-009
(5) Operate the pack for a minute to let the output temperature become stable.
SUBTASK 21-62-01-860-010
(6) Do these steps, on the P5-17 Cabin Temperature Panel:
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(a) Set AIR TEMP selector to the each of the three SUPPLY DUCT positions (AFT, FWD and
CONT CAB)
(b) Record the temperature shown on the indicator for each of the three SUPPLY DUCT
positions.
(c) Make sure that the supply duct temperature for the CONT CAB is higher than the supply
duct temperatures for the FWD and AFT.
I. Trim Air Pressure Regulating and Shutoff Valve Leakage Check
SUBTASK 21-62-01-790-001
(1) Do a soap bubble test of the duct joints at the trim air pressure regulating and shutoff valve [1].
NOTE: No air leakage is permitted.
(a) If there is leakage, do these steps:
1) Put the L PACK and R PACK switches to the OFF position.
WARNING
DO NOT TOUCH THE COOLING PACK DUCTS WHEN THEY ARE
HOT. THE COOLING PACK DUCTS CAN BE HOT AND CAN CAUSE
INJURY TO PERSONS.
2) Loosen the clamps.
3) Make sure that the ducts are aligned at the joints.
4) Tighten the clamps.
a) Make sure that the loop bands do not touch.
 006, 007, 013, 014, 018-020, 043, 044
b) Make sure that the clearance between the retainers is 0.050 in. (1.270 mm) -
0.310 in. (7.874 mm).
 056-063, 067-078, 081, 083-103, 111-114, 121-129, 131, 132, 135, 138-169, 174-179, 182-187,
189-203, 205-209, 212-220, 223, 224, 231-236, 239-298, 301-304, 306, 308, 315-317, 322-341, 343,
346-999
c) Make sure that the clearance between the retainers is 0.050 in. (1.270 mm) -
0.410 in. (10.414 mm).

5) Put the L PACK and R PACK switches to the AUTO position.
6) Make sure that the leak has been repaired.
